Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Identify needs
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Senior Economic Analyst (JFL) is currently expected to assess client requirements for statistical information, recommend the conduct of feasibility studies or launching of projects, select and evaluate research standards and techniques, and develop new data sources when necessary (e.g., 'Assesses client requirements for statistical information; recommends the conduct of feasibility studies or launching of projects; defines project objectives and scope; selects and evaluates research standards and techniques to be used in the conduct of studies'). Future GSBPM expectation: The future state shifts the 'Identify needs' subprocess to require a proactive scan of existing and alternative data sources, cost-benefit and risk analysis, and explicit prioritization of automated and reusable solutions before new survey work, as well as digitally enabled stakeholder engagement. Role evolution: The Senior Economic Analyst's responsibility evolves from relying primarily on subject-matter tradition and demand-driven needs identification, to a formalized, enterprise-wide assessment that begins with business intelligence tools, evaluation of data assets, and digital cost-benefit analysis. The analyst must produce documented justification when new collection efforts are pursued, and must collaborate with operational, IT, and automation specialists to ensure feasibility and compatibility. Capability implication: The position will increasingly require knowledge of metadata-assisted discovery, business intelligence/reporting tools, digital stakeholder engagement, and integration of risk, resource and automation factors at the pre-assessment stage, as these are now central criteria for statistical need validation and program initiation.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Consult and Confirm Needs
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The 'Senior Economic Analyst (JFL)' is expected to provide expert advisory and consultative services to data users, source data providers and other professionals on statistical and analytical outputs. The role explicitly includes 'assess[ing] the impact on divisional programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations,' and 'assesses client requirements for statistical information; recommends feasibility studies or launching of projects.' The analyst is also expected to 'develop and procure new data sources,' integrate multiple data sources, and provide advice on whether needs can be met with existing or new data. Future GSBPM expectation: The consultation and confirmation of needs will shift to leverage existing administrative and alternative data sources, using real-time data discovery platforms and machine-actionable metadata to jointly assess needs with stakeholders. The process will emphasize rapid, iterative engagement focused on maximizing reuse and minimizing new collections. Role evolution: The role will need to evolve from initiating custom surveys and lengthy needs consultations to supporting stakeholder-focused, data-discovery interactions. Analysts must facilitate transparent trade-off decisions and cost-benefit analyses, working collaboratively with stakeholders using automated platforms and metadata-driven tools, and making explicit recommendations on feasibility and reuse. Capability implication: The shift increases the importance of knowledge in data asset discovery, platform navigation, real-time collaborative analytics, assessing fit-for-use of existing data, cost-benefit argumentation, and the ability to integrate stakeholder needs quickly into outcome-focused decision environments.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Check data availability and suitability
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Senior Economic Analyst (JFL)' is presently responsible for evaluating multiple data sources to determine their fitness for use in statistical program data, integrating diverse information, developing and procuring new data sources, and providing expert recommendations for survey or study launches. 'Analyses and assesses multiple data sources using various methods and techniques to determine their fitness for use and best utilization in the production of statistical program data.' The analyst often investigates client requirements, recommends feasibility studies, and defines project objectives especially regarding new or revised data needs. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future, the process of checking data availability and suitability becomes highly automated, leveraging AI and metadata platforms to rapidly scan internal and external data assets. Human involvement is reserved for oversight, risk assessment, legal vetting, and partnership negotiation. The bar for launching new surveys rises, requiring clear, evidence-based justification that no suitable existing data source is available. Role evolution: The analyst's responsibility is refocused: manual canvassing and empirical suitability research is replaced by oversight of automated processes, strategic assessment of novel/complex cases, legal/ethical vetting, and negotiation. The analyst must become an expert in interpreting automated source assessment reports, managing relationships with new data holders, and making decisions about edge-case suitability, risk, and rights. Capability implication: It becomes increasingly important that the analyst deeply understands metadata standards, automated suitability scoring logic, risk and legal frameworks for data acquisition, and is skilled in partnership development and complex stakeholder negotiation. Subject-matter expertise will be leveraged to understand limitations of algorithmic recommendations and to intervene in complex or unprecedented data assessments.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Design frame and sample
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: The EC-06 Senior Economic Analyst is currently responsible for analyzing multiple data sources, evaluating their fitness for use in statistical programs, and developing new methods and models for producing and analyzing statistical information (e.g., 'Analyses and assesses multiple data sources using various methods and techniques to determine their fitness for use and best utilization in the production of statistical program data'). The future GSBPM state mandates a shift from manual survey design to highly automated, AI-powered pipelines that prioritize alternative and administrative data. This transition means the role will shift from operational execution to oversight of automated frame/sample selection, interpreting automated outcomes, resolving ambiguous or edge cases, and ensuring quality control. As a result, EC-06 Senior Economic Analysts will need to evolve towards providing expert oversight of AI-driven sample design, critically reviewing the automated logic and outputs, and supporting modular, metadata-driven frameworks. The capability implication is that strong expertise in integrating administrative and alternative data, understanding metadata standards, and overseeing/validating AI-driven decisions will be essential, as will a heightened ability to interpret outputs from automated systems and manage exceptions rather than executing routine manual sampling.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Design processing and analysis
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The 'Senior Economic Analyst (JFL)' EC-06 is responsible for planning and conducting analysis of economic and financial data, developing innovative methods and models, and performing detailed analysis and evaluation of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data. They further advise on the development of standards, classifications, and compilation methods, and conduct updates to program content and coverage with new concepts, definitions, methods, and models (e.g., “devises new concepts, definitions, methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend statistical information relating to the different subject matter domains”). Future GSBPM expectation: The future state of the 'Design processing and analysis' sub-process requires the wholesale transition to modular, metadata-driven, AI-enabled processing pipelines and analytical routines, including automation logic and validation rules designed for reproducibility, interoperability, and reuse. Analyst input is de-emphasized in favour of designing system logic and rules for automation, with design work prioritizing machine-actionable specifications. Role evolution: The Senior Economic Analyst's responsibilities will need to shift from developing bespoke analytical approaches and documentation for individual programs, toward producing standardized, auditable, cross-program design specifications that are system-ready for automation, ensuring new concepts and methods are embedded as reusable, machine-actionable modules. The EC-06 will need to work collaboratively with IT and automation specialists to translate subject-matter requirements into platform-based, metadata-driven designs, significantly reducing manual intervention and increasing the integration of new data sources with minimal rework. Capability implication: Much greater importance will be placed on deep understanding of metadata management, automation logic, modular workflow design, and the ability to embed validation, editing, and disclosure rules in machine-actionable formats. Knowledge of systems architecture, AI/ML decision logic, and principles of modular and reproducible design will be critical for specification and operationalization.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Senior Economic Analyst (JFL)' plans and conducts analyses using multiple data sources, develops new data sources and compilation methods, manages project teams, and advises on standards and compilation methods. The role includes developing or modifying program content, methods, and models for statistical production and participating in international work groups on frameworks and classifications. Evidence: 'Develops and procures in conformity to guidelines and policies new data sources, performs updates and modifications to program content and coverage to align to international frameworks or classifications and devises new concepts, definitions, methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend statistical information...' Future GSBPM expectation: The Senior Analyst must transition from contributing to bespoke instrument creation and manual testing to designing data collection strategies that exploit automation, AI-driven design, and modular reuse, favoring extraction from existing sources over survey creation. Role evolution: The role must evolve from consulting on manual survey instruments to configuring standard, metadata-rich components in enterprise platforms, validating AI-driven instruments, and ensuring compliance, reuse and interoperability for future analytical outputs. Capability implication: Increased importance in digital platform management, AI-enabled instrument configuration, enterprise metadata stewardship, and understanding of automation protocols and platform-based governance.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Test production systems
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: The Senior Economic Analyst (EC-06) currently performs detailed analysis, evaluation, and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve data, determine changes, and develop strategies—often using programming languages for data analysis ("Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on divisional programs and developing options and strategies"; "Recent and significant experience using programming languages and tools such as Python, R, SAS, SPSS or SQL for data analysis"). Testing practices in the past may have centered on manually reviewing analytic outputs or validating code correctness. The GSBPM future state shifts testing into automated, repeatable, enterprise-wide disciplines—including audit, security, FAIR compliance, and attestation-based approvals. The Senior Economic Analyst will need to adapt analytical methods and programming efforts to ensure integration with automated test suites, participate in the attestation and documentation required for system-level sign-off, and help extend model validation protocols to include regulatory and ethical compliance implications for AI-enabled analysis pipelines. This requires evolving traditional review responsibilities to operationalize new testing paradigms and being responsible for supporting business-led innovation within secure guardrails. Deep knowledge of enterprise testing infrastructure, reproducibility and regulatory validation, and integrated test documentation will be central.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Create frame and select sample
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: The EC-06 Senior Economic Analyst position includes duties such as planning and conducting analysis, evaluating analytical material, performing detailed reviews of statistical methods, and determining changes in statistical program needs (“Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes...”). Importantly, the role develops new concepts, definitions, methods, and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, and extend statistical information, particularly as related to integrating new data sources and making updates aligned with frameworks or classifications. In the GSBPM 4.1 future state, this role will need to contribute to the continuous improvement and evaluation of automated frame and sample creation methods, including assessing quality assurance logic and exception handling workflows. The Analyst’s input will shift towards innovating and evaluating the integration of rich administrative and alternative data into automated sampling modules, monitoring systematic outcomes, and supporting methodological advances in AI-driven sample generation and burden management. This increases the importance of capabilities related to evaluating advanced automation approaches, interpreting algorithmic sample outputs, ensuring auditability and traceability, and developing methods for auxiliary information fusion.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Derive new variables and units
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The Senior Economic Analyst (EC-06 JFL) plans and conducts analysis of economic and financial statistical data, develops innovative methods and models, and evaluates analytical material for publication. They perform detailed analysis and review of statistical methods, improve existing data, modify program content, and devise new concepts, definitions, and models to produce and analyze information. Recent and significant experience with coding and programming for data analysis is required. This indicates involvement with both the design and execution of variable derivation, including using statistical programming tools for manual and semi-manual processing. Future GSBPM expectation: Derivation activities will be embedded in automated, version-controlled microservices overseen by IT-governed platforms. Analysts will no longer routinely perform manual coding or custom derivations but will focus on authoring and validating transformation logic and overseeing compliance, exception handling, and quality assurance within modular pipelines. Role evolution: The analyst's role will pivot from hands-on coding and custom logic creation toward stewardship over transformation logic, metadata standards, and quality governance of automated derivation processes. The analyst will also be responsible for validating new or revised derivation logic, managing exceptions, and ensuring standardized logic is auditable, reusable, and deployed centrally across statistical domains. Capability implication: Advanced capability in formalizing transformation logic into metadata-driven modules, understanding pipeline orchestration, and managing compliance and quality in automated environments becomes paramount. Analysts must be adept at modular logic design, exception analysis, and ensuring auditability, with increased focus on pipeline impact analysis and cross-functional collaboration.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Calculate weights
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: The Senior Economic Analyst (EC-06) currently is responsible for 'performing detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data,' and 'develops strategies, innovative methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyse and expand analytical outputs', which includes activities like evaluating and designing weighting methodologies, often using custom scripting and data manipulation (evidenced by 'recent and significant experience using programming languages and tools such as Python, R, SAS, SPSS or SQL for data analysis'). The future GSBPM expectation is a shift from bespoke, manual weighting routines by analysts to fully automated, standardized, reproducible modules embedded in data pipelines, governed by pre-approved logic and orchestration frameworks. Analysts will focus on methodological oversight, reviewing and maintaining system performance, adapting approaches as needed, and acting through governance. Thus, the role will evolve from direct operational execution to system-level methodological design, oversight, exception handling, and interpretation of automated outputs. The capability implication is a heightened need for knowledge of modular system architectures, data pipeline orchestration frameworks, AI-assisted adjustment logic, metadata standards for weights, and the audit trail of automated processes, as opposed to manual scripting and case-by-case application. Broadly, expertise will focus more on designing weight logic that is robust for automation, ensuring cross-domain consistency, and governing pipeline calibration, rather than hands-on calculation.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Calculate aggregates
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The Senior Economic Analyst plans and conducts analysis of economic and financial statistical data, develops strategies and innovative methods, and models to produce, evaluate, analyse and expand analytical outputs, including evaluating analytical material for publication ("Plans and conducts analysis of economic and financial statistical data and develops strategies, innovative methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyse and expand analytical outputs"). There is evidence of hands-on involvement with statistical methods and custom computation for aggregates as part of analytical workflows. Future GSBPM expectation: Automation, AI-enabled aggregation modules, metadata-driven pipelines, and microservices mean manual data aggregation and custom scripting give way to configuration, validation, and interpretation tasks. The analyst's focus will shift from developing aggregation logic to supervising automated pipelines, managing exceptions, validating AI-driven outputs, and contributing to governance of reusable modules. Role evolution: The role evolves from direct implementation of aggregation methods to oversight, exception management, configuration of modular components, and ensuring compliance with standards for reproducibility and transparency. Analysts must understand the orchestration logic and intervene primarily in edge-case handling, validation and interpretive reporting, rather than hands-on coding. Capability implication: Critical knowledge will now center on modular pipeline architectures, metadata-driven process documentation, automated quality assurance, system auditability, and interpreting AI-driven results, rather than custom script development. Familiarity with enterprise-level orchestration, microservices, and version-controlled process management becomes central to continued effectiveness.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Prepare draft outputs
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Senior Economic Analyst (JFL) is responsible for 'preparing, editing and evaluating analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada' and 'providing expert analysis and advice to senior managers', including line and matrix supervision of teams responsible for research projects or statistical outputs. These activities involve hands-on engagement in assembling, formatting, and outputting statistical tables, aggregates, and explanatory material. Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 envisions that 'draft statistical outputs, including tables, charts, dashboards, and recurring write-ups, will be auto-generated by standardized, auditable analytical pipelines leveraging AI and automation', with analysts focusing more on interpretation and oversight, and less on manual technical preparation. Role evolution: The EC-06 role would shift from manual construction and curation of outputs to oversight and quality assurance of AI-driven pipelines, with greater emphasis on exception handling, reviewing automated outputs, and interpreting results for high-value contextualization. Capability implication: This change elevates the importance of understanding orchestration processes, automated analytical pipelines, and AI-driven production environments, as well as advanced skills in output validation, quality control, and nuanced contextual interpretation of standardized outputs.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Validate outputs
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The Senior Economic Analyst is tasked with performing detailed analysis, evaluation, and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and to evaluate analytical material for publication purposes, which includes substantive involvement in data validation ('Extensive and relevant subject matter experience analyzing data for data validation, data integration or analytical publications'). Key activities emphasize 'evaluates analytical material for publication purposes' and 'Plans and conducts analysis of economic and financial statistical data ... to produce, evaluate, analyse and expand analytical outputs.' Validation typically requires in-depth subject matter expertise and manual evaluation of outputs. Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 drives validation toward automated, AI-supported pipelines, where validation shifts from manual checking to oversight and interpretation of exceptions. Human experts are expected to focus on oversight of automated validation, interpretation of anomalies, and assurance of ethical validation logic. Role evolution: The analyst will need to transition from primarily executing manual data validation checks to overseeing automated processes, interpreting flagged outputs, and investigating complex cases where automation cannot resolve ambiguity. This oversight includes ensuring the transparency and auditable nature of validation pipelines. Capability implication: Advanced understanding of validation logic, metadata-driven quality frameworks, and AI validation tools becomes central. Additionally, critical interpretation of outputs flagged by automation and rigorous assurance of ethical and transparent validation processes will be more important in their work, as they move from routine manual checks to governance and oversight functions.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Interpret and explain outputs
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Senior Economic Analyst is responsible for planning and conducting detailed analysis of economic and financial statistical data, developing methods and models, as well as providing expert advisory and consultative services to data users, senior managers, and external stakeholders. The role includes evaluating analytical material for publication and interpreting complex data to provide decision makers with relevant statistics ("Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation for data users"). Future GSBPM expectation: With the automation of routine analytic preparation and standardized analysis, the future expectation is for analysts to focus on deep subject-matter interpretation, contextualization, and explaining AI-generated outputs in policy and societal terms. Manual technical preparation is reduced, and emphasis is placed on oversight and ethical narrative. Role evolution: This role must evolve to prioritizing high-level interpretation, contextualizing outputs in policy/societal frameworks, and communicating limitations/risks associated with automated analysis. Activities will shift from technical file handling to narrative building and transparent, ethical stewardship of analysis. Capability implication: Analysts must now possess advanced understanding of transparency, AI oversight, and the ethical interpretation of automated outputs, as well as deeper domain expertise to identify the contextual significance and risks of findings.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Apply disclosure control
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The Senior Economic Analyst (EC-06) is responsible for planning and conducting detailed analysis, reviewing statistical methods, evaluating analytical outputs, and providing expert advice on the security and confidentiality of information, as indicated by responsibilities such as 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts ... to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release data or information in a form that would violate the provisions of the acts.' Future GSBPM expectation: Disclosure control will become highly automated, standardized, and embedded within analytical pipelines, with human involvement primarily focused on oversight, validation, and exception handling. Role evolution: The analyst's role will shift from hands-on, manual disclosure review and negotiation to designing, monitoring, and auditing automated disclosure control components within analytical workflows. This will require analysts to collaborate more closely with system designers and engineers to ensure disclosure controls are robust and adaptable to new dissemination formats. Capability implication: The analyst will need deeper understanding of automated workflow validation, auditability, and the ethical dimensions of AI-driven confidentiality management, including the ability to interpret or troubleshoot automated disclosure suppressions, monitor outputs for compliance, and handle exceptions.

Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).title: Conduct evaluation
Senior Economic Analyst (JFL).justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Senior Economic Analyst (JFL)' is currently responsible for planning and conducting complex statistical analyses, providing evaluation and recommendations to improve data and methods, and generating analytical material for publication, including the review and evaluation of methods and serving as a consultative expert for changes in statistical programming. Evaluation is often based on post-hoc analyses, feasibility reviews, and narrative recommendations, with a focus on human-led synthesis of issues and options, and delivery of advice to senior management. Future GSBPM expectation: With the pivot to automated, ongoing evaluation, many of the analyst's traditional processes—collecting, reviewing, and narratively reporting on program performance—must shift toward interpreting, prioritizing, and acting on system-driven insights provided constantly via dashboards and embedded metrics. Human interventions increasingly follow from standardized performance signals, and recommendations are now implemented iteratively and tracked modularly instead of through periodic overhaul. Role evolution: This analyst must become adept in deriving insight from dashboards and automated reports (benchmarking, exception logs, etc.), rapidly prioritizing which signals require action, and integrating into agile, process-improvement cycles. The role's authority becomes less about evidence assembly, more about decision logic in face of a constant flow of system indicators, and more about championing change via concrete, tracked interventions within modular workflows. Capability implication: The main shift is toward advanced literacy with evaluation dashboards, understanding metric design and event-driven performance evidence, as well as multi-disciplinary collaboration to enact process changes. Knowledge of how systems emit and log evaluation-ready data and how exceptions trigger intervention becomes essential.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Identify needs
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources, collaborates across internal/external stakeholder communities, and is responsible for outreach to leverage new methods and sources to respond to user needs ('Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs'). Future GSBPM expectation: 'Identify needs' will require solution-oriented pre-assessment of all existing data assets, and integrate digital, cost, risk, and automation readiness into needs triage, further formalizing the evaluation of data reusability and automation potential. Role evolution: The Specialist’s activities will expand from outreach and data integration to include responsibility for digital discovery, cross-program feasibility assessment, documenting the business case for new collections, and supporting the enterprise-wide coordination of needs identification. Engagement with AI/automation platforms, cost model analysis, and digital stakeholder tools becomes integral to their operational workflow. Capability implication: The role will need deep familiarity with metadata-driven data asset inventory, digital collaboration workflows, enterprise business intelligence, and solution scoping that includes automation, reusability, and risk/impact assessment across internal and external data ecosystems.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Consult and Confirm Needs
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration' manages activities related to data integration, data analytics, and data acquisition—including outreach and collaboration with stakeholders to 'establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs.' The role leads projects involving acquisition and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs and participates in negotiations for data acquisition. Future GSBPM expectation: There will be increased reliance on data discovery platforms for stakeholder engagement. Needs confirmation is expected to be iterative, rapid, and anchored in the review of existing assets, reducing the default to new data collection. Role evolution: The Specialist will need to facilitate consultations using automated systems, jointly assess data assets, and move beyond traditional survey-centric approaches. Decision-making will be more outcome-driven, requiring the ability to structure engagements around prioritization criteria, trade-offs, and explicit reuse versus collection arguments. Capability implication: Advanced expertise in platform-based data asset navigation, co-assessment of fit-for-purpose, collaborative stakeholder facilitation, and synthesis of outcome-oriented options becomes more central in this role.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Establish output objectives
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration manages activities related to data integration, manipulation, analytics and dissemination, including 'setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis.' The role includes complex project leadership for data acquisition, integration, alternative sources, and stakeholder outreach for leveraging data/methods. These activities are fundamentally entwined with establishing output objectives for analytical/statistical programs. Future GSBPM expectation: Output objectives will be required to default to asset reuse, prioritize interoperability, machine-actionability, and automation-readiness, and be assessed for feasibility within strict resource/digital workflow constraints. Role evolution: The Specialist will need to lead in assessing digital feasibility and automation compatibility for new output objectives, justify any new survey or manual process as part of program planning, and actively embed interoperability and machine-readiness requirements in program objectives. Cross-disciplinary collaboration at the objective-setting stage will become critical. Capability implication: Elevated requirement for deep knowledge of agency data ecosystem, integration techniques, automation and digital workflow feasibility, interoperability standards, and rigorous justification and documentation of objective value cases within a digital production framework.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Check data availability and suitability
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration' (EC-06) 'leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs,' 'responsible for outreach and collaboration with ... stakeholders ... to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources.' This role involves not just integration but direct negotiation and acquisition. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future-state, the acquisition and suitability assessment processes are automated and prioritized; the specialist's involvement is reserved for edge cases too complex for automation, negotiating access, vetting legal and privacy risks, and ensuring metadata quality. Survey launches become rarer, with greater scrutiny on justification using evidence from automated tools. Role evolution: The specialist shifts from manual search and analysis towards overseeing and validating automated processes, curating metadata, managing external partnerships, and undertaking negotiations. Their expertise is needed for complex cases—such as new, proprietary or highly sensitive data types—and to ensure legal/ethical standards. Capability implication: Increased importance is placed on understanding machine-actionable metadata structures, legal and privacy frameworks in data acquisition, and advanced negotiation techniques. Deep knowledge of automated data discovery tools will be critical, together with the ability to strategically manage relationships with new multi-sector data providers.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Design variables
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: The Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration (EC-06) leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage, the development of analytical outputs, and collaborates with a wide range of stakeholders to understand user needs and bring new methods and data sources (see: 'leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary'). This position is engaged with implementing tools and software, program development, and ensuring overall quality and completeness. Future GSBPM expectation: Variable design will be standardized, designed for automated ingestion, interoperability and metadata-driven reuse across integrated pipelines. Analysts will need to ensure all variable definitions and metadata are compatible with enterprise standards and registries. Role evolution: The Specialist's responsibilities will shift toward ensuring variables used in integration projects are registered, interoperable by default, and richly described; less manual curation, more stewardship and quality assurance of reusable variable structures and metadata, and collaboration in maintaining variable libraries essential for automation and AI consumption. Capability implication: The role will require deeper insight into enterprise registries, interoperability protocols, metadata enrichment, and how integrated variable structures enable automated analysis and real-time integration.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Design collection
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: The 'Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration (EC-06)' manages data integration and analytics, including leading projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage, and use of alternative data sources, as stated: 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources...' In the new GSBPM future state, 'Design collection' requires prioritization and integration of existing and alternative data sources before any survey is considered, and demands automated, modular, and metadata-driven systems. The Specialist’s responsibilities already intersect with these requirements, but the evolution demands they transition from project-basis data acquisition and manual integration to configuration and oversight of automated frameworks that orchestrate collection strategies using AI, modular tools, and reusable APIs. Activities increasingly focus on curating and monitoring automated workflows, validating AI-generated instruments, and ensuring interoperability and ethical compliance across data acquisition channels—rather than solely negotiating and manually integrating one-off alternative sources. The role will require deeper engagement in framework-level management, oversight of automated processes, and continuous validation, rather than hands-on integration for each project. Capabilities in managing metadata-driven collection architectures, automation supervision, and system-wide interoperability management now become essential.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Design frame and sample
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: The EC-06 Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration currently manages activities related to data integration, manipulation, and use of alternative data sources, and leads projects involving acquisition, integration, and linkage of new data sources (e.g., 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs'). With the GSBPM 'Design frame and sample' moving toward automated, metadata-driven selection of frames and samples that prioritize administrative and alternative sources, the Specialist's role will become more central to orchestrating automated pipelines and defining data integration requirements for automated sample design. The role will evolve to provide critical oversight and domain expertise ensuring that integrated administrative/alternative data feeds are fit-for-purpose for automated sampling logic, that metadata is correctly structured for modular selection, and that ambiguous cases are properly resolved. Capability implications are increased importance of advanced understanding of data integration in the context of automated sampling, metadata management, oversight of AI-driven process outputs, and ability to resolve integration exceptions and edge cases.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Create frame and select sample
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: The EC-06 Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration holds responsibilities for data integration, analytics, and processing, including use of alternative data sources (“Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs”). This specialist manages activities that include setting objectives, overseeing program development and quality assurance, and collaborating with stakeholders to leverage new methods and sources. Under GSBPM 4.1’s strategic shift towards automation and alternative data for frame and sampling, this specialist will play a more central role in procedural oversight, exception handling, and methodological innovation related to the automated generation and maintenance of sampling frames derived from fused administrative and alternative data assets. Their responsibilities will increasingly require monitoring output quality from automated systems, evaluating integrated register-based and algorithmic sample creation, and contributing to continuous improvement of AI-enabled sampling logic. As a result, advanced methodological knowledge in automated data asset fusion, algorithmically optimized sample selection, and frame coverage evaluation become crucial.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Run collection
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration' (EC-06) leads data acquisition, integration, and use of alternative data sources, manages complex projects, and participates or leads negotiations for new data acquisition. The position is 'responsible for outreach and collaboration with stakeholders... to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments.'
Future GSBPM expectation: Data acquisition and integration activities must transition to supporting orchestrated, automated pipelines dominated by administrative and alternative sources, with survey-based data incorporated only as an exception. Stakeholder engagement explicitly focuses on system-level integration, digital acquisition, and process automation.
Role evolution: The Specialist must evolve from project-focused management of manual and semi-automated data integration tasks to the architectural design, implementation, and oversight of automated acquisition streams and digital platforms. Collaboration and negotiation now center on digital system integration agreements, API specifications, and continuous integration of alternative sources within automated workflows. Monitoring and process optimization rely increasingly on dashboard technologies and paradata.
Capability implication: Expertise in digital acquisition architecture, event-driven orchestration, automated data ingestion, API negotiation, and real-time dashboard-centric process monitoring is vital, alongside knowledge of exception management within highly automated environments.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Integrate data
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Currently, the 'Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration' role is responsible for managing activities related to data integration, data manipulation, analytics, processing, and preparation of dissemination and visualization products. This includes leading projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage, and leveraging alternative sources to respond to user needs (e.g., 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs'). These efforts often rely on manual intervention, bespoke integration processes, and ad hoc linkage strategies, as well as collaboration with stakeholders to establish new methods and sources. The future GSBPM expectation for data integration is a shift toward automated, metadata-rich, modular pipelines with minimal human intervention, where manual linkages and harmonization are replaced by platform-enabled, auditable, and standardized workflows. The Specialist’s activities would evolve from hands-on manipulation and project-specific solutions to configuring reusable integration components, managing event-driven pipelines, and focusing primarily on exceptions and integration-rule enhancements rather than custom coding. This demands a higher emphasis on pipeline logic, metadata management, interface governance, and auditable provenance, making knowledge of microservices, FAIR principles, and cross-domain deployable solutions central. Capabilities around logic abstraction, managing interoperability, and governing end-to-end automated processes become more important in this future state.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Review and validate
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: The Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration (EC-06) manages activities related to data integration, manipulation, analytics, processing, and the preparation of dissemination products, and 'ensures overall quality and completeness of program results.' While current responsibilities include implementation of tools/software and preparation of outputs, the future state of validation (GSBPM 5.3) shifts the entire error detection/validation workflow into automated, orchestrated processes. The Specialist’s role changes from hands-on validation and data manipulation to designing, overseeing, and evaluating the effectiveness of integrated, automated validation modules, orchestrating their interaction across subject-matter and data sources, and feeding back identified exceptions for rule improvement. This makes critical the ability to collaborate with pipeline designers, understand validation rule logic, manage exceptions, and contribute to the continuous improvement of validation frameworks within cross-domain pipelines.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Calculate weights
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: The Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration (EC-06) currently 'leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary,' and 'manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products.' The GSBPM shift implies that weighting is no longer handled through bespoke project routines but through system-level, reusable, modular services that must seamlessly process weights for integrated and alternative sources using standardized, AI-augmented methods as part of a pipeline. The Specialist's activities will pivot toward designing and configuring reusable weighting modules, governing their metadata and logic, reviewing system logs and AI outputs for adaptive weighting, and collaborating on governance processes for calibration and exceptions. Thus, capability needs will expand from custom programming and hands-on manipulation toward modular pipeline design, orchestration, embedded standards, and auditability across diverse input sources.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Calculate aggregates
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: This role manages activities related to data integration, manipulation, analytics, processing, and dissemination, setting objectives, implementing tools or software, and ensuring quality and completeness of results. The "implementation of various tools or software" currently includes hands-on aggregation through programmatic means, often requiring custom scripts, algorithms, or manual validation. Future GSBPM expectation: Aggregation logic will be embedded in standardized, automated microservices within modular data pipelines, orchestrated across programs. Responsibilities will move away from custom tool implementation toward configuring, monitoring, and validating centrally managed aggregation modules and workflows, tracking metadata for audit and reproducibility, and supporting exception handling for diverse subject-matter domains. Role evolution: The Specialist will be expected to shift from direct technical implementation toward configuration of automated processes, interpretation and validation of outputs, and contribution to governance processes that ensure shared components comply with standardization and auditability requirements. Capability implication: The knowledge base expands to cover pipeline configuration, automated aggregation module management, metadata lineage, and the ability to interpret and explain outputs of AI-enabled aggregation microservices, ensuring exception handling is properly governed and documented.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Prepare draft outputs
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: EC-06 Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration manages 'activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products.' This involves setting objectives and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results, which directly includes assembling and preparing draft outputs for dissemination and visualization. Future GSBPM expectation: Output drafting will be automated, shifting the role from technical assembly to overseeing system performance, ensuring quality of automated outputs, and handling exceptions, with new emphasis on interpretation and contextualization. Role evolution: Responsibilities transition from hands-on preparation to monitoring and reviewing AI-generated outputs, troubleshooting pipeline issues, and ensuring correct contextual alignment of results. Capability implication: Increased demand for advanced pipeline monitoring and troubleshooting, oversight of automated output generation, and capacity for high-value contextual interpretation of analytical products.

Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.title: Interpret and explain outputs
Specialist, Data Analytics and Integrati.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration manages activities related to data integration, manipulation, analytics, preparation of dissemination products, and provides expert advice and analysis. Currently, the role includes managing teams responsible for statistical outputs and leading projects involving data acquisition, integration, and analysis ("Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products..."). Future GSBPM expectation: With automation of data manipulation and standardized analysis, the focus shifts to interpretation, contextualization, and communication of insights from automated outputs. Routine technical activities are reduced, and the role centers on reviewing results for relevance, ethical considerations, and policy applicability. Role evolution: The Specialist must now emphasize deep subject-matter interpretation of outputs, ensure responsible communication, and oversee the fairness and transparency of automated analytical pipelines. Capability implication: Greater importance is placed on domain expertise, transparency in interpretation, oversight of AI methods, and ethical framing of results.

Assistant Director.title: Identify needs
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 Assistant Director directs sub-divisional statistical program operations and leads high-profile survey, study, and data integration projects. The role includes reviewing strategic directions for the management of significant surveys, defending proposals for new survey development, and negotiating allocation of funding for projects ('Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives...Defends proposals for the development of new surveys and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of projects'). Future GSBPM expectation: The operational context for needs identification requires surveys to be a last resort, only after documented assessment of existing/internal/alternative data sources and automation solutions, and mandates explicit cost-benefit and timeliness trade-offs based on enterprise-wide resource and strategic fit. Role evolution: The Assistant Director must move from a primarily survey-centric option set to overseeing rigorous digital pre-assessment of needs, ensure their teams implement standardized tools for discovery across all data holdings, and personally defend business cases for new surveys only when all digital/automated alternatives are exhausted. Budget and resource planning will also shift toward multi-source, cross-program asset reuse and digital feasibility prioritization. Capability implication: Leadership must be able to direct, interpret, and defend assessments of digital data assets, automation readiness, and sustainability at the needs-identification stage, integrating them into both strategic project selection and resource negotiation in ways compliant with StatCan2030 mandates.

Assistant Director.title: Consult and Confirm Needs
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Assistant Director' directs sub-divisional work in statistical operations, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination, including approving survey content/design, sample methods, and integration from different sources. The role involves reviewing strategic directions, defending proposals for new surveys, negotiating funding, and providing expert recommendations on the socio-economic implications of studies and surveys. The Assistant Director also mediates with senior stakeholders to establish agreements and to address user needs. Future GSBPM expectation: Needs confirmation will prioritize review of existing and alternative data assets; proposals for new surveys will be subject to stricter criteria, only advanced when gaps remain after exhaustive asset review. Consultation cycles are to be shorter and structured, focusing on cost-benefit, feasibility, and reuse. Role evolution: The Assistant Director will need to lead more outcome-driven, rapid, and transparent consultation cycles—moving from traditional survey advocacy to asset-centric analysis, using automated platforms to guide negotiations. Defending new surveys will require clear, evidence-based justification centered on organizational priorities and reuse potential. Capability implication: This change requires enhanced capability in synthesizing machine-actionable metadata, supporting transparent stakeholder dialogue, navigating asset-centric assessment platforms, and articulating cost-benefit and reuse trade-offs during multi-stakeholder negotiations.

Assistant Director.title: Establish output objectives
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 Assistant Director directs sub-divisional work across statistical program operations. They 'develop long term plans and objectives', approve survey content/design, assess integration with other data sources, recommend survey objectives/content, and defend proposals for new surveys, including resource allocation. The role includes approval and strategic direction-setting for objectives of survey/analytical programs. Future GSBPM expectation: The establishment of output objectives is pivoting from survey-centric or user-driven acceptance to a 'data ecosystem optimization' model. Approvals require evidence that re-use or automation is maximized, and that new surveys or manual processes are justified with agency-aligned cost-benefit analysis. Automation-readiness, real-time delivery, and digital workflows become explicit acceptance factors. Role evolution: The Assistant Director will need to embed automation, interoperability, and digital feasibility criteria at the earliest stage of objective-setting and approval. Survey initiation and resource allocation decisions will only proceed with thorough evaluation of all alternative data assets and automated delivery models, and collaboration with project/IT stakeholders. Capability implication: Enhanced knowledge regarding enterprise automation frameworks, data source integration, interoperability and machine-actionability, as well as ability to formally evaluate value cases and cost-benefit of manual/survey initiatives under digital execution constraints.

Assistant Director.title: Identify Concepts
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs sub-divisions focused on statistical program operations and is accountable for approving survey content and design—including data concepts and definitions for programs (decision_making | 'Directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results... Develops recommendations for senior management on the objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs in order to develop new statistical information or programs or expand existing programs, and data concepts and definitions to be included in the programs.'). Their responsibilities include strategic review of concepts at the program level and mediation with stakeholders around concepts and practices (communication | 'Mediates with senior executives... to monitor relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results.'). Future GSBPM expectation: Identifying concepts is increasingly machine-driven, requiring directors to advocate for enterprise-wide alignment, justify deviations from standardized assets, and ensure rapid arbitration in compressed timelines. The strategic focus is on validation, prioritization, negotiation, and the integration of concept identification within end-to-end digital architectures. Role evolution: The Assistant Director’s responsibilities will center on steering cross-program alignment, orchestrating arbitration and conflict resolution among AI-proposed concepts, and establishing justification processes for rare deviations from machine-suggested frameworks, rather than top-down manual development of concepts. Capability implication: Skills in enterprise metadata analysis, policy negotiation, digital platform integration, and arbitration for alignment across multiple domains gain heightened importance, along with the ability to evaluate and endorse machine-generated conceptual recommendations.

Assistant Director.title: Check data availability and suitability
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 'Assistant Director' directs the review and assessment of survey quality, recommends strategic directions, approves survey content and design, and assesses data integration options. They also 'defend proposals for the development of new surveys' and negotiate allocation of funding. Importantly, this leadership role directs recommendations about launching surveys vs. leveraging administrative or alternative data sources. Future GSBPM expectation: The default in future is to exhaust existing and alternative data sources (via automated, exhaustive scans) and only launch surveys if automated tools demonstrate necessity, with evidence. Survey planning becomes an exception, with higher stakes, deeper vetting, and greater scrutiny. Human involvement will be focused on overseeing technology-enabled assessment processes, legal vetting, and negotiating access to new sources, rather than routine survey launch planning. Role evolution: Assistant Directors must shift their strategic decision-making from balancing various data source options ad-hoc, to operating in an ecosystem where surveys are only justified by transparent, algorithmic evidence of necessity. Their leadership is critical in managing complex legal/risk cases, securing partnership agreements, and defending rare survey launches through evidence-based argumentation. Capability implication: Ability to interpret automated suitability screening results, understand machine-actionable metadata logic, and lead complex negotiations and legal/ethical risk assessments with new and existing data holders becomes central. Deep knowledge of decision rules governing automated source scans and ability to manage multidisciplinary teams working on new data partnerships is required.

Assistant Director.title: Prepare and submit business case
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 Assistant Director is responsible for reviewing strategic directions, defending proposals for new surveys, and negotiating resource allocations for projects. The work description highlights this through statements such as, 'Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives,' and 'Defends proposals for the development of new surveys and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of projects.' Future GSBPM expectation: The revised business case process requires explicit consideration of automation-first solutions, prioritization of non-survey data, and empirical cost-benefit justifications, fundamentally redefining how proposals are constructed and evaluated. Role evolution: The Assistant Director's role must shift from defending traditional, survey-centric proposals and incremental improvements to actively building cases for scalable, automated, and modular approaches that are aligned with corporate platforms and able to be rapidly iterated or stopped if conditions change. The approval process becomes more agile and expects transparent trade-offs instead of exhaustive legacy documentation. Capability implication: Strategic understanding of automation and enterprise platforms, rapid option analysis, and disciplined, evidence-driven recommendation are now central. Capability to justify alignment with automation, data reuse, and outcome-driven logic is increasingly essential for proposal success.

Assistant Director.title: Design variables
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs major statistical program operations, approves survey content and design, and develops recommendations for program objectives and data concepts (see: 'approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations... develops recommendations for senior management on the objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs... and data concepts and definitions to be included in the programs'). Their decisions directly influence the adoption of definitions, classifications, and methods across programs. Future GSBPM expectation: As variable design is formalized into enterprise-registry and standardized frameworks, approval and direction must consider interoperability, automated downstream use, metadata quality, and reusability across domains. Role evolution: The Assistant Director's decision-making must prioritize enterprise-standard variable design, alignment to FAIR principles, and the enablement of automated ingestion and transformation processes. Their oversight extends into new governance, cross-program stewardship, and ensuring variables are suitable for AI and automation-driven processes. Capability implication: Familiarity with enterprise metadata systems, semantic registries, and how variable choices impact automation and analytic infrastructures will become a core part of their strategic and operational capacity.

Assistant Director.title: Design collection
Assistant Director.justification: The 'Assistant Director (EC-08)' oversees significant survey and program operations, with authority to approve survey design, negotiate agreements, and review strategic directions: 'Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys...Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration...' The shift in 'Design collection' mandates that surveys are no longer the default, requiring business units to prioritize data acquisition from administrative and alternative sources, and to integrate AI and automation into instrument and workflow design. As a result, the Assistant Director's strategic planning and decision-making must now pivot from managing and defending bespoke survey operations—often involving lengthy stakeholder negotiation and resource allocation—to curating standardized, modular, and automated frameworks for collection, guiding their teams to focus efforts on system-level integration, configuration, and validation of AI-driven outputs. Their role will require closer collaboration with IT/data governance, oversight of ethical constraints and system guardrails, and stewardship of interoperability and machine-actionability in collection processes. Thus, deep capability in platform integration, automated process management, and strategic oversight of AI-mediated collection designs becomes vital, moving beyond traditional survey pilot and management activities.

Assistant Director.title: Design frame and sample
Assistant Director.justification: The EC-08 Assistant Director directs programs covering survey design, sample estimation, imputation methods, and the integration of data sources ('Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints'). The future GSBPM expectation is a shift towards survey as a last resort, with automation and AI driving frame/sample design and prioritization of alternative data. The Assistant Director's responsibilities will transition to setting standards for automated processes, making strategic decisions about when to intervene in automated processes, overseeing quality of AI-generated sample designs, and defining criteria for selection/optimization of frames and sources across programs. There will be a greater emphasis on strategic oversight and governance of automated, modular systems—ensuring interoperability, intake standards, and evaluating outcomes. Capability implication is deeper proficiency in managing/overseeing automated sampling designs, operationalizing standards for AI-driven decision logic, and quality assurance of cross-domain integration and reuse of frames and samples.

Assistant Director.title: Create frame and select sample
Assistant Director.justification: The EC-08 Assistant Director is responsible for directing work that spans statistical program operations, analysis, and program management; specifically, they approve survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, and integration of data from different sources (“Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency...”). The role also directs reviews of quality and completeness of program results, and develops recommendations on objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs. With GSBPM 4.1’s transformation to automation and ‘surveys as last resort’, the Assistant Director must pivot towards governance and oversight of automated frame/sample processes, making strategic decisions regarding the invocation of survey sampling only when alternative sources are insufficient. The role will focus more on monitoring and evaluating process outputs, managing exceptions and rare cases requiring human expertise, and guiding methodological R&D. Their responsibilities will require more forward-looking, strategic evaluation of data asset potential, algorithmic sampling quality, and enterprise-wide sample coordination.

Assistant Director.title: Set up collection
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs the strategic management of survey programs and approves content, design, sampling, and data integration, including proposing innovative solutions and approving operational parameters. Their remit covers negotiation, resource allocation, and overseeing quality and completeness of survey results. Future GSBPM expectation: Operation is driven by enterprise-automated, AI-assisted workflows; the set-up activities are standardized, modular, and rapidly executed, with staff focusing on validating system logic, monitoring risk and quality, and exception management. Role evolution: The Assistant Director will shift from direct oversight of operational preparation, staff training, and bespoke survey instrument design toward high-level governance over self-service platform implementations, ensuring risk, quality, interoperability, and ethical compliance in automated setups. Strategic direction pivots to evaluating system outputs, approving new data integrations, and managing rare exceptions, rather than the day-to-day preparation. Capability implication: Strategic oversight now requires deep understanding of automated logic, risk/quality management in system-driven environments, and an ability to evaluate alternate and external data integration as the set-up process compresses and pivots away from manual execution.

Assistant Director.title: Run collection
Assistant Director.justification:
Current responsibility: The Assistant Director (EC-08) sets directions for survey management, approves content and design, directs unique surveys, and recommends strategic solutions to survey operations. The role 'develops recommendations for senior management on the objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs... expands existing programs, and data concepts and definitions.' They are also responsible for reviewing and assessing the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results.
Future GSBPM expectation: 'Run collection' is fundamentally transformed with surveys as a fallback option, automated via AI-driven platforms, and orchestrated among multiple digital data streams. This requires oversight of hybrid collection modes, prioritization of non-survey sources, and real-time, system-led process monitoring.
Role evolution: As direct field collection becomes rare, the EC-08 Assistant Director must pivot their focus from survey content management and logistics to strategic oversight of automated collection systems, prioritization of alternative data acquisition, and optimization of AI-enabled survey deployments. Operational guidance will transition from project management of manual fieldwork to governance, supervision, and continuous improvement of multi-source, event-driven collection platforms. Human interventions must now center on quality assurance, monitoring system signals, managing exceptions, and ensuring effective AI workflows.
Capability implication: Advanced knowledge of digital collection orchestration, integration of administrative and alternative sources, AI-driven survey deployment principles, real-time monitoring for quality, and digital stakeholder relationship management become crucial.

Assistant Director.title: Review and validate
Assistant Director.justification: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs the work of sub-divisions involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, dissemination, and critically, 'directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results.' The future expectation of GSBPM 5.3 places the responsibility for ensuring automated validation processes are robust, audit-ready, and fully integrated across domains and sources. The Assistant Director’s decision-making must shift from managing manual review processes and responding to quality gaps, to setting strategic direction for orchestration and governance of automated validation systems. This involves supporting continuous improvement of validation rules, setting oversight standards, and managing cross-functional teams focused on pipeline monitoring and exception management. The centrality of pipeline governance, enterprise-level audit standards, and oversight of AI-enabled quality processes becomes more pronounced.

Assistant Director.title: Calculate weights
Assistant Director.justification: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs the work of sub-divisions focused on survey operations, approves sample estimation and imputation methods, and 'directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results,' as well as developing recommendations for senior management on survey objectives and methods. With weighting now embedded within automated pipelines, the Assistant Director's responsibilities shift from approving and overseeing human-driven calculation workflows to ensuring the continuous governance, calibration, and strategic oversight of automated routines, including reviewing system-level performance, auditing version-controlled processes, and managing exceptions arising from pipeline operation. The role evolves into one where methodological changes, system enhancements, and cross-program consistency are managed as governance interventions within automated environments, requiring new capabilities in strategic oversight of modular services, adaptive AI-supported methodologies, and setting standards for system-wide deployment.

Assistant Director.title: Prepare draft outputs
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 Assistant Director 'directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination,' reviews program quality and completeness, and sets strategic directions relating to survey content and output dissemination. The role includes approving and overseeing methodological and operational approaches to preparing draft outputs. Future GSBPM expectation: The Assistant Director's focus will shift more toward setting strategic directions for automated analytical pipelines, monitoring their effectiveness, and ensuring oversight of exception handling and system performance. Role evolution: The position will move toward governance of automated pipelines, agile updating of templates and AI frameworks, and broader oversight of operational dependencies, validation, and quality control, with less involvement in technical output preparation. Capability implication: System-level oversight, governance for automated output sign-off, and performance metrics in AI-driven environments will be critical for this position.

Assistant Director.title: Interpret and explain outputs
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 Assistant Director directs statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination through subordinate teams, provides expert recommendations to senior officials, approves and explains socio-economic survey results, and develops conclusions and recommendations from analytical material ("Provides expert recommendations and advice to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government...on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information..."). Future GSBPM expectation: With routine analytic preparation automated, the focus is on oversight of interpretation, responsible narrative communication, and assurance of quality, fairness, and transparency in AI-generated outputs. Assistant Directors must ensure that outputs are meaningfully integrated into policy, societal, and operational contexts, and oversee human-AI collaboration frameworks. Role evolution: The role requires greater emphasis on evaluation of automated outputs, ensuring the ethical interpretation and relevance for decision makers, defending the credibility and transparency of analytic outputs, and guiding teams to focus on insight and user impact. Capability implication: Deep expertise is required in methodological boundaries of automated analytics, data ethics, transparency frameworks, and in communicating complex findings effectively and responsibly.

Assistant Director.title: Apply disclosure control
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs sub-divisions through subordinates involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing, and dissemination, establishes strategic directions, approves survey content, and ensures compliance with confidentiality laws/policies ('Knowledge of the Statistics Act ... and of the Privacy Act ... to ensure ... confidentiality of all information provided ...'). Future GSBPM expectation: As disclosure control is programmatically embedded in production pipelines, the Assistant Director will be responsible for strategic oversight of its implementation, auditing, and exception handling, and for ensuring enterprise-wide policy compliance as dissemination diversifies and accelerates. Role evolution: The Assistant Director's role shifts from overseeing manual/analyst-driven disclosure processes to directing operational oversight, policy design, and audit/compliance activities for embedded, automated disclosure controls, including resource allocation for upskilling and adaptation strategies. Capability implication: Broader strategic and operational awareness of enterprise-level implementation, monitoring, and escalation processes for automated disclosure control, alignment of policy and system design, and accountability for ethical deployment and auditability across all teams.

Assistant Director.title: Conduct evaluation
Assistant Director.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-08 'Assistant Director' directly oversees the review and assessment of statistical program quality and completeness, develops recommendations for senior management, and is accountable for strategic direction based on periodic evaluations and the interpretation of survey results. The methodology includes organizing and approving quality reviews and producing summaries and recommendations for large-scale, often post-hoc, program changes. Future GSBPM expectation: Under a regime of automated, real-time evaluation, the Assistant Director must oversee a much more dynamic environment where evaluation is continuous, system-integrated, and largely automated. The operational focus shifts toward interpreting the constant feed of performance metrics, benchmarking to standards, and collaborating with technical staff for iterative, modular improvements. Role evolution: The role must adapt from overseeing periodic, narrative-based assessment toward ongoing, dashboard-driven management, ensuring that all interventions—both technical and analytical—follow from system evidence and are logged and tracked for transparency and governance. The Assistant Director's strategic advice centers less on synthesizing evidence manually and more on demonstrating leadership in responding to event-driven indicators and guaranteeing agile, data-driven improvements across the division.
