Capability implication: Mastery of automated evaluation systems, understanding KPI design and event logic, and operationalizing modular process changes become management imperatives, as does governance over how evaluation outputs are escalated and acted on.

Assistant Director.title: Agree an action plan
Assistant Director.justification:
Current responsibility: The Assistant Director (EC-08) directs, through subordinates, the management of subdivisions involved in statistical program operations, analysis, and review. The position 'reviews strategic directions' and 'develops recommendations for senior management', including negotiation of resources and overseeing the quality and objectives of survey programs. The role is responsible for allocating resources and developing long-term plans, implying significant involvement in both forming and ensuring execution of action plans derived from program evaluations or program needs.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future model requires action plans to be formulated and deployed across automated and modular infrastructures, emphasizing real-time monitoring, rapid follow-through, distributed accountability, and highly transparent and iterative adjustment. Ownership and progress are digitally tracked, and impact monitoring is expected to be continuous as opposed to periodic.

Role evolution: The Assistant Director's approach to action planning must pivot from hands-on oversight and negotiation through traditional channels to orchestrating, facilitating, and ensuring the effectiveness of digital, enterprise-scale mechanisms for action plan assignment, execution, and recalibration. Assistant Directors must ensure plans are actionable within automated systems and that their outcomes are tracked and visible across the organization. They will serve as key nodes in a transparent, agile governance model rather than acting exclusively as final authorities.

Capability implication: This future state raises the importance of understanding and leveraging enterprise workflow and action plan management tools, algorithmic impact monitoring methodologies, and digital dashboards for real-time visibility and follow-up. Familiarity with agile organizational models, and the facilitation of distributed decision authority and accountability, become central to effective leadership in this context.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Identify needs
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 role includes reviewing data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of existing data sources, proposing changes, assessing feasibility/impact of new or modified programs, and analyzing current socio-economic trends to provide recommendations ('Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs'). Future GSBPM expectation: Needs identification will require systematic inventorying and scanning of existing data, alternative sources, and digital platforms, with formalized cost-benefit and risk criteria; the process shifts to digital, metadata-driven, rapid triage, rather than reactive adjustments. Role evolution: The Economist/Sociologist must expand from ad hoc or subject-matter expert-driven program suggestions to actively contributing to digital discovery processes, triaging program feasibility against automation and reuse potential, and documenting justification for new collection only after full evaluation of alternatives. Capability implication: This role must be able to critically assess and synthesize information from agency-wide digital data platforms and understand enterprise-level risk, cost, and automation criteria, so that their recommendations are aligned with the StatCan2030 vision for solution-first needs identification.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Design variables
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The Economist/Sociologist 4 (EC-04) analyzes statistical program data, assists in developing recommendations for improvements to survey methods, and provides advice to data users (see: 'modifies existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions. Develops operational plans and project priorities and identifies areas necessitating study at the local, regional or national levels'). They review data collection and information systems, propose changes, and support subject-matter concept development. Future GSBPM expectation: Variable design will move from project-based definition toward stewardship of standardized, metadata-rich frameworks, requiring collaboration in maintaining enterprise variable and metadata repositories. Role evolution: The role will move away from bespoke, manual variable definition, toward participating in the enhancement and adoption of enterprise-reusable variable structures, supporting alignment to standards and metadata richness, and ensuring operational adherence to interoperability requirements. Capability implication: Deeper familiarity will be required in collaborative metadata management, enterprise registries, FAIR-compliance, and stewardship of shared variable libraries rather than ad hoc project-specific definitions.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Design frame and sample
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 currently modifies and improves statistical methods, reviews data collection systems, and leads analytical teams evaluating program methods and feasibility ('Modifies existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs... develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; reviews data collection and information systems to determine usefulness of existing data sources...'). With GSBPM's 'Design frame and sample' embracing automated, metadata-driven frame/sample pipelines and prioritizing alternative data, this role must evolve from active manual design of surveys/samples to oversight and interpretation of automated selections, troubleshooting exceptions, and improving metadata frameworks. Responsibilities will lean more towards validating the suitability of administrative/alternative data for frame/sample creation, collaborating across teams to set requirements for automated processes, and resolving cases that the automation cannot address. Capability implication is heightened importance of expertise with metadata-driven processes, knowledge of integration of administrative/alternative sources, and oversight of AI-based frame/sample design outputs.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 'Economist/Sociologist 4' leads project teams for special studies, develops recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities, reviews data collection and system usefulness, and modifies approaches based on subject-area changes. Responsibilities also include translating requirements into system development specifications and advising on improvements. Evidence: 'Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.' Future GSBPM expectation: With collection instrument creation moving to platform-driven, automated and modular pipelines, the role will shift from recommending bespoke improvements to actively configuring, validating, and managing automated, metadata-rich collection instruments within self-service environments. Role evolution: Instead of hands-on instrument design or manual system modifications, responsibility centers on configuring platform components, validating automated extraction routines, and enforcing enterprise standards for metadata, digital guardrails, and paradata. Capability implication: Deep understanding of modular, automated platform configuration, enterprise metadata schemas, compliance protocols, and the validation of automated instrument creation routines grows in importance.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Test production systems
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 4 (EC-04) is tasked with reviewing data collection and information systems, proposing changes, reviewing feasibility and impact of modified statistical programs, and assessing and resolving problems in statistical information processing ("Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs"; "Identifies and evaluates problems in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management"). Previously, system testing likely involved manual or locally-developed approaches. In the future GSBPM environment, automatic, integrated testing becomes a routine, governed requirement for any changes, requiring the role to embed test suite design and attestation into operational plans, to take responsibility for reproducibility, compliance, and security within every project, and to translate analytical requirements into testable, enterprise-validated specifications. The role shifts from recommending improvements at a component/subject-matter level to operationalizing enterprise test frameworks, documenting evidence for attestation-based approval, and ensuring audit-ready change practices. Capabilities in automated testing, regulatory compliance, reproducibility documentation, and integration with business-led low/no-code development environments are increasingly critical.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Test statistical business process
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 is involved in reviewing and analyzing the effectiveness of collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods, and assists in developing recommendations for improvements. There is direct evidence of providing feedback on methods and procedures based on analysis and review, as well as suggesting improvements and leading teams involved in special studies. Key technical activities include analyzing and synthesizing methods, reviewing development of new methods, and conducting studies to improve surveys and data. Future GSBPM expectation: As 'Test statistical business process' becomes more formalized and rigorous in the future state, there is an increased expectation on design, implementation, and evaluation of testing protocols for statistical processes. This involves not just ad hoc feedback, but structured, documented, and iterative testing including scenario-based evaluations, pre-implementation assessments, and the use of more systematic approaches to process validation. Role evolution: The Economist/Sociologist 4 will need to play a more active and structured role in defining, executing, and documenting test plans for new or modified statistical processes, including contributing to the development of formal testing frameworks, participating in prototype testing, tracking test outcomes, and feeding systematic observations into process improvement cycles. Capability implication: This will increase the need for knowledge and application of process testing design and evaluation techniques, familiarity with automated testing or test harnesses for statistical systems, and understanding of how to document, interpret, and communicate test results for process improvement and risk mitigation.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Create frame and select sample
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 role currently includes participating in the analysis of socio-economic trends, reviewing data collection and information systems, suggesting feedback on collection, processing, editing, and compilation, and recommending improvements to survey methods and activities (“Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of... existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs”). With the GSBPM 4.1 transition, this position will need to increase its focus on monitoring and reviewing outputs from automated frame/sample creation modules, identifying issues in frame coverage, sample coordination and burden management, and participating in exception handling and recommendations for workflow refinements. The role’s feedback and improvement activities become more oriented to the evaluation of automated processes, AI-enabled modules, and integration logic, and less about routine sampling or manual frame management. Thus, capabilities related to auditing automated sampling outputs, understanding algorithmic logic, and performing advanced evaluations of composite data asset fitness become increasingly important.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Classify and code
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 undertakes analysis of statistical data, provides subject matter advice, leads project teams in reviewing and recommending improvements to collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods—including coding routines. This role interfaces directly with operational methods and coding approaches, giving feedback and suggesting enhancements, often at the granularity of clerical or manual processes. Future GSBPM expectation: Automated, AI-enabled classification and coding will replace routine human coding and operational involvement in day-to-day coding tasks, except for monitoring, validation, and exception management. Feedback will need to focus on pipeline functionality, AI output quality, and revision of standard classification schemes. Role evolution: This position's focus will move from recommending improvements to manual or semi-automated processes and providing direct subject-matter advice on coding operations, to participating in oversight and validation of automated coding pipelines, reporting anomalies, and supporting the maintenance and evolution of classification schemes. Capability implication: In-depth understanding of AI-enabled coding operations, monitoring and validation protocols, and update procedures for classification frameworks becomes critical, along with the ability to interpret and communicate exceptions or edge cases that require human resolution.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Edit and impute
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 assists in the analysis of statistical program data, provides feedback on editing and compilation procedures, and helps develop recommendations for improvements. The role also includes identifying and evaluating problems in the processing, editing, compilation, and presentation of information and writing reports/manuals for system implementation.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state replaces manual editing feedback loops with automated edit/impute routines, where oversight, validation, and exception management become the central responsibility. Traditional feedback on manual methods evolves into recommendations for AI-driven process improvements, performance review, and compliance.

Role evolution: The EC-04 position will shift from hands-on editing procedure evaluation to participating in the assessment and monitoring of AI-driven pipelines, refining automated edit/impute approaches, and providing feedback on algorithmic performance and exceptions encountered. Their role in report writing and system documentation will become more focused on auditability and reproducibility of automated edit/impute interventions.

Capability implication: Capabilities will shift toward evaluating automated outputs, participating in ethical and process oversight, audit trail analysis, and system traceability, moving away from manual editing proficiency.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Finalise data files
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 provides feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods following data analysis and assists in recommendations for improvements ('Suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.'). They also identify and evaluate problems in processing and compilation, providing solutions and recommendations. Future GSBPM expectation: The manual steps of consolidation, cleaning, and custom file formatting in the 'Finalise data files' process will be replaced by orchestrated, automated pipelines with rich metadata and strict version control. Exception handling, validation, and audit oversight will be the central focus. Role evolution: The incumbent will need to adapt their feedback and analysis work to the context of automated pipelines, validating the output of these systems, translating feedback into metadata adjustments or configuration changes, and resolving exceptions flagged by the system. Analytical recommendations will concern pipeline performance and compliance rather than manual procedure adjustments. Capability implication: This underscores the importance of understanding automated processing, metadata-driven validation, and reproducibility, as well as the capability to diagnose issues in automated production environments and interpret audit trails for decision making.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Prepare draft outputs
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 assists in 'the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and provides feedback on presentation methods as well as technical support in subject matter studies. Activities feature direct involvement in compiling, editing, and assembling tables, charts, and analytical content for draft outputs. Future GSBPM expectation: Draft outputs will be auto-generated, requiring staff to shift from manual assembly to interpreting and reviewing outputs, providing feedback primarily within an automated environment. Role evolution: Responsibilities will move toward monitoring automated processes, validating the integrity and appropriateness of automated outputs, and escalating exceptions for human review. Capability implication: Familiarity with automated tabulation and dashboard production, as well as critical output assessment in AI-driven environments, becomes more central, alongside knowledge of exception handling in automated systems.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Validate outputs
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 role currently undertakes analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for publication, which inherently involves validating outputs for accuracy ('Reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used'). Participates in data analysis and reviews collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods to assess quality, thus engaging in manual validation and quality assurance. Future GSBPM expectation: As validation becomes automated and metadata-driven, this role will increasingly need to oversee automated checks, interpret exceptions, and ensure trust in algorithmic validation, rather than relying on traditional manual review. Role evolution: The EC-04 will shift toward interpreting and providing context for exceptional cases uncovered by AI or orchestration tools. Their responsibilities will include monitoring validation processes and engaging in root-cause analysis for anomalies flagged by automation, focusing on oversight rather than execution. Capability implication: Greater importance on understanding automated validation frameworks, auditability, metadata-driven quality indicators, and interpreting exceptions, moving beyond manual assessment to system-based oversight and governance.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Interpret and explain outputs
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 undertakes the analysis of statistical program data, prepares analytical material for publication, provides subject matter advice to data users, interprets and reviews study and survey results, and writes/presents detailed concepts for program content ("Reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used"). Future GSBPM expectation: For future workflows, low-level analytic tasks (data cleaning, manipulation, descriptive statistics) will be automated, and EC-04 analysts will focus on interpreting and contextualizing output from automated pipelines, ensuring user relevance, and communicating limitations and ethical concerns. Role evolution: The position will be required to build subject-matter narratives from automated outputs, assess their policy/societal implications, and contribute to oversight and transparency of automated analysis. Capability implication: Stronger requirements for ethical and transparent interpretation, domain knowledge for contextual framing, and familiarity with AI-driven analytics, including their strengths and limitations.

Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Conduct evaluation
Economist/Sociologist 4.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 'Economist/Sociologist 4' is responsible for analyzing statistical program data, assisting in the preparation of analytical material, leading project teams for special studies, and, centrally, 'suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' Decision-making tasks include reviewing data collection and information systems, identifying and evaluating problems in statistical processing, and preparing management reports, all of which rely heavily on periodic, human-led review and subjective assessment. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state transforms evaluation into a real-time, system-driven function where ongoing monitoring, use of embedded dashboards and automated quality checks replace periodic, manual reviews. The evaluation emphasis is on interpreting automated metrics and rapid, system-driven identification of issues, shifting away from narrative report production toward log-based, actionable updates and agile process improvement. Role evolution: The Economist/Sociologist 4 will need to move from periodic review and ad hoc, narrative reporting into continuous engagement with system-generated dashboards, interpreting a stream of alerts, anomalies, and performance indicators, and collaborating quickly with cross-functional teams to enact modular improvements. Their feedback will transition from proposing after-the-fact system changes to promptly responding to event-driven signals and justifying interventions with evidence supplied by standardized, automated metrics. Capability implication: This accelerates the need for fluency in using, interpreting, and triaging automated performance dashboards, understanding how algorithmically generated insights lead to process change, and a deeper operational awareness of how interventions are tracked and increasingly codified through workflow and system updates. Familiarity with metadata, exception handling, and practical workflow management in automated settings becomes crucial.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Identify needs
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 investigates client requirements, defines scope and sources, assesses need for new studies, evaluates feasibility, and develops recommendations for improvements to survey content and coverage ('Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the nature and scope of studies, as well as the sources of information, methods and approaches to be used'). Future GSBPM expectation: All new statistical needs must be triaged through digital, automated platforms, inventorying all available data assets, explicit cost-benefit/risk analysis, and strategic fit assessment before any recommendation or proposal for new collection/survey activities. Role evolution: The position will move from program-focused, subject-matter-driven need identification to implementing digitally enabled, enterprise-wide scanning of data assets, documenting the rationale for new collections based on operational feasibility, resource and automation criteria, and collaborating across teams to ensure cross-program data reuse and digital/AI alignment. Capability implication: Greater focus on understanding digital discovery tools, cross-linking of data assets, integration of cost/timeliness/automation criteria into recommendations, and contributing to enterprise approaches for needs identification.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Consult and Confirm Needs
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Economist Sociologist 5' investigates client requirements for statistical information, assesses feasibility studies and project proposals, develops proposals for new studies, and recommends changes to survey content, coverage, and collection systems. The role also involves providing advisory and consultative services, often interpreting client needs and negotiating resources and approaches. Future GSBPM expectation: Stakeholder engagement will be supported by automated metadata platforms, prioritizing the assessment of existing assets. Proposals for new surveys are only advanced when clear gaps exist, and consultation cycles are expected to be rapid, iterative, and focused on reuse and transparent trade-offs. Role evolution: The role must move away from survey-centric needs identification towards facilitating evidence-driven, real-time review of existing assets, structuring trade-off dialogues, and supporting outcome-driven decision cycles. Much of the advisory and consultative activity will be anchored in collaborative asset assessment and transparent feasibility analysis. Capability implication: There will be increased emphasis on collaborative stakeholder facilitation within automated platforms, evidence-based asset assessment, rapid translation of needs into data asset reviews, and expertise in articulating outcome- and feasibility-driven recommendations.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Establish output objectives
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist plans/conducts analysis of program data, assesses feasibility/impact of new programs, and leads teams on studies/reviews that often inform or establish statistical program objectives. '[Assesses the requirement to conduct research into socio-economic trends and developments, evaluates feasibility studies and project proposals]' and '[Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans...]' connect directly to the output objective establishment process. Future GSBPM expectation: Output objectives now require up-front demonstration of digital/automation readiness, asset reuse, and explicit trade-off evaluation before launch; survey collection must be justified and tightly scoped; outputs must be interoperable and machine-actionable. Role evolution: The position will need to drive the evaluative process for output objectives to incorporate automation/readiness, digital workflow, interoperability, and resource discipline, moving from user-driven/technical feasibility toward evidence-based digital ecosystem alignment. Capability implication: Greater importance of agency data asset evaluation, digital production feasibility assessment, automation and interoperability understanding, and rigorous justification/documentation for objective-setting—alongside traditional analytical and subject-matter leadership.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Identify Concepts
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The Economist Sociologist 5 (EC-05) investigates client requirements, develops new methods for collecting, processing, and presenting statistical data, and makes recommendations for modifications to content, definitions, and conceptual frameworks (decision_making | 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the nature and scope of studies, ... modifies existing techniques or develops new methods of collecting, processing, editing, compiling and presenting statistical data.'). Responsibilities include leading teams conducting subject matter studies and representing divisions in developmental projects (leadership_and_operational_management & communication). Future GSBPM expectation: Concept identification is automated, requiring economists/sociologists to evaluate, validate, and contextualize AI-driven conceptual suggestions while arbitrating priorities and resolving conflicts among standardized assets. Role evolution: The role will focus on validation, arbitration, and negotiation, supporting rapid throughput and harmonization for digital integration, shifting away from manual ad hoc concept formulation. Capability implication: The ability to interpret and arbitrate digitally derived and machine-actionable concepts, understand enterprise metadata, and align recommendations to strategic frameworks is essential for effective performance.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Design variables
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The Economist Sociologist 5 (EC-05) plans and conducts the analysis of statistical data, improves survey methods and activities, and represents subject-matter divisions on development projects (see: 'modifies existing techniques or develops new methods of collecting, processing, editing, compiling and presenting statistical data… develops proposals for further study and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes'). They provide consultative services and manage subject-matter studies. Future GSBPM expectation: Variable definitions must be standardized, registered and designed for programmatic discovery and automated integration. New emphasis will be placed on stewardship and participative improvement of enterprise variable libraries. Role evolution: Their work will become more consultative around variable stewardship and metadata enrichment, supporting the integration of standardized and machine-actionable variable frameworks into survey improvements and development projects. Capability implication: They will need enhanced knowledge of standards-based variable registry management, metadata enrichment practices, and interoperability frameworks for cross-program variable reuse and automation compatibility.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Design frame and sample
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 is engaged in analysis of data, method improvement, client requirement assessment, and feedback on data collection, processing, and survey methods ('Develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes...'). The move to AI-automated, metadata-driven sample/frame design and prioritization of alternative sources requires this role to evolve from hands-on design to overseeing automated pipelines and focusing on ambiguous cases and exceptions. The role will be increasingly tasked with specifying requirements for automated sampling, interpreting automated decisions, validating the suitability of administrative data, and advising on improvements to metadata/automated design logic. Capability implication is increased need for integration expertise, knowledge of metadata standards, and overseeing/interpreting automated decision outputs for frame/sample selection.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Economist Sociologist 5' represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, leads project teams for special studies, provides recommendations for improvements to collection methods and survey content, and develops proposals for modifications to survey instruments, systems, and processes. Evidence: 'Develops proposals for further study and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes...' Future GSBPM expectation: The role will need to adapt from manually recommending and developing survey and collection instrument modifications to configuring, validating, and governing AI-enabled, modular platforms that automate instrument creation and prioritize reuse and data extraction over custom surveys. Role evolution: The focus will shift to platform configuration, ensuring compliance with modularity and metadata standards, and managing automated instrument pipelines; manual design and editing will be replaced by system oversight and digital governance. Capability implication: Knowledge of platform configuration, metadata-driven automation, AI-enabled dynamic instrument generation, digital compliance, and interoperability will become critical.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 is responsible for planning and conducting statistical analysis, leading teams involved in subject-matter studies, representing divisions in development projects, and modifying or developing techniques for data collection and processing. They influence system improvements through 'Makes recommendations for improvements to established survey methods and activities' and 'Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees.' Future GSBPM expectation: System and process improvements, development work, and team projects are executed in modular, automated, enterprise-standard environments with reusable components assembled by program staff using toolkits, moving away from manual coding and custom ad hoc solutions. Rigor in auditability, security, role-based access, and reproducibility is compulsory. Role evolution: The incumbent must adjust from promoting and implementing unique, custom technical solutions to validating and configuring modular components, focusing on attestation, governance, orchestration, and integration within automated frameworks. Expertise now also means selecting and assembling from a toolkit, ensuring compliance and auditability, and promoting reuse rather than recreating solutions. Capability implication: Increased importance of understanding orchestrated workflows, modular architecture, attestation and governance requirements, automated validation and reproducibility protocols, and setting standards for component use across programs and projects.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Test statistical business process
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 oversees the analysis of statistical program data, provides feedback and recommendations for improvements to established survey methods, and develops new methods and approaches. The role includes leading teams, developing proposals for study, modifying techniques, assessing feasibility, and reviewing techniques for 'testing' purposes ("reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs"). Future GSBPM expectation: The future 'Test statistical business process' phase will expand beyond informal assessment and feedback into controlled, scenario-based testing prior to deployment. Testing will be more closely integrated with risk management and quality assurance, requiring structured protocols and documentation. Role evolution: The EC-05 will be expected to actively participate in formal testing cycles, define test objectives, select test scenarios, interpret results with statistical rigor, and make systematic recommendations for final process improvements before operationalization. Capability implication: This increases the importance of knowledge relating to test methodologies (statistical and operational), the use of test environments or sandboxes, risk-based evaluation, and the ability to synthesize test outcomes for process certification and readiness.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Create frame and select sample
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 position undertakes planning and analysis related to statistical program data, reviews and modifies existing techniques, and recommends changes and improvements to survey methods, content, and coverage (“Reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs ... reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs”). In the automated, AI-driven future state for GSBPM 4.1, this role must adapt from directly involved sample design to monitoring and assessing the output quality of automated frame/sample modules, participating in quality assurance and exception evaluation, and contributing to the continuous improvement of automated sampling methods. The position will need to expand capabilities in auditing automated process flows, evaluating the use and integration of auxiliary and administrative data for frame refinement, and interpreting algorithmic outputs for sample and frame quality.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Classify and code
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 plans and conducts analysis, provides feedback and recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities, including collection and processing (which covers coding and classification), leads teams, and represents subject-matter divisions on development projects. This role frequently modifies, enhances, or supervises coding routines and assists with resolving data inconsistencies or operational bottlenecks that stem from manual coding procedures. Future GSBPM expectation: With the transition to modular, AI-enabled, automated coding pipelines, manual coding is dramatically reduced, and focus shifts to oversight, exception management, model validation, and updating classifications and coding schemes on an ongoing basis, as well as contributing to organizational resilience and consistency in coding. Role evolution: The Economist Sociologist 5 must emphasize monitoring, exception handling, pipeline performance, updating classification standards, and validating AI outputs, rather than intervening in manual coding or advising on routine procedures. Oversight of automated systems and stewardship of centralized classification schemes is required, plus involvement in continuous improvement and feedback for pipeline enhancements. Capability implication: Knowledge of AI-driven coding systems, scalable and auditable pipeline protocols, exception resolution frameworks, and feedback loops for classification evolution become paramount, in addition to robust subject-matter expertise for rare manual interventions and updating scheme logic.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Edit and impute
Economist Sociologist 5.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 actively modifies editing techniques and develops new methods for editing, compiling, and presenting statistical data, including revising approaches based on study requirements and leading teams focused on operational improvements. They are involved in feedback and recommendations for improvements to established survey methods and activities, including editing procedures, handling inconsistencies in collection, processing, and editing.

Future GSBPM expectation: As manual interventions are drastically minimized, edit and impute activities require oversight of automated algorithms, exception management, and procedural governance, as opposed to designing incremental manual improvements. The EC-05 will oversee refinement of AI-enabled processes and ensure edit/impute methods are standardized, reproducible, and auditable.

Role evolution: This role will pivot from hands-on improvement of editing techniques to the governance and validation of modular, automated edit/impute pipelines, refining AI processes based on empirical outputs, and handling rare exceptions. Leadership will involve managing operational teams in system configuration, audit, and review, rather than continual manual editing process improvement.

Capability implication: The role will now prioritize capabilities in algorithmic assessment, risk-based exception management, audit trail interpretation, and performance evaluation of automated systems, with an increased emphasis on reproducibility and compliance in edit/impute activities.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Calculate aggregates
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: This position plans and conducts analysis involving statistical program data, often writes and edits analytical material, investigates client requirements, modifies or develops new methods for collecting, processing, editing, compiling, and presenting statistical data, and leads project teams involved in subject matter studies. Tasks include modifying techniques and approaches, interpreting results, and recommending improvements to survey methods. Future GSBPM expectation: The hands-on aspect of aggregation shifts to automated, standardized components, substantially reducing the need for bespoke aggregation scripts and custom methods. The role’s focus will move toward configuring and validating aggregation logic via standardized microservices and ensuring that exceptions, unique domain needs, and edge cases are managed through pipeline configuration and governance procedures. Role evolution: The incumbent will transition from direct implementation and modification of aggregation approaches to oversight of automated aggregation pipelines, ensuring results meet analytical and quality requirements, supporting exceptions via configuration mechanisms, and contributing to auditability and reproducibility standards. Capability implication: Priority moves to understanding modular pipeline orchestration, metadata-driven audit trails, automated quality frameworks, and the interpretive skills needed to explain aggregation outcomes generated by automated systems.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Prepare draft outputs
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 'plans and conducts the analysis of statistical program data; writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' as well as leading project teams and providing advisory and consultative services. The role includes hands-on output assembly and manipulation, generation of analytical tables and notes, and direct contributions to draft publications. Future GSBPM expectation: Automated pipelines will handle most output assembling, making the manual drafting and editing less central to daily activities. Role evolution: This position will need to focus more on reviewing, interpreting, and contextualizing automated outputs, overseeing exceptions, and managing the interface between human oversight and system-generated products. Capability implication: Advanced knowledge of reviewing AI-generated tables and dashboards, output validation, and contextualizing analytical results within a highly automated production environment will be required.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Interpret and explain outputs
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 plans and conducts analysis of statistical program data, writes and edits analytical material, provides advisory services, leads teams in subject-matter studies, and interprets study results to assess relevancy and impact ("Interprets study results, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions"). Future GSBPM expectation: The role will shift from technical analysis to deep interpretation and communication of automated outputs, focusing on narrative-building, explanation for decision makers, and oversight of output quality and methodological limits. Role evolution: The EC-05 analyst must build domain-specific narratives, assess societal and policy implications of findings, and ensure transparency and ethical stewardship for outputs produced by automated pipelines. Capability implication: Increased importance of contextual interpretation, explanation of quality and fairness boundaries of automated methods, and understanding of AI-generated analytical frameworks.

Economist Sociologist 5.title: Conduct evaluation
Economist Sociologist 5.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Economist Sociologist 5' plays a major role in planning and conducting data analysis, making recommendations for improvements to established methods, providing consultative services (often based on retrospective, manual studies), and leading projects to review or modify methodological and operational processes. A core function is to write and present study results and recommendations, often as detailed reports following manual investigation and post-hoc review. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state shifts the basis of evaluation away from periodic, human-led review and toward system-generated, real-time monitoring embedded throughout the pipeline. Evaluators interpret automated alerts and performance benchmarks, prioritize recommended interventions, and support the logging and tracking of iterative change implementations. Documentation moves from narrative reports to standardized resolutions and dashboard updates. Role evolution: This position will need to engage consistently with automated quality and performance monitoring tools, synthesize and act on the outputs of dashboards, and pivot from issuing lengthy reports to integrating evaluation recommendations directly into workflow and system update cycles. Collaboration shifts toward rapid, cross-functional intervention that leverages codified performance evidence for modular change. Capability implication: This necessitates confidence in analyzing and explaining algorithm-generated alerts, understanding dashboard logic and event triggers, and operationalizing recommendations through digital workflows and standardized follow-up—while remaining trusted as a subject matter authority for interpreting when and how to escalate issues for process adjustment.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Identify needs
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter plans, develops, and directs analysis, determines changes in statistical needs of clients, assesses impact, develops options/strategies to manage issues, and investigates client requirements for statistical information and capacity of existing programs ('Determines changes in the statistical needs of clients; assesses the impact on divisional programs; develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations'). Future GSBPM expectation: Needs identification is now a digitally enabled, cross-program, solution-first process, anchored by standard cost-benefit/risk/resource and automation triage, and requires operationalization of digital/AI readiness. Role evolution: The Unit Head must transition from periodic/ad hoc review of needs to continuous, digitally enabled scanning, implement processes for formalized enterprise evaluation, and supervise staff who document and defend business cases for any proposed new collection. Stakeholder engagement and feasibility analysis are embedded earlier in the workflow. Capability implication: Proficiency in digital platforms for data asset discovery, understanding and integrating operational feasibility, automation compatibility, and cross-program resource optimization into needs identification, and leadership in shaping team approaches to digital, enterprise-wide prioritization.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Consult and Confirm Needs
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Unit Head, Subject Matter' assesses client department policies and programs to determine requirements for statistical information, develops strategies to manage complex issues, and provides expert advisory and consultative services. The role is responsible for 'investigating client requirements for statistical information and determining the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements,' as well as developing options, strategies, and recommendations for new or modified data sources. Future GSBPM expectation: Needs confirmation will be rapidly and collaboratively conducted using data discovery platforms and metadata tools, focusing intensively on repurposing existing assets and only recommending new collection when clear gaps persist. Outcome-driven and transparent criteria, including cost-benefit and resource alignment, are central. Role evolution: The Unit Head must move from traditional, exploratory consultations toward more structured, rapid iterations anchored in asset-based reviews. The role will require leading teams in evidence-based decision-making, facilitating stakeholder dialogues focused on reuse and clear trade-off discussions, and aligning recommendations with agency prioritization criteria. Capability implication: Essential capabilities will shift toward real-time data asset evaluation, platform navigation, agile stakeholder engagement, transparent feasibility assessment, and advanced articulation of trade-offs and prioritization logic.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Establish output objectives
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter is centrally involved in defining objectives and content of studies, determining standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques for development and analysis (see: '[Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed...]'). They also assess policies and client departmental needs to determine requirements, and recommend studies for approval ('[Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information and recommends, for approval, those studies that should be conducted.]'). Collaborative activities include representing subject-matter divisions on development projects from inception. Future GSBPM expectation: Establishing output objectives must now prioritize automation, interoperability, and re-use of internal/alternative data assets, with up-front trade-off discipline and documented justification for any manual/survey-based solutions. Objectives are not only user-driven; they must align with agency-wide digital execution and minimize respondent burden. Role evolution: This position will need to shift from primarily translating user/statistical needs into study objectives, to proactively evaluating program objectives against a new set of digital, automation, and inter-program reuse criteria. They will need to demonstrate automation-readiness, evidence-based value for any survey interventions, lead cross-functional collaboration (IT/project automation) from the outset, and more formally document feasibility and justification. Capability implication: The role will increasingly require capabilities in enterprise data asset evaluation, digital workflow integration, automation feasibility, interoperability standards, and cost/benefit evaluation within digital guardrails, in addition to subject-matter expertise.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Identify Concepts
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The Unit Head, Subject Matter (EC-06) defines the objectives and content of studies, determines standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied, and develops enhancements or recommends modifications to the program content, coverage and operational procedures (decision_making | 'Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied...'). They also provide expert advisory services on survey concepts, participate in cross-departmental committees, and manage integration of concepts across programs (leadership_and_operational_management & communication). Future GSBPM expectation: With concept identification becoming machine-suggested and metadata-driven, the Unit Head will need to arbitrate, validate, and justify exceptions, ensuring digital interoperability and harmonization across multiple programs. Human input will focus on negotiating priorities and context for AI-selected concepts. Role evolution: The Unit Head becomes a chief arbiter and validator of machine-derived concepts—negotiating alignment among programs, resolving conflicts, and representing the divisional perspective in enterprise-wide harmonization, rather than ground-up manual concept development. Capability implication: Advanced contextual understanding of metadata, interoperability practices, and cross-program enterprise standards, combined with the ability to interpret AI-driven suggestions within sectoral and organizational priorities, are increasingly central.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Check data availability and suitability
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Unit Head, Subject Matter' investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet needs, and develops enhancements and recommends modifications to program content, coverage, and operational procedures including new or modified data sources. They also manage project teams and represent subject-matter divisions in development projects and committees. Future GSBPM expectation: The automated suitability assessment and prioritization of existing and administrative/alternative data sources means Unit Heads must oversee the process of vetting outputs from technology-assisted platforms and focus on strategic oversight, risk evaluation, and negotiation for external data partnerships, rather than hands-on source canvassing. Survey proposals need clear, evidence-based justification validated by automated tools and partnership outcomes. Role evolution: The Unit Head evolves into a strategic manager who interprets results from automated suitability systems, manages legal and ethical vetting, and coordinates multi-stakeholder partnership negotiations for data access. Their team’s operational focus shifts to ecosystem management (metadata curation, partnership maintenance) and oversight of complex decision points, rather than repetitive manual research and assessment. Capability implication: Expertise in metadata standards, automated suitability assessment rules and processes, and partnership/relationship management will be increasingly essential. Understanding the new evidence thresholds for survey initiation and leading teams to collaborate with legal, privacy, and technical specialists is required.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Prepare and submit business case
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter directs analysis and review, develops options and strategies to manage complex multi-stakeholder relations, and represents divisions on development projects. The work description includes, 'Develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations' and 'Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques...' Future GSBPM expectation: The business case formulation requires multidisciplinary collaboration, explicit documentation of automation-first and data reuse options, and evidence-based trade-off assessments. Role evolution: The Unit Head must evolve from focusing on traditional subject-matter expertise to facilitating collaborative business case development that emphasizes automation and empirically justified modular solutions, ensuring rapid, strategic alignment with enterprise platforms. Capability implication: Increased importance on knowledge of automation, AI opportunities, transparent cost-benefit and risk analyses, and the ability to align recommendations with enterprise roadmap and strategic priorities.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter, manages and coordinates analysis, review and presentation of program results, 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes,' and leads multi-disciplinary teams for dissemination, advises data users, and manages dissemination activities. The role also includes representing subject-matter divisions on committees and overseeing projects related to dissemination and output specification. Future GSBPM expectation: Unit Heads must drive transformation from static, human-oriented dissemination to standardized, machine-actionable, metadata-driven outputs integrated in automated pipelines and available through APIs and open formats. They will need to collaborate deeply with IT and metadata teams, embed new output models and confidentiality controls, and manage modular dissemination frameworks that anticipate scalable user and AI consumption. Role evolution: The Unit Head's responsibilities expand to include the stewardship and evolution of dissemination protocols, integration of standard output templates and metadata schemas, and operational coordination of platform-based dissemination assets alongside traditional analytical material oversight. Capability implication: Critical capability shifts towards metadata design and governance, automated dissemination process alignment, platform and protocol specification, and managing confidentiality, access rights, and quality in automated distribution contexts.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Design variables
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The Unit Head, Subject Matter (EC-06) plans, develops, and directs the analysis, coordinates the development and processing of statistical data, and initiates enhancements to data sources, concepts, methods, and definitions (see: 'develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied'). They set standards, data concepts, and definitions for studies, and ensure compatibility and integrity across programs. Future GSBPM expectation: The new operating context requires variable definitions and standards to be machine-actionable, interoperable, and maintained in shared registries, structured for cross-domain reuse and automated integration. Role evolution: The Unit Head will have to integrate variable standardization and metadata-driven management into unit operations, moving away from bespoke, siloed definitions. They will contribute to the governance and enrichment of variable libraries, facilitate cross-program interoperability, and enable automated pipelines. Capability implication: They will need advanced capability in collaborative variable stewardship, interoperability and metadata management, and a strategic view of enterprise-wide data structures, variable versioning, and automation implications.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Design collection
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: The 'Unit Head, Subject Matter (EC-06)' is charged with defining objectives, content, and methods for studies and programs, including recommending changes to operational procedures and developing options for new data sources ('Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach...Develops enhancements and recommends modifications...such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions...'). The future-state GSBPM sub-process for 'Design collection' requires that these activities shift from individualized, manual survey design to configuring automated, standardized, and modular systems that default to non-survey sources and leverage interoperable, metadata-driven tools. The Unit Head must now evaluate and oversee collection strategies that incorporate AI automation, real-time instrument generation, and extend their review and approval processes to validation of AI outputs and monitoring compliance/ethical standards embedded in automated designs. Their decision space expands to a system-level stewardship of collection frameworks, with a significant responsibility for curating reusable components, question banks, and APIs, while ensuring procedural transparency and auditability. Therefore, capabilities in metadata management, AI/automation supervision, and strategic oversight of system-level collection architecture become increasingly central, moving beyond traditional instrument design and project-by-project approaches.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Design frame and sample
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter supervises teams developing methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, and extend divisional statistics, regularly adapts concepts, methods, data sources, and frameworks, and consults widely on program design ('Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies... develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.'). The future-state GSBPM workflow necessitates a strategic role in directing modular, automated, AI-driven design pipelines and ensuring that new and existing data sources (especially administrative/alternative) are fit for automated sample design. Responsibilities will shift towards defining requirements and standards for metadata and inputs, validating AI-generated designs, and resolving complex or ambiguous issues that automated systems escalate. Capability implication is deeper knowledge in metadata-driven modular design, AI pipeline oversight, cross-domain data integration, and quality assurance of automated sample/frame creation.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Design processing and analysis
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Unit Head, Subject Matter' EC-06 plans, develops, and directs the analysis, review, and presentation of program results, coordinates and reviews processing and analysis, and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present, and extend divisional statistics. They assess changes in client needs, develop options and strategies for complex issues, and represent subject-matter divisions on development projects and task forces (e.g., “Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics”). Future GSBPM expectation: The design phase will require that all new methods, procedures, and analysis routines be modular, standardized, metadata-driven, and easily integrable into AI-enabled, automated pipelines with embedded validation, audit, and disclosure controls. Ad hoc, program-specific designs will be replaced by systematized, machine-actionable workflows, demanding that design choices anticipate automation, reuse, and cross-domain interoperability. Role evolution: The Unit Head will have to transition from orchestrating traditional development and analysis activities toward leading teams that design modular, system-ready routines and templates, prioritizing automation, version-control, and FAIR principles as core design criteria. Their decision-making will increasingly involve configuring reusable, automation-enabled components and validation logic that interact seamlessly across divisions and programs. Capability implication: They will need advanced knowledge of system design, modular workflow configuration, metadata-driven specification, and automated orchestration of processes; deep expertise in embedding privacy/disclosure controls and auditability within system specifications will become central to their leadership and advisory contributions.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Unit Head, Subject Matter' leads analysis, review, and presentation of statistical program results, coordinates and reviews the development, processing, and analysis of statistical data, as well as manages teams responsible for studies and statistical program development. This includes developing new methods and enhancements that impact collection methods, defining standards and techniques for studies, and representing divisions in development projects. Evidence: 'Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of studies...' Future GSBPM expectation: The future state reframes instrument creation as configuring modular, metadata-driven, AI-enabled platforms, greatly reducing manual assembly and bespoke instrument design. The Unit Head will increasingly need to manage teams that leverage self-service, low-code/no-code environments for instrument creation, focusing on platform configuration, validation, and governance, rather than manual design. Role evolution: The role shifts from hands-on development of survey instruments to overseeing the configuration of automated collection platforms, ensuring modularity, interoperability, and alignment to enterprise metadata and paradata capture standards. Decision-making will focus on digital guardrails and governance of decentralized instrument development. Capability implication: Knowledge of advanced platform configuration, digital governance, enterprise metadata management, and AI-driven instrument design become critical, as well as a heightened understanding of automation, compliance, and platform interoperability.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter is accountable for coordinating, reviewing, and developing statistical methods and operational procedures, often leading cross-functional teams in developing, modifying, and implementing new data sources, methods, or operational frameworks. Evidence includes 'Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics,' and 'Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects.' Future GSBPM expectation: All method development and operational change occurs within pre-existing modular, automated, and reproducible platforms, assembled and attested by both IT and subject-matter staff. Enhanced governance and auditability, rapid scale-out, and democratization of development are required. Role evolution: The Unit Head must shift from managing bespoke method or system development toward orchestrating, configuring and validating modular components that are interoperable, auditable and reproducible. Managing teams that now curate and assemble workflows in standardized platforms (rather than hand-crafting solutions), and enforcing governance protocols for automation and auditability are key. Capability implication: Knowledge of orchestration, end-to-end automated workflow configuration, component attestation, governance and audit controls, version management, and reproducibility standards become far more central. Familiarity with low-code/no-code platforms and democratized component assembly is important to manage evolving teams.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Unit Head, Subject Matter' plans, develops, and directs analysis, review, and presentation of program results. The role coordinates and reviews development, processing, analysis, marketing, and dissemination of statistical data and supervises the operation of a unit engaged in these activities ('Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data; prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.').
Future GSBPM expectation: Dissemination must be handled with modular, standardized, reusable components based on corporate platforms and strict guardrails. Outputs must be automation-ready, AI-consumable, and rapidly published for both human and machine users, requiring re-engineering and new quality oversight of dissemination approach.
Role evolution: The Unit Head must transition project and operational management toward configuring and validating dissemination components using enterprise toolkits. The focus moves from bespoke development to compliance, interoperability, and automation within the corporate ecosystem. The Unit Head must ensure teams are equipped to use low/no-code tools, metadata standards, and machine-actionable formats.
Capability implication: Understanding of modular dissemination, corporate platform architectures, metadata governance, and automation pipelines becomes pivotal. Capability to manage transition, validate outputs, and assure interoperability and machine-consumable formats is required.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Configure workflows
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The Unit Head, Subject Matter (EC-06) coordinates, reviews, and manages the development, processing, and analysis of statistical data, prepares operational plans, manages project teams, and represents divisions on development projects and committees. These responsibilities include evaluating operational procedures, systems, and processes, as well as proposing modifications and enhancements—suggesting involvement in how workflows underpin statistical production. Evidence: 'Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.' and 'Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees.' Future GSBPM expectation: The configuration of workflows moves from manual, bespoke assembly and process step management to a discipline involving standardized, modular, automated, and auditable pipelines, using orchestration platforms. This introduces new expectations for operational transparency, automation, version control, guardrails, and delineation between business and IT roles—business lines will be empowered to configure and adapt workflows directly. Role evolution: The unit head will need to transition from managing bespoke operational process changes to engaging with enterprise workflow platforms and practices, including adapting business requirements for modular, automated pipeline configuration, ensuring reproducibility, auditability, and compliance. Their leadership of project teams and operational management activities will involve supporting the adoption of self-service orchestration tools and new workflow standards, driving operational change management, and ensuring business staff are equipped to use low-code/no-code platforms within enterprise guardrails. Capability implication: Their success will increasingly depend on deep operational knowledge of enterprise-level orchestration, automation concepts, modular architecture, and workflow governance—understanding how to embed statistical requirements in standardized, automatable workflows, manage versioning and attestation processes, and work collaboratively with IT and business roles to drive transformation.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Test production systems
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: The Unit Head, Subject Matter (EC-06) is responsible for planning, developing, and directing analysis and review of program results, representing subject-matter divisions on development projects, and leading project teams in multi-sectoral and inter-departmental files ("Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics"; "Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees"). In the past, this included oversight of program review and potentially ad hoc examination of system changes. Given the GSBPM future expectation of standardized automated testing across all production systems, the Unit Head’s responsibilities will shift toward ensuring that automated, continuous testing, compliance, reproducibility, and attestation processes are embedded in their program teams' operations. They must evolve from ad hoc sign-off to governing operationalization of test protocols, actively manage cross-domain impacts and compliance requirements, and lead teams in attestation-based approvals, while documenting testing evidence as part of reporting to senior management and stakeholders. Understanding enterprise testing frameworks, audit/readiness attestation, security/compliance monitoring, and reproducibility protocols become core knowledge areas.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Test statistical business process
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter plans, develops, coordinates analysis and review of program results, manages studies including the development of new methods, and explicitly "reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption." The position manages a unit supervising multidisciplinary teams to enhance content and direction of studies and takes responsibility for recommendations regarding changes in operational procedures, methods, and concept definitions. Future GSBPM expectation: The formalization of 'Test statistical business process' will place greater emphasis on structured, pre-operational testing of business processes and validation of methods before broad deployment. This will require management to ensure that testing regimes are comprehensive, documented, and integrated in project workflow, and that test results are evaluated for organizational decision-making. Role evolution: The Unit Head, Subject Matter will need to oversee and coordinate formal test plans, evaluate compliance with testing standards, synthesize outcomes, and make recommendations on the basis of evidence generated from systematic testing. The role will also require facilitating continuous improvement cycles and ensuring rigorous documentation of testing activities. Capability implication: Increased importance will be placed on understanding testing standards and frameworks, organizing test environments, interpreting multi-stage test results, and integrating feedback loops from testing outcomes into program management.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Finalise production systems
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: The Unit Head, Subject Matter (EC-06, 900-216) supervises multi-disciplinary project teams, directs analysis and review of program results, manages operational procedures, and leads enhancements to program content and operational systems. Evidence for current responsibility includes 'Supervises a unit and multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for significant multi-sectoral and inter-departmental files/issues; manages the financial resources attached to each statistical program,' and 'Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.' The future expectation that system finalization becomes a collaborative, ongoing process requiring operational monitoring, role-based enablement, and adherence to modular, automated pipelines directly affects this position, requiring it to ensure the seamless integration of new AI-enabled systems and compliance with digital guardrails, security, and FAIR standards. The role will shift toward overseeing operationalization of production systems, managing their adaptability, ongoing monitoring, and user enablement, with heightened importance placed on capabilities around operational compliance, modular system design, and documentation for broader user cohorts.

Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Create frame and select sample
Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification: The EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter position currently holds responsibilities for planning, managing, and coordinating economic, financial, and/or socio-economic studies, including the development of new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend divisional statistics (“develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics”). Further, the role supervises teams in the development of program content, coverage, and operational procedures, and investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines if existing and modified program activities can meet these requirements. In the future GSBPM 4.1 context, frame creation and sample selection will shift to being highly automated and conditional, leveraging administrative and alternative data, with survey sampling minimized. The Unit Head will increasingly focus on overseeing and refining system-driven sampling operations, monitoring automated workflows for exceptions, and contributing to methodological innovation in how data sources are fused. Their role must evolve from hands-on, manual sample design and execution to providing governance and oversight, ensuring traceability, auditability, and evaluating the performance of AI-driven sampling systems.
