Chief.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-07 'Chief' position is accountable for managing sections and project teams that plan, review, and evaluate statistical programs and methods, often via comprehensive post-hoc analyses and reporting, to improve program quality and efficiency. The Chief establishes the framework for ongoing evaluation, reviews program results, and manages changes based on periodic review findings. Future GSBPM expectation: The paradigm for evaluation shifts from cyclical review and report-based feedback to responsive, ongoing interpretation of automated dashboards and continuous system metrics. Recommendations arise directly from system-tracked events, and management emphasizes producing log-based, modular change records. Role evolution: The Chief must now embed real-time performance oversight in section operations, direct the triage of system-generated evaluation outputs, and ensure that recommendations and their follow-up are codified and tracked. The management of program quality now focuses on steering teams in rapid, event-based course corrections versus traditional, annual/biennial review cycles. Capability implication: Profound understanding of diagnostic dashboards, event- and metric-driven workflow triggers, and the application of modular interventions becomes central. The Chief must synthesize technical insights from performance monitoring and ensure accountability for continuous, transparent follow-up on system-generated recommendations.

Chief.title: Agree an action plan
Chief.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-07 Chief manages a section or multidisciplinary teams involved in statistical program operations. The role is responsible for 'planning and implementing long-term strategies', 'managing complex studies', and 'initiating changes and implementing new systems and processes' (1. Decision making). Chiefs also 'manage the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts', set priorities and milestones, and are accountable for ensuring quality and program relevance—implicitly including developing and acting on recommendations and action plans resulting from evaluations. 

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state emphasizes the need for action plans that are integrated within automated, modular, and rapidly evolving statistical services. Developing plans must be rapid, transparent, and have explicit, ongoing mechanisms for accountability and monitoring, informed by real-time feedback and digital tools. Agile, distributed governance and systematized impact tracking replaces infrequent committee-based decision making. 

Role evolution: Chiefs will need to transition from periodically directing action based on reviews to facilitating the rapid development, operationalization, and digital tracking of action plans. They will need to structure processes to ensure continuous monitoring and iterative adjustment of action plans, facilitate distributed decision-making and accountability (e.g., assignment via platforms/dashboards), and ensure action plans are directly aligned with automated/modular production workflows. 

Capability implication: This raises the importance of proficiency in using and interpreting digital impact dashboards, automated assignment and tracking tools, algorithmic impact monitoring, as well as the ability to lead within agile governance frameworks and structure transparent, iterative processes for plan evolution. Chiefs will need deep knowledge of enterprise statistical workflow orchestration and automated program management systems.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Identify needs
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator coordinates retrieval/editing/validation/marketing/dissemination of data, recommends improvements to methods, and participates as a subject area representative on teams and working groups ('Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data'). Future GSBPM expectation: The initial phase of needs identification now incorporates cross-program, enterprise-wide scanning of existing and alternative data assets, operational feasibility, automation/AI compatibility, and digitally enabled stakeholder engagement as criteria, with formal cost-benefit and risk triage preceding any new collection activity. Role evolution: The Coordinator would need to contribute actively to digital discovery and inventorying efforts, document justification for new collection needs, and engage in cross-functional teams to ensure automated solutions and reuse of data assets are prioritized in operational improvement proposals. Capability implication: Knowledge of enterprise data assets, digital and metadata-driven discovery platforms, ability to interpret operational feasibility and automation compatibility in the context of new data needs, and supporting digitally enabled workflows in program initiation.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is tasked with 'coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'provides custom tabulations and time-series information for ad-hoc client requests.' There is also direct involvement in implementing changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data, and frequent liaison with subject-matter specialists to develop specifications for system development and improvements. Future GSBPM expectation: With dissemination designs needing to be machine-actionable, standardized, API-accessible, and metadata-rich, these activities will shift from manual tabulation and file delivery to designing and testing automated and interoperable dissemination pipelines and protocols. Role evolution: The coordinator’s role will evolve from managing ad-hoc, manual data outputs to developing, specifying, and validating dissemination systems that can provide self-serve, automated access to data in open and machine-consumable formats. This will put greater emphasis on integrating metadata standards, managing access rules, and maintaining automated dissemination platforms rather than simply responding to individual requests. Capability implication: Greater emphasis will fall on understanding interoperability and metadata structuring, specifying API endpoints and automated system behavior, as well as ensuring outputs are aligned to FAIR principles and confidentiality policies in automated environments.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' coordinates data retrieval, editing, validation, recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures, implements changes to processing systems, and participates as a subject-matter representative or leads work groups implementing program activities. Evidence: 'Determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to retrieve, edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data.' Future GSBPM expectation: The Coordinator's involvement in enhancements and modifications to systems and applications will increasingly require configuring and validating corporate platforms for instrument creation—supporting modularity, metadata integration, and automation. Manual recommendations and system changes will be replaced by platform-based, automated workflows. Role evolution: The coordinator will become a steward for configuring, validating, and managing digital collection pipelines within self-service environments; focusing on ensuring interoperability, compliance, and paradata capture in an automated ecosystem. Capability implication: Platform stewardship, metadata-driven workflow management, paradata integration, and digital compliance become core, with less emphasis on manual system enhancements.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator coordinates, organizes, and implements enhancements to data retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination systems, and leads work groups in system development. Technical efforts include 'Implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to retrieve, edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data' and 'Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement program activities.' Future GSBPM expectation: Component enhancement and deployment become standardized and automated, focusing on modular, AI-enabled systems assembled with low-code/no-code tools. Operational capacity hinges on rapid configuration, automated validation, and robust governance. Role evolution: The Coordinator must shift from organizing ad hoc, custom enhancements toward orchestrating, validating, and attesting to the assembly and use of standardized, reusable business components within strict metadata and role-based access frameworks. Capability implication: Orchestration, attestation, validation, and governance of modular components, understanding enterprise-standard toolkits and automated platforms, and maintaining rigorous reproducibility and security protocols are key. Documentation and transparent oversight are critical.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' is directly involved in coordinating the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data. The position also recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications ('Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' and 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.'). This includes leading work groups tasked with these program activities ('Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement program activities.').
Future GSBPM expectation: The shift is toward assembling dissemination components from modular, standardized, reusable toolkits, with automation, APIs, and machine-actionable metadata as baseline requirements. Custom work is discouraged, and dissemination outputs must meet new interoperability, automation, and machine-consumption standards. Employees are expected to operate within strict guardrails and must ensure outputs are instantly usable and AI-ready.
Role evolution: The Coordinator will need to transition from managing ad-hoc, program-specific dissemination to leveraging approved, standardized corporate platforms and libraries. Responsibility shifts to configuring predefined dissemination components, using low/no-code tools where permitted, ensuring outputs meet both human and machine requirements, and validating modularity and reusability. Custom tabulations and client-requested outputs must comply with corporate platform standards and metadata requirements, reducing bespoke work.
Capability implication: The role requires greater familiarity with standardized dissemination architectures, corporate platforms, and metadata-rich design. Knowledge of version control, API-based product delivery, and automation principles becomes crucial for managing workflows and output validation. Metadata and interoperability understanding is necessary to ensure outputs are compliant and reusable.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Test production systems
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) currently coordinates and organizes retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination of data, recommends improvements to statistical methods and implements changes to processing systems ("Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications"), and participates as a subject area representative in development teams. Traditionally, system testing may be a discrete, manual activity; however, the GSBPM future state mandates embedding testing in automated, integrated workflows, including compliance and reproducibility checks. The Coordinator's role must evolve from assisting with and recommending local improvements to taking responsibility for attesting and documenting the readiness, security, and compliance of operational processes—all within enterprise continuous testing frameworks. Their activities shift to supporting integration of automated test harnesses and audit-ready results, ensuring operational steps comply with new guardrails and participating in attestation/sign-off processes. Capabilities in automated test suite management, understanding regulatory audit requirements, and operationalizing reproducibility documentation become substantially more important.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Test statistical business process
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is responsible for recommending improvements to statistical methods and procedures, implementing changes to processing systems and applications, and identifying and evaluating problems related to the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information. The role includes leading work groups, organizing testing activities, and developing or modifying statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys. Future GSBPM expectation: Testing will move from ad hoc troubleshooting towards a formal phase in the business process, requiring structured test plans, acceptance criteria, and clear documentation of results, to ensure statistical processes are validated for quality and fitness for use. Role evolution: The Coordinator will need to formalize and participate in structured testing activities, including test preparation, execution, documentation, and synthesis of outcomes for process improvement. Test-driven development and validation will become a more central activity, prior to changes being made operational. Capability implication: Increased importance on structured test protocol knowledge, process evaluation and validation methodologies, and documentation and communication skills related to test reporting and recommendations.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Finalise production systems
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03, 900-219) coordinates retrieval, validation, and dissemination of data, recommends improvements to statistical methods, and implements changes to processing systems and applications. Evidence, such as 'Implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to retrieve, edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data,' links directly to production system finalization activities. The GSBPM future state introduces operationalization of production systems through automation, modularity, continuous monitoring, and documentation for technical and business users, with compliance checks and support for self-service. This requires the Coordinator's responsibilities to expand from discrete technical implementation to ongoing operational monitoring, compliance, robust documentation, and enablement for a broad set of users. Broader capability requirements arise in automated system maintenance, digital security, modularity, real-time monitoring, and authoritative documentation for both technical and non-technical users.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Finalise collection
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03)' is responsible for coordinating and organizing activities related to the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data, recommending improvements to methods and procedures, and leading workgroups for program implementation ('Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' 'Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement program activities.'). Future GSBPM expectation: The new expectation is that data are finalized and archived in standardized, machine-actionable formats through automated pipelines, with clerical or manual operations minimized. The Coordinator's operational tasks shift from manual coordination and validation to monitoring automated workflows, flagging exceptions, and supporting continuous improvement to automation. Role evolution: Responsibilities move to monitoring pipeline health and quality metrics (paradata), troubleshooting flagged exceptions, and helping optimize metadata-driven automation rather than routine manual oversight. Capability implication: The Coordinator must become proficient in interpreting automated validation logs, exception tickets, and metadata standards, and contribute to end-to-end workflow improvement for real-time, auditable statistical production.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Classify and code
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is tasked with coordinating retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination of data—including implementing and recommending improvements to processing systems, composing custom tabulations, and advising users on subject-matter concepts, as well as participating in and leading work groups on program activities. This includes hands-on involvement and problem-solving in manual coding, editing, and validation logic and a degree of control over the process mechanics. Future GSBPM expectation: The shift to fully automated, modular, AI-enabled pipelines surrounding classification and coding means the Coordinator's direct involvement in routine coding and manual editing becomes limited, replaced by pipeline monitoring, exception resolution, and feedback roles for maintaining automated quality. Human tasks will center on managing edge cases, supporting pipeline governance, and contributing to updating classification systems. Role evolution: The Coordinator must redeploy from hands-on coding work, focusing instead on monitoring automated pipeline performance, exception handling, supporting audit routines, and collaborating in updating classification and coding standards in response to operational feedback. Capability implication: Key expertise transitions towards automated pipeline operation, monitoring AI-driven coding outputs, validation and exception management, and the contextual knowledge required to interpret and explain pipeline anomalies or model performance to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Review and validate
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) currently plays a direct role in the coordination, organization, and execution of data retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination. Quoting relevant responsibilities: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Identifies and evaluates problems related to the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations.' The future state of GSBPM 5.3 shifts validation from routine manual review to an automated, standardized, and reproducible process embedded within pipelines, meaning manual data validation will no longer be the primary work activity. Instead, staff will oversee automated validation pipelines, manage exceptions, and refine validation rules and AI/ML logic. The EC-03 role will evolve into an exception manager and process overseer, focusing on monitoring pipeline outputs, understanding complex validation failures, and collaborating on improving validation logic. This transformation increases the importance of capabilities in pipeline monitoring, understanding automated validation logs, and diagnosing automated rule failures rather than routinely examining raw data.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Edit and impute
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator coordinates and organizes data retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination, recommends improvements to statistical methods, implements changes to systems and applications, and leads work groups for program activities. The role is heavily engaged with hands-on data manipulation and process supervision.

Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030’s vision for edit and impute will replace many manual tasks with automated, AI-driven pipelines, where Coordinators’ work shifts to monitoring and validating automated system outputs, handling exceptions, and participating in the configuration and reporting of edit/impute microservices. Manual hands-on editing recedes, replaced by oversight of automated tools.

Role evolution: The EC-03 Coordinator will transition from direct data editing and process management to managing exception handling, monitoring AI-enabled edit/impute modules, and supporting the integration and operational compliance of automated routines. Participation in work groups will now involve contributing to the governance and configuration of cross-program automated systems, not the maintenance of manual solutions.

Capability implication: Domain knowledge will now favor system oversight, exception management, auditability, process traceability, and interpretation of automated edit/impute outcomes within the statistical production environment, rather than legacy manual editing skills and operational coordination.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Finalise data files
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is assigned responsibility for coordinating and organizing the retrieval, editing, validation, and dissemination of data, implementing changes to processing systems and applications, and recommending improvements ('Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' & 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.'). Future GSBPM expectation: Assembly and finalization of analysis-ready files will be executed through automated, event-driven pipelines with reduced need for manual file manipulation or custom formatting. The process relies on full auditability, traceability, and compliance with metadata standards. Role evolution: The coordinator’s work will evolve towards supporting and monitoring the automated process, validating outputs against standards, and handling exceptions, rather than performing manual tabulations or cleaning. Involvement in configuring, testing, and maintaining event-driven processing flows and ensuring process transparency will be central. Capability implication: This increases the required fluency in standardized, automated workflow operations, exception management, and understanding audit trails in version-controlled environments. The ability to translate subject-matter requirements into metadata specifications and interface efficiently with automated systems becomes increasingly important.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Prepare draft outputs
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator 'coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data' and provides custom tabulations, recommendations for improvements, and direct support for the assembly and release of statistical outputs. This position frequently participates in the hands-on drafting of statistical products as well as leading work groups for program activities. Future GSBPM expectation: Output preparation will be predominantly automated, requiring less manual intervention and greater oversight of AI-generated products. Role evolution: The coordinator will move toward overseeing and troubleshooting automated workflows, monitoring quality metrics, and dealing with exceptions where automation fails or encounters unusual cases. Capability implication: Skills in monitoring and validating outputs from AI pipelines, understanding automated production cycles, and exception handling will be increasingly integral.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Validate outputs
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 role is fundamentally involved in coordinating the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data ('Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, ... of data'). The role includes implementing changes to processing systems for manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data. Existing activities are closely tied to manual validation checks and making recommendations for improvements to validation procedures. Future GSBPM expectation: As StatCan2030 envisions AI-powered pipelines, the validation of statistical outputs will be less reliant on manual intervention and will demand oversight, monitoring, and interpretation of automated validation modules as part of routine operations. Role evolution: This role will need to focus more on managing, monitoring, and troubleshooting automated validation workflows, and interpreting or acting upon complex outputs or flags from automated systems. The day-to-day work will include designing and updating validation rules, and providing subject-matter guidance in the context of automated checks. Capability implication: Strong understanding of automated validation, statistical QA pipelines, metadata quality controls, and audit trails will become essential. Ability to interpret flagged anomalies and oversee the integrity and transparency of validation systems will be increasingly critical.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: GSBPM 6.5 Finalise Outputs
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator organizes, validates, and disseminates data, implements changes to processing systems, and coordinates detailed validation and editing workflows. The position also leads work groups implementing program activities, as evidenced by: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications,' and 'Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement program activities.' Future GSBPM expectation: Data output finalization, including validation, caveat collation, and approval documentation, will be handled by orchestrated, automated systems, and humans will intervene mainly for interpretation and strategic review of exceptional or flagged cases. Role evolution: The Coordinator will shift from managing manual editing, validation, and assembling outputs for dissemination to monitoring automated workflows, interpreting system-generated metadata, and intervening when exceptions or irregularities are flagged by the system. Capability implication: Advanced capability in auditing automated validation pipelines, interpreting automated caveats and supporting information, and understanding when and how to intervene in the automated workflow for final output signoff will become essential.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Update output systems
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' (EC-03) coordinates activities relating to retrieval, editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of statistical data, recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures, implements changes to processing systems, and provides subject matter advice. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' and 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.'

Future GSBPM expectation: Retrieval and dissemination processes will be part of an automated, metadata-driven, enterprise infrastructure. Output updates triggered by pipeline events will require minimal human intervention, with the Coordinator's role evolving toward metadata specification, monitoring for exceptions, and ensuring output compliance with central standards.

Role evolution: The Coordinator’s work will shift from direct operational manipulation and validation toward collaboration with central automation teams to specify metadata, monitor system health, and resolve exception cases. Their involvement will be less hands-on and more focused on compliance and configuration within centrally orchestrated pipelines.

Capability implication: A deeper understanding of automated dissemination pipelines, metadata specification, enterprise interoperability standards, and exception handling will become central, while traditional manual retrieval and local formatting are deprioritized.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Produce dissemination products
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator' (EC-03) is responsible for coordinating and organizing the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data, as well as providing custom tabulations and responding to ad-hoc client requests. The work description further details involvement in recommending and implementing changes to processing systems, leading work groups, and addressing issues in dissemination practices. Key evidence includes activities like 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data' and 'Identifies and evaluates problems related to ... dissemination of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state for 'Produce dissemination products' shifts this work from manual assembly and editing to orchestration of automated, AI-enabled pipelines. Employees are expected to monitor, interpret, and validate outputs rather than create them directly, focusing on continuous improvement of dissemination templates, troubleshooting exceptions, and enabling machine-actionable outputs for both human and digital users.
Role evolution: This role demands a pivot from manual and routine output production to oversight of pipeline-generated products, error diagnostics, and quality assurance, especially in edge cases where automation is insufficient. The coordinator will engage more in facilitating automation, configuring templates and rules, and contributing feedback on ecosystem improvement rather than manually assembling products.
Capability implication: Increased importance is placed on understanding automated pipeline operations, standardization and modular template logic, metadata integration for dissemination, error detection in AI-generated outputs, and oversight of rules-based production. Deep knowledge of dissemination standards (machine-actionable, reusable, interoperable), and collaborative engagement with IT and subject-matter experts becomes critical.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Release dissemination products
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03)' coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data. The work includes providing custom tabulations for client requests, identifying and evaluating problems related to dissemination, and implementing enhancements or modifications to computer systems used for data release ('coordinates and organizes the ... dissemination of data', 'determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used ... to disseminate statistical data').
Future GSBPM expectation: The release process will shift to automated, platform-based workflows where manual intervention in dissemination scheduling, monitoring, and release will diminish. Employees will increasingly oversee and govern automated pipelines, managing exceptions like embargo breaches or urgent retractions, and ensuring operational resilience and security/governance of dissemination workflows. Dissemination products will be machine-actionable as well as human-readable, requiring more digital and workflow-centric engagement.
Role evolution: The position will need to shift from hands-on coordination of dissemination mechanics to operating as an overseer of end-to-end automated dissemination platforms. Decision-making will increasingly involve monitoring dashboards, responding to system alerts, auditing release logs, and escalating rare exceptions or breaches. Solutions and recommendations will target workflow improvements, platform rules, and system security rather than case-by-case procedures.
Capability implication: Familiarity with enterprise dissemination platforms, understanding of digital workflow governance, audit trails, exception management protocols, and platform logic regarding embargoes and time-based release becomes essential. The coordinator will need to interpret and audit system-driven dissemination, and provide input on exceptions, rather than implementing manual release procedures.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Promote dissemination products
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator organizes the retrieval, validation, marketing and dissemination of data, and leads groups responsible for dissemination activities. The work involves developing and implementing improvements to statistical dissemination methods and processing systems and includes providing advice to users and participating on various teams/working groups. Future GSBPM expectation: Data dissemination promotion will be automated, digitally optimized, and machine-actionable, demanding proactive outreach and continuous engagement through digital channels and APIs. Manual processes are replaced by metadata-driven, AI-enabled systems that promote products to both human and machine users. Role evolution: The Coordinator must pivot from manual retrieval and dissemination to curating metadata for discoverability, overseeing API-driven catalog population, and continuously analyzing user engagement to optimize promotional activities. The role will contribute to omnichannel integration and ongoing quality assurance for automated outreach. Capability implication: This position grows in the direction of digital catalog management, metadata curation for automated discoverability, and pragmatic understanding of AI-driven engagement tracking and analysis.

Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.title: Provide user support (GSBPM Phase 7.5)
Data Production and Dissemination Coordi.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-03 Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator routinely provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts and participates in custom tabulations and ad-hoc client requests. Evidence is found in key activities such as 'Provides custom tabulations and time-series information for ad-hoc client requests' and 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts.' Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 transforms user support from reactive service into proactive, platform-enabled functions where data and metadata are machine-actionable, discoverable via APIs and digital tools, and the support function emphasizes empowering both human and machine users. Role evolution: The Coordinator's responsibility will shift from responding to individual queries and tabulation requests, towards maintaining and enhancing self-service platforms, curating knowledge repositories, supporting automated queries (including API and AI-based requests), and addressing advanced technical scenarios that arise from new user types. The role will need to become more involved in ensuring metadata quality, digital platform usability, and seamless integration for both human and machine consumption. Capability implication: This evolution places priority on deep understanding of metadata structures, interoperability standards, platform usage analytics, and the ability to troubleshoot and support machine-oriented query environments. Knowledge of digital user experience and interaction patterns, as well as nuanced awareness of support automation mechanisms, will become substantially more important.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Identify needs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist coordinates manipulation, storage, retrieval, consultative services, leads/supervises teams, and defines sources and approaches for special studies ('Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used'). Future GSBPM expectation: All needs identification is now expected to begin with enterprise digital scanning and triage, including cost, automation, resource, and operational feasibility, with explicit rationale documented before any new collection is pursued. Role evolution: The Specialist will need to systematically leverage digital tools/platforms to evaluate whether existing assets and automation solutions can fulfill new information requirements, prepare documentation for new collection justification, and coordinate across units to ensure solution-first approaches and auditability in project initiation. Capability implication: Understanding digital inventory/discovery platforms, ability to assess operational feasibility, automation, and reusability for new needs, and integrating enterprise resource and risk models into production and dissemination strategies.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Prepare and submit business case
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads development projects, prepares work plans and guidelines, and makes recommendations for improvements to processing systems and procedures. Phrases such as 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources,' and 'Represents subject matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees...' indicate involvement in operational business case development. Future GSBPM expectation: Business cases must demonstrate prioritization of automation, modularity, and data reuse, with rapid evidence-based options analysis and trade-offs. Role evolution: The Specialist must shift from incremental improvements and survey-focused proposals to developing business cases emphasizing automation and enterprise platform leverage, defending decisions empirically and succinctly. Capability implication: Key knowledge now includes identifying automation and AI opportunities, rapid cost/benefit assessment, and transparent articulation of risk/benefit trade-offs in business case proposals.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist oversees 'develops databases for the provision of time-series information,' 'coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data,' and 'leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' The Specialist also interacts with users and oversees project management for dissemination activities. Future GSBPM expectation: Production specialists will need to focus on designing dissemination databases and systems that are inherently interoperable, open-format, and accessible through APIs for both human and automated consumption. The role will demand developing and maintaining automated pipelines that minimize manual effort, embedding metadata and confidentiality controls, and supporting scalable, user-facing dissemination platforms. Role evolution: Responsibilities shift from managing various manual outputs and systems toward architecting, specifying, and continuously improving modular, automated dissemination solutions, participating in the design of reusable data assets and metadata schemas. Capability implication: Deep understanding of dissemination platform architectures, metadata and open data protocols, confidentiality automation, and engagement with IT for system integration and API design becomes essential.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design processing and analysis
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) develops databases, coordinates staff activities for manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, provides consultative services, represents divisions on development committees, and leads teams in development and implementation of new processing systems (“Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems. Plans, organizes and coordinates the work of a unit or project team involved in the conduct of special studies, surveys and projects”). Future GSBPM expectation: With the transition to modular, automation-enabled designs, this role will need to focus on designing and coordinating reusable, metadata-driven pipelines and workflows. Processing routine development will shift to system configuration, automation logic, and version-controlled template creation, enabling rapid integration and minimal manual intervention. Role evolution: The Specialist will need to orchestrate the team’s move from legacy, bespoke processing system development to standardized, modular configuration work for automation platforms. Decision-making around database development, processing methodologies, and quality control will require expertise in system-ready automation, auditability, and cross-domain interoperability. Capability implication: More advanced knowledge of automation logic, modular workflow and pipeline design, machine-actionable metadata systems, and template-based configuration will be necessary. The ability to embed validation and disclosure control logic in reusable, auditable system specifications will be critical.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' coordinates staff manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data; leads teams implementing new processing systems; and represents divisions in development projects. They develop guidelines for system design, evaluate and test processing systems, and manage operational projects. Evidence: 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' Future GSBPM expectation: With the shift to modular, AI-enabled, self-service platforms, the Specialist's focus moves from custom database and system development to configuring reuse-enabled platforms for automated collection instrument creation, embedding paradata and metadata requirements, and ensuring operational compliance. Role evolution: The Specialist must adapt leadership to guide teams in configuring and validating platform-driven workflows. The emphasis is on modularity, interoperability, and rapid deployment within digital guardrails, supporting decentralized, self-service instrument development. Capability implication: Essential capabilities involve enterprise platform management, metadata integration, digital compliance, and knowledge of automated testing and validation tools, alongside understanding of AI-driven design and paradata management.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems, manages teams involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data, develops databases and provides subject-matter expertise for system development. Evidence includes activities like 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems' and 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications.' Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 requires such design and development to happen within enterprise-standard modular, reusable, and automated platforms, with deep business participation and democratized development through low-code/no-code tools. Automation, orchestration, governance, and auditability are default and compulsory. Role evolution: The Specialist must evolve from managing bespoke system development toward overseeing the assembly, attestation, and governance of reusable microservice components, managing integration, security, and documentation standards, and ensuring that all development is reproducible and traceable. Capability implication: Greater emphasis on managing modular architecture, orchestrating automated flows, validating component security and auditability, and ensuring compliance with robust governance protocols is required. Understanding of business-side engagement in toolkits and low-code workflows also increases in importance.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' develops databases, coordinates staff involved in manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, and leads project teams for new or modified processing systems. The position also provides subject-matter expertise for development projects and consultative services ('Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.').
Future GSBPM expectation: Dissemination and data provision are shifting toward standardized, reusable components using pre-approved corporate tools. Output must be auditable, version controlled, metadata-rich, and ready for AI consumption. Custom approaches are replaced by configuration of modules within strict guardrails.
Role evolution: The Specialist must shift from leading bespoke system development to assembling, configuring, and validating modular dissemination components using common enterprise platforms. Coordination of staff and projects will focus on compliance with platform standards, automation, and metadata interoperability. Output design must ensure machine-friendly formats and reusability across programs.
Capability implication: A deep understanding of enterprise platforms, component configuration, metadata standards, and automation pipelines is required. Familiarity with APIs, machine-actionable output validation, and modular system integration becomes more important than traditional, custom database development.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Configure workflows
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) manages, coordinates, and leads operational teams involved in statistical processing, database development, and implementation of new or modified systems. The position defines project objectives, designs processing parameters, develops guidelines for system evaluation and testing, and negotiates technical aspects with various stakeholders. Evidence: 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' Future GSBPM expectation: The transition to automated, standardized, and modular workflow configuration, managed via self-service business platforms and orchestration engines, signals a shift in how processing flows are designed, configured, and maintained. Role evolution: The incumbent will need to move from manual configuration and custom system design toward engagement with modular, event-driven workflow orchestration, supporting business staff empowerment in workflow adaptation, and managing operational standards, auditability, and compliance. The specialist’s responsibility for project team management, processing parameter approval, and operational guidance will now focus on training/support for new tooling, maintaining operational discipline in workflow versioning and attestation, and ensuring proper implementation within enterprise-level platforms. Capability implication: The role will demand intricate knowledge of digital workflow orchestration, process automation, modular design, operational change management, and the ability to embed subject-matter needs in standardized, auditable business workflow platforms.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Test production systems
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) currently coordinates and controls activities related to manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, leads project teams in processing system development, and provides subject-matter expertise regarding the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems ("Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements"). The future GSBPM phase expects testing to be automated, standardized, and integrated into continuous deployment, moving beyond component-focused to end-to-end system validation, including regulatory, security, and compliance checks. The role must shift from overseeing mainly manual or semi-automated tests to implementing and maintaining scalable automated test harnesses for all production modules, ensuring that any new business-led developments meet enterprise-level guardrails. This requires the Specialist to direct operational testing, document reproducibility and attest to system readiness for automated approvals, expanding their focus to cross-domain impact and regulatory requirements. Enhanced importance will be placed on familiarity with automated testing frameworks, orchestration tools, and deep comprehension of security and reproducibility standards within the broader production environment.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Test statistical business process
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications, and reviews and approves detailed processing parameters including criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications. The role also chairs meetings, provides consultative services, and evaluates processing systems for effectiveness via test procedures and acceptance criteria. Future GSBPM expectation: Testing will transition from ad hoc or isolated acts into structured, iterative, and documented phases that are necessary for process validation before operational release, involving broader participation of quality assurance and risk analysis. Role evolution: The Specialist will be expected to design, execute, and document formal test plans for processing systems, organize test teams, evaluate system behavior under test conditions, and synthesize outcomes for final approval and process improvement. This includes establishing and applying acceptance criteria and reporting in a way that links test results directly to readiness decisions and risk mitigation. Capability implication: Increased importance will be placed on process test design, knowledge of formal quality assurance testing protocols, operational risk analysis, and communicating test outcomes to stakeholders and decision-makers.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise production systems
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05, 900-221) leads the development and implementation of statistical processing systems, manages teams, and defines processing guidelines, focusing on manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data. Evidence includes 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' and 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters.' The future GSBPM implications mean finalization involves not only deployment but active operationalization of AI-powered, automated, and role-based pipelines, including ongoing monitoring, compliance attestation, and ensuring systems are self-service and FAIR-compliant. The role will evolve to balance traditional system deployment with enabling rapid updates, modular adaptation, and supporting a wider user community through robust documentation and training. Capabilities will shift toward expertise in modular system design, automation strategies, digital guardrails and security, and interdisciplinary communication supporting both technical and business users.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Set up collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) develops databases, leads teams managing the storage and retrieval of statistical data, provides subject-matter expertise, and develops guidelines for design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems. They are involved in negotiating operational processes, planning and organizing statistical projects, coordination, and deployment of new or modified systems. Future GSBPM expectation: Automated systems and platforms take over most set-up activities including instrument deployment and onboarding of data sources, requiring staff to focus on oversight, exception handling, and validation of automated logic. Role evolution: The Production and Dissemination Specialist will transition from direct system configuration and manual deployment to monitoring and validating automated set-up routines, participating in managing exceptions, and approving system logic. Their teams will focus more on risk, quality, and secure integration of new data sources rather than repetitive system preparation. Capability implication: Understanding of automated platform logic, system interoperability, exception management frameworks, and the governance of modular, rapid deployment solutions become fundamental to their oversight and coordination efforts.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Run collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) leads teams in the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical data, plans and organizes operational activities, and supports survey collection and operational processes (including planning, development, coordination, technical support, and data collection). The role also 'reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs, assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data.'
Future GSBPM expectation: With 'Run collection' shifting to automated, multi-source data acquisition, the role must manage and operate business process automation platforms, coordinate API-driven and digital collection streams, continuously monitor real-time dashboard metrics, and handle rare cases requiring manual intervention or escalation.
Role evolution: Day-to-day responsibilities will shift from overseeing manual collection methods and operational support to managing and optimizing digital collection pipelines, integrating administrative or alternative sources, troubleshooting system failures, and facilitating live dashboard-driven process adjustments. The specialist becomes responsible for orchestrating automated workflows, participating in digital data negotiations, and handling quality escalation for exception cases, rather than transactional survey logistics.
Capability implication: Familiarity with data pipeline orchestration, digital platform integration, real-time metrics, automated exception resolution, and the operational mechanics of AI-enabled collection tools becomes increasingly relevant.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05)' coordinates staff manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, leads teams in developing new or modified processing systems, and develops guidelines for system evaluation and improvement. ('Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.' 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'). Future GSBPM expectation: The transition to automated, metadata-driven collection finalization means the specialist will oversee automated workflows, manage version control, and ensure seamless, auditable transitions between data collection and downstream processes. Manual intervention is restricted to troubleshooting edge cases and refining pipeline logic. Role evolution: The role shifts toward managing automation and exception handling, ensuring that new guidelines, procedures, and system enhancements target auditable, scalable pipeline integration rather than discrete manual tasks. Capability implication: The specialist must master automated data pipeline operation, audit/monitoring frameworks, metadata governance, and exception-based issue management, focusing on enterprise systems and continuous improvement in a highly automated, privacy-centric environment.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Integrate data
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) coordinates and controls activities of staff manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data and leads teams implementing new or modified statistical processing systems. This role currently relies on managing hands-on integration and retrieval from diverse sources, including resolving compatibility of data definitions and manually handling integration tasks. The GSBPM future state shifts integration towards automated, modular pipelines governed by standardized and auditable processes, using microservices and common metadata frameworks. The Specialist would need to transition from manual database management and custom integration techniques to configuring and maintaining reusable integration modules, validating interface logic, and monitoring exception reports from automated workflows. The focus moves to governing system-level interoperability, ensuring adherence to standardized input/output requirements, and championing automation while managing exceptions. Capabilities in digital integration architecture, metadata stewardship, and platform governance become critical, together with coordinated management of exception outcomes.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Classify and code
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams engaged in coordinating, controlling, and improving statistical data manipulation, storage, retrieval, and coding systems. The role involves developing and modifying coding approaches, leading implementation of new processing systems, providing consultative expertise on methodology, and ensuring compatibility and continuity across data sources and coding schemes. Much of this is currently rooted in human judgment and routine operational oversight of manual or semi-automated coding and classification routines. Future GSBPM expectation: Classify and code will operate in AI-driven, modular, auditable pipelines, minimizing direct human intervention and manual coding. Routine clerical work shifts to pipeline oversight and governance, monitoring AI output, handling exceptions or edge cases, and maintaining/revising classification and coding standards in collaboration with central metadata managers. Role evolution: The role must transition from direct involvement in coding and system specification to stewardship and governance of automated, AI-driven pipelines, focusing on pipeline performance, exception handling, model retraining, validation activities, and maintaining organizational consistency in coding standards. Capability implication: Advanced understanding of AI-enabled coding operations, pipeline governance, audit protocols, centralized metadata management, and the technical and conceptual challenges involved in automated exception management and system validation become crucial, while pragmatic subject-matter expertise is needed for rare manual intervention and updating classification schemes.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Review and validate
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) both coordinates staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data and leads teams responsible for new or modified statistical processing systems, 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data,' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' With Review and Validate shifting to automated, modular, auditable pipelines, the Specialist’s coordination responsibilities shift from managing manual validation tasks to overseeing the implementation, monitoring, and upkeep of automated validation rules and exception-handling mechanisms. Their team management will increasingly prioritize process supervision, exception flow management, and supporting iterative improvement of validation modules and AI-model outcomes. Therefore, capabilities surrounding pipeline supervision, exception triage, and the governance and documentation of automated validation become more central.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Edit and impute
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist manages and coordinates teams involved in manipulating, storing, retrieving, and editing statistical data, including developing databases for time-series and special studies, and leading projects to implement new statistical processing systems. Activities include reviewing and approving processing parameters and devising criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies in data.

Future GSBPM expectation: With the advent of automated edit/impute modeled in StatCan2030, these manual methods and criteria must be translated into AI-enabled, auditable microservices. Operational teams become responsible for configuring, monitoring, and overseeing AI-powered edit/impute pipelines, focusing on auditability, exception handling, and cross-program standardization.

Role evolution: The EC-05 Specialist’s leadership will shift away from overseeing staff engaged in direct editing and validation to guiding teams in managing automated processing environments—monitoring AI pipeline outputs, validating rare exceptions, and ensuring traceable and auditable interventions. Project management and process improvement will be directed at designing and integrating standardized, modular pipeline components rather than traditional bespoke solutions. Their role in consultation and multidisciplinary coordination will now prioritize governance, reproducibility, and the ethical implementation of automated edit/impute systems.

Capability implication: Key knowledge areas shift toward system oversight, AI process governance, audit traceability, cross-program integration, and the capacity to critically evaluate AI/automation performance in statistical production environments rather than manual editing proficiency or routine procedural supervision.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Derive new variables and units
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) develops databases for time-series and special requests, coordinates staff for data manipulation and retrieval, and leads project teams in developing and implementing new or modified statistical processing systems. Tasks include investigating client needs, modifying techniques, and designing/evaluating processing systems, often directly handling data derivation via manual procedures. They decide on project objectives, parameters of processing and derivation, and improvements to processing approaches. Future GSBPM expectation: Derivation work will be encapsulated in automated, auditable microservices governed by metadata standards, replacing manual intervention. The specialist's focus will shift from implementing bespoke derivation systems to designing standardized transformation logic, deploying modular services, and managing compliance, exception handling, and audit requirements across integrated pipelines. Role evolution: The Specialist's responsibilities shift from hands-on system development for derivation to stewardship over modular transformation logic, cross-team collaboration on module reuse, and governance over pipeline performance and quality. Exception handling becomes a matter of tracing workflow events, and adaptation for rapid changes is managed centrally via metadata-driven deployments. Capability implication: There is a greater requirement for understanding metadata repositories, microservice architecture for statistics, and audit-focused pipeline design. The Specialist must be skilled at modular transformation logic creation, pipeline governance, cross-team module coordination, and impact analysis of upstream changes.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Calculate aggregates
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: This role develops databases, coordinates the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data, and leads project teams in the development and implementation of statistical processing systems, often involving custom aggregation techniques and processes. Key tasks include reviewing and approving processing parameters and developing criteria to ensure data continuity. Future GSBPM expectation: Processing and aggregation activities move into automated, standardized microservices, requiring specialists to configure aggregation modules, validate operational pipelines, manage exceptions, and support auditability, transparency, and reproducibility via metadata-driven processes. Manual intervention is minimized, with custom aggregation logic discouraged unless justified and formally governed. Role evolution: The Specialist must shift from manual parameter development to management and configuration of modular aggregation services, interpreting their outputs, and supporting governance processes for audit trails and exception handling. Capability implication: The knowledge base increasingly includes enterprise-level pipeline design, standardized aggregation module management, metadata-driven process controls, and expertise in automated quality monitoring and exception configuration.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise data files
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is responsible for developing databases for time-series and special studies, leading staff who manipulate, store and retrieve data, and devising criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies ('Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.' & 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'). They also develop guidelines for processing systems and approve processing parameters. Future GSBPM expectation: 'Finalise data files' will be performed via orchestrated, automated pipelines, demanding oversight of standardized, versioned, audit-ready outputs. The role will need to ensure that automated workflows deliver standardized, metadata-rich, reproducible final files and resolve exceptions, rather than manual cleaning or bespoke file formatting. Role evolution: The specialist’s activities will transition from hands-on manipulation and ad hoc problem-solving to configuring and monitoring automated data assembly systems, validating pipeline outputs, and sustaining process auditability. Exception handling and reproducibility of outputs will become day-to-day priorities. Capability implication: Expertise in pipeline configuration, metadata stewardship, automated validation, and advanced process audit and traceability will become essential, including the ability to interface with IT, governance, and analytic stakeholders around automated data delivery.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Prepare draft outputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist 'coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data,' develops databases, leads teams, and produces statistical outputs, including the preparation and review of tables and explanatory notes. These tasks involve direct technical and collaborative engagement in output preparation. Future GSBPM expectation: Automation will supplant manual output preparation, shifting responsibilities to oversight of automated pipelines, tracking output quality, performance targets, and exception handling. Role evolution: Responsibilities evolve toward managing and monitoring the operation of automated analytical pipelines, investigating anomalies, and ensuring quality, reliability, and traceability in publication-ready outputs. Capability implication: Proficiency in managing automated output generation, pipeline monitoring, performance evaluation, and quality assurance will become paramount.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Apply disclosure control
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) develops databases, coordinates staff involved in manipulating/storing/retrieving statistical data, provides consultative services on methods and results, and ensures confidentiality compliance as part of project management. The work description includes 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices ... to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.' Future GSBPM expectation: Disclosure control processes transition to automated, standardized modules within production and dissemination pipelines, with real-time audits and exception handling. Role evolution: The Specialist will need to move from manual confidentiality review and consultative support toward supporting the operation, oversight, and validation of embedded disclosure controls in database and dissemination systems, and participate in troubleshooting or escalating exceptions flagged by automated tools. Capability implication: Stronger focus on automated system monitoring, operational auditability, interpretation of AI-driven suppression logs, and collaboration with IT and data engineering counterparts to adapt disclosure mechanisms to new data workflows and formats.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: GSBPM 6.5 Finalise Outputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist coordinates staff involved in manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data and leads project teams for developing and implementing processing systems. They are responsible for reviewing and approving processing parameters and ensuring continuity and compatibility of data. This includes managing modifications for output preparation and overseeing dissemination practices, as shown by: 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' and 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications.' Future GSBPM expectation: Automated pipelines will dominate consistency checking, caveat assignment, and even release documentation, moving routine preparation to technology-enabled systems with subject matter experts focusing on exception handling and oversight. Role evolution: The Specialist's focus will shift from hands-on management of output consistency and manual dissemination workflows to oversight and auditing of automated pipeline outputs, ensuring quality and addressing exceptions where system criteria are not met. Capability implication: Integrated knowledge of auditing automated processes, understanding how system-generated caveats and metadata are assembled, and providing strategic guidance on approvals and exceptions will be increasingly significant. Familiarity with systematized provenance and release workflows powered by automation will be crucial.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Update output systems
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) develops databases for dissemination and special studies, coordinates and controls staff involved in manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, provides subject-matter expertise to users, and leads teams in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems. Evidence includes 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'

Future GSBPM expectation: Output systems will no longer be operated at the program-specific or manual level; instead, updating and dissemination activities will be automated, metadata-rich, and governed by central standards. The role at this level will focus on specifying output requirements via metadata, monitoring system health and compliance, and handling exceptions rather than direct manipulation and formatting.

Role evolution: This specialist's work would shift from platform-specific custom database development and hands-on dissemination towards collaborating with central automation teams, specifying metadata requirements for outputs, and ensuring compatibility and compliance with enterprise standards. They will need to support machine-actionable dissemination through APIs and reusable modular components and work more closely with governance and exception management processes.

Capability implication: Expertise in metadata specification, modular dissemination standards, and integration with enterprise dissemination platforms increases in importance. Understanding FAIR principles as they relate to data and metadata for both human and machine (AI) consumption and practical knowledge of API-based publication becomes crucial, alongside the ability to monitor and resolve system exceptions, rather than manual formatting or creation of ad hoc outputs.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Produce dissemination products
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) is tasked with developing databases for time-series and custom requests, coordinating activities for manipulating, storing, and retrieving data, and leading teams to implement new or modified processing systems. The specialist also provides consultative services, adapts and presents complex information in clear formats, and manages dissemination practices and policies. Evidence includes 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' and 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
Future GSBPM expectation: Automated and AI-driven dissemination products are the norm, and the focus is on oversight, interpretation, and improvement of standardized outputs and templates. Manual creation and formatting yield to configuration and quality assurance within the automated ecosystem.
Role evolution: This role must evolve to lead operational and system change management, enabling automated production of dissemination products. The specialist will support system configuration, monitor pipeline accuracy, troubleshoot exceptions, participate in platform improvements, and ensure products remain compliant with user, legislative, and disclosure standards.
