Capability implication: Knowledge of automated dissemination pipelines, workflow monitoring, interpretation of AI-generated outputs, integration of metadata and disclosure controls, and collaboration on modular tools and templates for dissemination are more prominent. Ensuring products are actionable for both human and digital consumption is fundamental.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Release dissemination products
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05)' develops databases for dissemination, coordinates staff involved in manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, and leads teams for implementation of new or modified processing systems. The specialist represents subject matter divisions and provides expert guidance on dissemination ('coordinates and controls ... staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data', 'leads project teams or supervises work units in ... new or modified statistical processing systems').
Future GSBPM expectation: Dissemination will become more centrally managed and automated, requiring the specialist to focus on oversight, quality assurance, auditing of automated workflows, and rare exception handling. The role's involvement will shift from direct supervision of manual dissemination tasks to governance of standardized, IT-maintained platforms, contributing to dissemination rules and ensuring integrity, security, and compliance.
Role evolution: The specialist will need to monitor dissemination pipelines via dashboards and logs, respond to alerts or breaches, and provide leadership on system improvements. Supervisory responsibilities become more about managing workflow exceptions, auditing platform configurations, and ensuring release processes follow mandated protocols, rather than coordinating manual activities.
Capability implication: Deeper understanding of platform-based release mechanics, digital governance, workflow rules, and exception processes become crucial. The specialist must interpret audit logs and engage in platform oversight rather than manual database management for releases.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Promote dissemination products
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist develops databases, coordinates the manipulation and retrieval of data, and provides consultative advisory services. Key activities include representing subject-matter divisions on development projects, managing dissemination systems, and leading project teams for new or modified dissemination systems. Future GSBPM expectation: Promotion is expected to be programmed, automated, and user-centric, focusing on surfacing products in machine-actionable formats via APIs and optimizing for real-time digital engagement. Continuous improvement tied to engagement analytics and metadata optimization replaces static marketing approaches. Role evolution: The Specialist must transition to providing operational support for digital and automated dissemination systems, ensure metadata standards for discoverability, participate in development of API-based dissemination and logic, and analyze engagement data to measure impact and drive iterative improvements. Capability implication: This position will require nuanced knowledge of metadata-driven dissemination, API-enabled publication logic, and practical ability to support real-time engagement analytics and targeted digital outreach strategies.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Provide user support (GSBPM Phase 7.5)
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams involved in manipulating, storing, retrieving, and disseminating data, provides consultative services to users, and develops guidelines and databases for statistical output. Key activities include 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' Future GSBPM expectation: User support shifts to digital-first, with automated, standardized, metadata-rich platforms supporting user discovery and access, and success measured by digital engagement and self-service enablement. Human support focuses on resolving complex technical queries and maintaining digital trust. Role evolution: The Specialist's role will need to expand from direct consultative service delivery towards designing, implementing, and maintaining robust digital support structures such as automated user guidance, digital FAQs, machine-actionable documentation, and supporting programmatic access workflows. Monitoring digital user behaviour and collaborating with platform and metadata teams will be a new expectation. Capability implication: Detailed knowledge of digital engagement analytics, metadata and API documentation standards, and capacity to design and maintain scalable automated support mechanisms are increasingly vital. The specialist must become fluent in digital trust management and advanced support workflows for machine and human users.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Gather evaluation inputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) develops databases for studies and ad hoc requests, coordinates and controls activities involved in manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, and develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications ('Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.'). Quality checks and evaluation inputs have traditionally been collected and assessed manually by the specialist or their teams.
Future GSBPM expectation: Automatic, system-driven collection of evaluation inputs reduces manual data gathering and positions staff to focus on monitoring system outputs, configuring evaluation dashboards, and interpreting quality or anomaly indicators generated by production architecture.
Role evolution: The specialist must transition from overseeing or performing manual compilation and assessment of evaluation materials to ensuring that processing systems are properly configured to emit standardized, actionable evaluation data in real time, and to using dashboards and automated reports for ongoing quality verification.
Capability implication: Greater importance is placed on understanding system instrumentation, configuring automatic collection mechanisms, and interpreting real-time operational and quality metrics as part of statistical production and dissemination activities.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Identify needs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and implements long term strategies, defines and evaluates system development, reviews quality and completeness, researches developments in data processing concepts/methods/techniques, consultative service, and manages units and teams ('Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs'). Future GSBPM expectation: Needs identification moves to a digital-first, enterprise-wide, proactive process, requiring staff to scan existing/alternative data assets, formalize cost-benefit/risk/automation/feasibility assessments, and justify any new collection with documented evidence. Role evolution: The Head is required to lead and manage digital scanning initiatives, evaluate operational feasibility and automation compatibility, and ensure their unit's proposals for new production/dissemination systems are justified through solution-first, digitally traceable workflows aligned with agency strategic priorities. Capability implication: Familiarity with data asset discovery/metadata platforms, assessment of digital/AI-enabled operational feasibility, integration of cost-benefit/resource/risk models, and leading teams in digital-enabled needs identification and documentation.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Prepare and submit business case
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and controls development and implementation of statistical systems, prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations, and manages multiple projects and teams. This is illustrated by statements such as, 'Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' and 'Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work.' Future GSBPM expectation: Business cases must be constructed to demonstrate automation-first, data reuse, modularity, and empirical cost-benefit logic within an agile governance framework. Role evolution: This role must move from preparing proposals and recommendations seeking incremental change to framing business cases for scalable, automated, and modular solutions, with explicit alignment to corporate platforms and transparent evidence-based decision criteria. Capability implication: Capabilities in multidisciplinary collaboration, cost-benefit analysis, automation and platform alignment, and outcome-centric business case construction become critical for supporting new approval processes.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans, implements, and controls development and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes, 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' and 'participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems.' They develop policies, guidelines, and methods regarding acquisition, production, and dissemination of data, and set policies for confidentiality and quality. Future GSBPM expectation: The role transitions toward overseeing design of modular, scalable dissemination platforms, integrating open and machine-actionable technologies, metadata standards, and new access protocols designed for both human and AI consumption. Heads must embed automation and reusability into their long-term strategies, coordinate cross-functional teams for platform-centric output design, and ensure systems support differentiated access, embargoes, and compliance with ethical rules. Role evolution: This means evolving from managing discrete systems and projects toward orchestrating platform-based dissemination architecture, rigorous metadata management, and continuous improvement of self-serve systems, focusing more on platform stewardship and cross-team collaboration. Capability implication: Knowledge in enterprise platform governance, metadata structuring, API ecosystem management, confidentiality in automated release, and system integration for machine-actionable outputs becomes central.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design processing and analysis
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and controls the development, implementation, and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes, reviews quality and completeness, researches trends in mass data processing, and provides expert consultative services (“Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes… Identifies and researches trends and developments in mass data processing concepts, methods and techniques”). Future GSBPM expectation: The future design phase mandates that all system development deliver modular, AI-enabled, metadata-driven, standardized processing pipelines and workflows that are easily auditable, template-based, and ready for automation. Design must anticipate rapid integration of new data sources and real-time processing requirements, making legacy design and ad hoc customization obsolete. Role evolution: The Head will have to transition from overseeing traditional system design and development to managing teams that configure modular, metadata-driven, automation-ready workflows and templates. Specification, guideline and contract development will need to focus on automation and machine-actionable standards, requiring close collaboration with IT and automation specialists. Capability implication: The role will require significant expertise in metadata management, modular and microservices architecture, automation enablement, and template-based design for processing and dissemination. Principles of auditability, privacy/disclosure controls, version-control, and responsible AI deployment will become central to system planning, review, and consultative guidance.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Head, Production and Dissemination' manages strategies for statistical program development, new or modified statistical systems, and leads teams involved in systems design. Responsibilities include defining methods for production and dissemination, reviewing processing trends and system development, establishing guidelines for system use, and overseeing quality and compliance. Evidence: 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs. Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.' Future GSBPM expectation: In the future, collection instruments will be built and maintained through AI-enabled, modular, self-service platforms, with staff configuring automated pipelines and managing integration with enterprise metadata systems, and ensuring paradata capture. The Head will need to support automated instrument assembly and adapt quality governance to a highly digital, platform-based environment. Role evolution: Operational management will focus less on custom development, and more on configuring, validating and managing automated instrument platforms, ensuring auditability and compliance in decentralized, self-service environments. Capability implication: Deep expertise in automated platform governance, digital compliance, metadata integration, AI-assisted design, and the operational standards for interoperability and security are crucial.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems, manages system design teams, and provides expert advisory services on production and dissemination systems. Technical activities describe management of system development, defining processing specifications, and implementing new technology. Future GSBPM expectation: Component development occurs in standardized, AI-enabled, modular environments, with default automation, auditability and role-based access. Business staff participate actively in component assembly and attestation, while development focuses on configuring reusable elements rather than writing custom code. Role evolution: The Head must shift toward managing the orchestration, attestation, documentation, and governance of modular, automated components developed within enterprise platforms. Leadership is needed in fostering cross-unit reuse, overseeing rigorous security and reproducibility standards, and ensuring the rapid adoption and auditability of component usage. Capability implication: Deep familiarity with orchestration frameworks, automated governance and validation, audit and security protocols, and scalable, reproducible pipeline management is increasingly critical. Leadership is required to embed these standards across heterogeneous teams and programs.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Head, Production and Dissemination' plans and implements long-term strategies for statistical programs, dictates development and operational policies for statistical systems and processes, and manages teams for production and dissemination systems ('Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.' and 'Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems.').
Future GSBPM expectation: Strategic oversight and operational management are now tightly bound to enterprise-level, modular, reusable dissemination system architectures. Mission-critical dissemination is limited to systems managed centrally by IT and must be AI-ready, interoperable, and standardized. The Head must ensure strict compliance with platform, security, and quality requirements, shepherding the shift away from ad-hoc, custom build approaches.
Role evolution: The Head must refocus strategy and operations on sustaining modular, standardized dissemination, leading migration to corporate platforms and automation tools, and prioritizing reusability and machine-actionable outputs. Oversight of teams and projects will focus on maintaining compliance, achieving interoperability, and supporting rapid, automated publication.
Capability implication: Deep knowledge of platform governance, metadata standards, automation, integration with central IT, and enterprise dissemination architectures becomes central. Skills in managing compliance and driving organizational adoption of automation and open formats are increasingly necessary.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Configure workflows
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) is responsible for planning, implementing, and controlling the development and operation of divisional statistical systems and processes, managing program requirements, preparing program proposals, developing and evaluating system frameworks, and leading teams involved in systems design and projects. The work description details setup, modification, enhancement, and evaluation of statistical processing systems and workflows. Evidence: 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.' and 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.' Future GSBPM expectation: The future state demands automated, modular, and standardized workflow orchestration replacing bespoke and manual assembly—configuration is event-driven, auditable, version-controlled, and empowered for business staff through self-service platforms. Role evolution: The head must shift from manual operational setup and system design toward enabling and governing the deployment of automated workflows, supporting business empowerment through no-code/low-code tools, and collaborating closely with IT to define guardrails and maintain workflow standards, resiliency, and auditability. Their operational management will now require oversight of versioning, attestation, roll-back, and change governance, with reduced custom coding, increased automation, and coordinated support and knowledge sharing. Capability implication: Their role will require advanced operational knowledge of enterprise workflow orchestration, automation principles, modular system design, workflow governance, as well as the ability to translate business requirements into configuration standards for scalable, auditable and compliant workflow deployment.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Test production systems
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) presently plans and implements strategies for statistical program development and operation, including reviewing and certifying program results and managing unit teams involved in systems design ("Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results"; "Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems"). Historically, this has meant overseeing quality review processes and test activities at major stage gates. In the GSBPM future state, testing becomes a continuously integrated, automated function required for every production system and deployment, shifting away from manual sign-off toward automated attestation and reproducibility documentation. This role must evolve to oversee and govern testing discipline across domains, ensure all systems meet organizational guardrails, and drive operationalization of automated test and monitoring regimes. Leadership in embedding these practices, developing robust enterprise testing frameworks, and sustaining shared controls becomes critical—especially with business-led development and expanded use of self-service platforms. Capabilities in designing and governing automated testing infrastructure, attestation-based workflow oversight, and regulatory audit readiness and monitoring become paramount.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Test statistical business process
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of statistical systems, including "reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results," and "defines processing and production specifications and guidelines," which includes overseeing system testing and evaluation. The role explicitly involves reviewing trends and developments and presenting options for new technology. Future GSBPM expectation: Testing will become a mandatory, structured phase where the certification of business process readiness relies on systematic testing outcomes, requiring leadership to organize, interpret, and communicate test results as part of program approvals and operational launches. Role evolution: The Head will be responsible for establishing comprehensive test strategies, ensuring team adherence to testing protocols, evaluating and signing off on test outcomes, and integrating findings into continuous improvement and operational decisions. Capability implication: There will be greater need for understanding test management frameworks, evaluating test results for risk and operational readiness, and communicating test outcomes as part of stakeholder engagement and program sign-off.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Finalise production systems
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06, 900-222) is responsible for planning, developing, implementing, and operating statistical production systems, which currently includes preparing proposals, defining specifications, managing quality, and overseeing system development and operation. Evidence includes activities such as 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' 'Defines processing and production specifications,' and 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.' The future GSBPM expectation shifts this role toward operationalizing modular, automated, and AI-enabled pipelines, embedding practices like automated deployment, version control, real-time monitoring, as well as boosting user enablement. The finalization process will require coordinated operational and compliance checks, integration of self-service platforms, and active governance around digital guardrails and security postures. This transforms the role from traditional technical implementation and hand-off to continual operational readiness, compliance, and cross-team enablement. The required capabilities evolve from classic system management toward advanced knowledge of automation and modularity principles, enterprise architecture, digital security, and interdisciplinary enablement—especially the ability to document and train a more diverse user community and manage reproducibility and FAIR compliance.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Finalise production systems
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06, 900-222) is responsible for planning and controlling the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes, making it highly implicated in the finalization phase. Activities such as 'Defines processing and production specifications and guidelines for the contracting of development work,' and 'Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files,' are directly implicated by the expectation for automated, AI-enabled, modular production systems, continuous monitoring, compliance with digital guardrails, and FAIR standards. In the future, the role has to operationalize and oversee systems that facilitate automation, real-time monitoring, role-based enablement, continual compliance, and compatibility with wider enterprise architecture and self-service models. This increases the importance of advanced digital system design, automation, cross-team enablement, and interdisciplinary governance, particularly around operational risk management and reproducibility.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Set up collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) plans and implements strategies for statistical program development, controls development and implementation of new systems, defines processing and production specifications, manages units, and reviews system quality and completeness. Their leadership extends to managing financial resources and leading project teams responsible for systems design and operational efficiency. Future GSBPM expectation: Automated, AI-enabled, enterprise workflows will be responsible for most setup activities; human involvement is focused on validating system logic, managing exceptions, conducting risk reviews, and ensuring security and ethics. Role evolution: The Head will need to transition from managing custom system design and manual operation to overseeing automated platforms, validating outputs, and managing rare exceptions. Management becomes increasingly oversight and governance-driven, with heightened focus on system interoperability, risk management, and ethical AI deployment, rather than traditional hands-on preparation. Capability implication: Expertise in platform automation, data integration, system governance, and risk/quality assurance will be fundamental for effective supervision and strategy, as traditional operational execution is minimized.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Run collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) manages a unit and project teams overseeing the development and operation of divisional statistical programs, including overseeing statistical system development, production, and dissemination strategies. This role is tasked with 'planning and controlling the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' and 'defining, coordinating and evaluating the cost of statistical system development work.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The operational landscape for 'Run collection' is now dominated by AI-driven, automated pipelines, requiring the orchestration and maintenance of complex digital systems that ingest multi-source data (administrative, alternative, survey), with minimal human intervention outside monitoring and exceptions.
Role evolution: The Head must adapt from managing legacy production and dissemination systems to strategic oversight and optimization of digital, multi-source collection architectures, process automation, and real-time performance monitoring using dashboard tools. Decision-making broadens to system refinement, exception handling, and integration of AI workflow improvements. Quality assurance pivots from procedural compliance and routine oversight to dynamic system monitoring, paradata-driven adjustments, and escalated relationship management for complex respondent cases.
Capability implication: Architectural knowledge of digital data acquisition, process automation frameworks, real-time operational monitoring, orchestration of API-driven collection streams, and managing AI-based exception handling procedures is now critical.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Finalise collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06)' plans and implements long-term strategies for development and operation of statistical systems, defines and coordinates statistical system development, reviews and certifies program quality and completeness, and manages units and project teams involved in system design ('Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.' 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.'). Future GSBPM expectation: In a future where collection finalization is automated and standardized, strategic oversight focuses on ensuring compliance with real-time automated data pipelines, machine-actionable standards, and privacy-by-design. The role must ensure operational resilience, audit-readiness, and continual adaptation of platforms to evolving metadata and privacy standards. Role evolution: The Head's focus moves from traditional project management for system upgrades toward enterprise pipeline orchestration, real-time monitoring, exception analysis, and strategic governance of metadata standards, privacy controls, and automated archiving requirements. Capability implication: The Head must now be deeply versed in automated statistical pipeline management, strategic metadata and privacy governance, and continuous improvement for system resilience, auditing, and compliance.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Integrate data
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and implements strategies for divisional statistical programs, develops and implements new statistical systems and processes, and reviews quality and completeness of program results. This includes managing units and task forces involved in system design and participating as an expert in production and dissemination systems. The role traditionally involves overseeing the design, development, and operational management of custom data processing solutions, including integration logic for diverse sources. In the automated GSBPM future state, integration is managed through standardized, metadata-rich, modular, and auditable pipelines—restricting manual intervention. The Head must move from overseeing customized integration and manual intervention to supervising the deployment and governance of platform-driven pipelines, setting and maintaining standardized interface and metadata rules, and championing exception handling at scale. Capabilities in platform governance, metadata architecture, pipeline auditability, and exception logic management become more prominent.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Classify and code
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, manages and plans the development, implementation, and operation of statistical systems and processes, including review and certification of program quality and completeness. The role involves leading project teams for systems design, guiding development work, and producing guidelines and policies for statistical production systems and coding routines. Many current duties include overseeing manual coding approaches, quality assurance, and direct intervention in systems development that may be non-standardized or decentralized. Future GSBPM expectation: The subprocess is fundamentally automated and AI-driven. The head's new expectation is to manage ongoing maintenance and governance of automated classification modules, standardize coding and metadata practices, embed AI ethics and audit protocols, monitor and manage exceptions, and guide continuous adaptation in response to classification changes and data drift. Routine human coding work is replaced by oversight of AI modules and continual improvement cycles. Role evolution: The Head must shift from overseeing hands-on coding and manual QA activities to managing modular AI-powered pipelines, ensuring auditability, orchestrating governance protocols, monitoring model performance, resolving exceptions, and aligning centralized classification standards. Capability implication: Dominant importance is placed on model and pipeline governance, standards management, audit protocols, exception monitoring, metadata harmonization, and responsible oversight of AI-driven routines, leveraging cross-domain consistency and resilience in the classification subsystem.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Review and validate
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) holds strategic responsibility for planning and controlling the development, implementation and operation of statistical systems and for reviewing and certifying overall quality and completeness of program results: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' and 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.' In the GSBPM 5.3 future state, quality assurance becomes embedded by design: automated validation modules and AI/ML pipelines replace manual inspection. The Head must shift focus from overseeing manual quality reviews to steering governance of automated, standardized validation, managing exception processes, and establishing/monitoring audit trails. Their operational decisions now revolve around validating the performance and resilience of automation, ensuring version control of validation logic, and setting oversight standards for automated rules. This magnifies the importance of governance frameworks, auditability, and quality assurance in automated settings.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Edit and impute
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is responsible for long-term development, operational management, and quality assurance of divisional statistical programs, including the implementation and review of new or modified systems. Their responsibilities involve certifying program completeness and quality, overseeing mass data processing, and managing units involved in system design and production. They participate in committees and lead teams focused on processing and dissemination systems.

Future GSBPM expectation: The shift to AI-powered, automated edit/impute processing means program leaders must now drive the adoption, integration, and oversight of modular microservices and automated frameworks rather than continuous manual enhancement. Operational quality assurance will be centered on audit trails, algorithmic fairness, standardized component reuse, and exception handling.

Role evolution: The Head must now lead units in transitioning from hands-on, process-specific data editing and validation to managing automated pipeline infrastructure. They will develop and enforce policies for system traceability, oversee risk-based escalation for exceptions, and spearhead the adoption of agency-wide standards for edit/impute in a reproducible, scalable, and auditable manner. Strategic advice, resource allocation, and operational guidance will center on the deployment and continual improvement of AI processes, not traditional manual intervention.

Capability implication: The role requires enhanced knowledge in system orchestration, AI governance, auditability frameworks, performance monitoring of automated pipelines, and regulatory compliance regarding automated data editing. Familiarity with the ethical and reputational criteria for oversight of automated statistical production becomes increasingly critical.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Derive new variables and units
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) plans and implements strategies for statistical program development and coordinates new systems and processes, including quality review and certification of program results. Key activities include defining processing specifications, developing guidelines for system development, reviewing technical trends, and managing teams tasked with system design. Currently, these responsibilities often require managing the design and implementation of custom derivation processes, assessing new methodological approaches, and making decisions about analytical workflows. Future GSBPM expectation: Processing and derivation activities will be embedded as modular, metadata-driven microservices within orchestrated, auditable pipelines. The Head will oversee the transition to these automated pipelines, ensuring standardized logic, compliance with metadata and audit standards, and rapid, traceable deployment across domains. Role evolution: The Head’s operational and system management responsibilities evolve toward governance of automated, version-controlled transformation logic and stewardship over pipeline auditability, exception handling, and quality assurance. Decision-making pivots to managing modular design, implementation oversight, and cross-functional impact analysis as well as supporting real-time deployment and compliance. Capability implication: Advanced understanding of pipeline orchestration, modular microservices, metadata-driven logic, and audit-focused governance becomes essential. The Head must be adept at managing system integration and performance within automated production environments, overseeing exception events, and ensuring traceable, compliant pipeline operation.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Calculate aggregates
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The Head plans and controls the development and operation of statistical systems, evaluates system development work, certifies program quality, researches processing concepts, and manages units involved in systems design. Historically, this involves overseeing aggregation processes, developing policies, and setting technical guidelines. Future GSBPM expectation: Aggregation becomes managed through standardized, automated microservices orchestrated in modular pipelines. The Head’s role will focus on ensuring systems comply with metadata governance, monitoring auditability, supporting configuration for domain-specific exceptions, and directing teams away from manual aggregation or program-specific coding. Role evolution: Focus on strategic adoption of automation, oversight of system auditability and version control, guidance on exception handling through configuration (rather than bespoke coding), and alignment with institutional standardization and reproducibility objectives. Capability implication: Understanding of modular pipeline orchestration, metadata management, automated process configuration, governance mechanisms for exception handling, and audit trail documentation become central.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Finalise data files
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination directs the development, implementation, and operation of statistical systems and processes, defines policies and guidelines for production and dissemination, certifies overall quality and completeness of results, and researches data processing innovations ('Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.' & 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.'). Future GSBPM expectation: The process moves to highly automated, metadata-driven pipelines with reduced manual intervention. Oversight, validation, and audit become central; Heads are expected to certify reproducible, versioned outputs in machine-actionable formats and ensure compliance with standardization and transparency requirements. Role evolution: Production management will shift towards configuring process pipelines, enforcing metadata/standardization discipline, and actively managing exceptions and system audits rather than manual review or consolidation. Leadership includes ensuring coordination between subject matter, IT, and quality assurance functions. Capability implication: The ability to interpret, validate, and assure automated pipeline outputs, steward metadata and version control practices, and oversee exception resolution and audit quality are required, along with cross-functional collaboration and process innovation skills.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Prepare draft outputs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination 'plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs' and controls system development, quality certification, as well as managing units and teams for output production and dissemination. The role involves defining, coordinating, and evaluating specifications and outcomes related to draft outputs. Future GSBPM expectation: The head will oversee managerial and operational transitions to AI-enabled, automated output preparation pipelines, focusing on system orchestration, template standardization, exception handling, and continuous system improvement. Role evolution: The role will need to evolve toward leading the adoption and operational integration of automated processes, establishing performance metrics (e.g., time to publication, reduction in manual edits), and managing governance for automated output validation and sign-off. Capability implication: System orchestration, change management, agile governance, and advanced output quality monitoring will become increasingly relevant, alongside in-depth understanding of AI-driven production environments.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Validate outputs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: This role involves reviewing and certifying the overall quality and completeness of program results, and preparing policies, guidelines, and instructions for development, use and evaluation of systems and processes including validation ('Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results'). It also defines processing specifications and assesses trends in mass data processing, reflecting responsibility for validation system design and operation. Future GSBPM expectation: Operational responsibility is now focused on overseeing AI-powered validation modules, ensuring standardized, auditable processes, and governance of automated pipelines. Accountability remains for final data quality, but the execution is primarily automated. Role evolution: The Head moves toward policy and governance of automated validation, developing and monitoring metadata-driven quality frameworks, investigating exceptions flagged by automated systems, and ensuring auditability and transparency. Capability implication: Advanced knowledge of AI-driven validation, orchestration of automated statistical QA, and formulation of audit and oversight policies for automated pipelines is necessary. The role increases in importance for compliance, ethical assurance, and exception handling.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Apply disclosure control
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) plans and implements new statistical systems/processes, defines policies, guidelines, and procedures for confidentiality, quality, and dissemination, manages teams and projects, and establishes policies for data security ('Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and ... protection of computer systems ... databases and files'). Future GSBPM expectation: Disclosure control is tightly embedded in automated pipelines, requiring standardized, auditable, and automated security/confidentiality solutions. Role evolution: The Head's responsibilities will evolve toward managing the lifecycle and operation of AI-driven, automated disclosure control within production and dissemination systems, collaborating closely with IT and data engineers, maintaining oversight and escalation procedures, and ensuring real-time confidentiality safeguards. Capability implication: Advanced knowledge in system integration, automated workflow auditability, and operational oversight of AI-driven disclosure, with a focus on managing exception processes and adapting disclosure rules to novel formats and rapid dissemination timelines.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: GSBPM 6.5 Finalise Outputs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination is tasked with planning, controlling, and certifying the overall quality and completeness of program results, as well as managing the development, implementation, and operation of statistical systems and processes. This includes defining processing specifications, developing policies and guidelines for system use and evaluation, and leading teams involved in systems design and data dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' and 'Manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design.' Future GSBPM expectation: The finalization of outputs will be systematized, automated, and embedded in orchestrated pipelines, where AI and automation handle consistency checks, caveat assignment, and documentation, requiring oversight rather than hands-on manual output finalization. Role evolution: The Head must transition from overseeing manual workflows and quality review to directing and assuring automated pipeline validation, monitoring system-generated outputs, and focusing on strategic oversight, exception management, and trust in automation. Capability implication: This shift places greater importance on expertise in monitoring, auditing automated processes, interpreting system-generated caveats and validation flags, and maintaining standards for automated approval and release workflows. Deep understanding of orchestration, reproducible pipelines, and trust management in statistical output systems will become central.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Update output systems
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement, and operation of divisional statistical programs, including the development, implementation, and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes. They define processing and production specifications, develop policies, guidelines, and procedures for systems and processes, and review trends and developments in data processing concepts and methods. They also manage units and project teams involved in systems design and oversee the quality and completeness of program results. Evidence: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.', 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.', 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.'

Future GSBPM expectation: The updating of output systems will shift from manual or semi-automated, program-specific approaches to fully automated, standardized, and centrally governed procedures. Outputs must be machine-actionable, compliant with enterprise metadata and FAIR principles, and published via APIs and open formats for immediate use by both humans and AI. Manual interventions will be limited to governance, exception handling, and continuous improvement of metadata standards.

Role evolution: The EC-06 Head must transition from overseeing multiple program-specific systems and bespoke dissemination processes toward stewarding centralized, automated dissemination platforms governed by strict metadata and interoperability standards. Their focus will shift to ensuring system health, compliance with enterprise metadata schemas, exception resolution, and orchestrating cross-program output needs through metadata and configuration. They would need to establish protocols for real-time, automated publication and version control, prioritizing platform-level governance rather than granular manipulation of output formats or local troubleshooting.

Capability implication: Deep understanding of enterprise metadata standards, automation frameworks, and API-driven publication becomes central. The role will require competence in platform-level governance and compliance monitoring, expertise in reviewing and improving modular dissemination components, and knowledge of how metadata ensures interoperability and machine-readiness. Familiarity with FAIR principles, real-time dissemination, and event-driven publication pipelines also becomes more critical.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Produce dissemination products
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and implements strategies for developing, enhancing, and operating divisional statistical programs, including defining the methods for production and dissemination, managing teams, and certifying program quality. The position guides policy for systems and participates in strategic planning and operational management. Evidence is visible in activities such as 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs,' and 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.'
Future GSBPM expectation: Leadership is required to drive the adoption and continuous improvement of AI-enabled, automated dissemination pipelines. Product oversight shifts from hands-on creation to high-level orchestration, platform governance, template evolution, and quality assurance.
Role evolution: The Head must champion automation strategies, ensure alignment between subject-matter and IT teams, manage exception handling, guide template and platform evolution, and provide leadership on quality assurance for both human- and machine-consumable outputs. Managing stakeholder expectations and system performance is central.
Capability implication: Critical capabilities are in platform-centric production management, advanced oversight of automated pipelines, collaborative governance of dissemination standards/templates, and strategic operational change management for modular, scalable dissemination. Decision-making will increasingly focus on orchestrating automated systems and troubleshooting systemic/edge-case dissemination issues.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Release dissemination products
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06)' plans and implements long-term strategies for statistical programs, defines and evaluates statistical system development, reviews quality and completeness of program results, and manages units involved in systems design and operation. They set policies and procedures for data security, system maintenance, and dissemination ('develops policies, guidelines, instructions ... for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes', 'establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data ... and dissemination applications').
Future GSBPM expectation: Strategic and operational responsibility for dissemination moves toward platform-centric oversight, requiring heads to manage the operational resilience, exception handling, and governance of automated release systems. They will need to engage with enterprise toolkits, rules configuration, and design of auditable workflows for embargoes, security, and mission-critical releases. The scope becomes less about designing custom systems and more about ensuring sound operation, compliance, and improvement of centralized dissemination platforms.
Role evolution: The head will require advanced oversight of platform workflows, auditor logs, and system alerts, identifying risks and breaches, and setting escalation protocols. Strategic planning will increasingly revolve around platform improvement, operational resilience, and digital governance rather than bespoke production or dissemination design.
Capability implication: Knowledge of enterprise dissemination platform architecture, workflow auditing, rule-setting for release authorization, security governance, and exception process design becomes highly relevant. The head must lead organizational change toward automated, platform-based release management.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Promote dissemination products
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, plans and implements strategies for divisional statistical program development, including 'development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.' The role covers defining dissemination concepts and methods, reviewing program results for quality and completeness, and providing consultative services on data dissemination. Future GSBPM expectation: Dissemination product promotion will become tightly integrated with automated, AI-enabled, API-driven platforms, requiring digital catalogs and metadata management as core activities. Promotion will increasingly target machine consumers (bots, aggregators), demanding machine-actionable publication and proactive surfacing of products. Role evolution: The Head must oversee automated population of digital catalogs, enforce metadata quality, implement real-time engagement analytics, and manage integration with web/social/API channels. The position must shift focus to governance of metadata and promotional logic, and continuously analyze effectiveness through digital data streams. Capability implication: The Head will need operational knowledge of digital dissemination systems, metadata governance for discoverability, API integration for automated promotion, and data-driven analytical approaches to monitor and optimize outreach impact.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Provide user support (GSBPM Phase 7.5)
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and controls development and operation of statistical systems, provides expert consultative services to users, and manages teams for development of new dissemination platforms. Key activities include 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs' and 'Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada.' Future GSBPM expectation: The function transitions from information management and ad-hoc support to stewardship of highly standardized, machine-actionable, user-friendly discovery and access platforms that enable self-service and automated responses for both human and machine users. Role evolution: The Head will be expected to lead the transition towards digital support environments, focusing on platform-based user enablement, real-time monitoring of user feedback, ensuring interoperability of metadata and APIs, and curating high-value automated support tools. Certification of quality will increasingly involve measurement of digital user experience and support effectiveness metrics. Capability implication: Advanced knowledge of digital platform management, API and metadata standardization, real-time usage analytics, and platform-integrated support systems becomes essential. The capability to anticipate emerging user needs (including for AI and programmatic access) and adapt support environments accordingly is required.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Gather evaluation inputs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) is tasked with planning and implementing strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs, and with reviewing and certifying overall quality and completeness of program results. Their responsibilities include preparing program proposals on statistical frameworks, developing policies and guidelines for system use and evaluation, and reviewing trends and developments in data processing concepts (see: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results...' and 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes'). This typically involves manual assessment of data quality and system performance based on materials assembled ad hoc or provided by staff.
Future GSBPM expectation: Evaluate inputs are now expected to be systematically emitted by statistical workflows, with staff monitoring standardized dashboards and configuring quality indicators, instead of compiling evaluation materials manually. The operational expectation is for all systems to be instrumented for automatic capture of evaluation inputs.
Role evolution: The Head, Production and Dissemination will need to shift from overseeing manual compilation and review of evaluation materials to ensuring that production and dissemination systems are designed for real-time monitoring and automated generation of actionable evaluation data. Their efforts become more focused on enabling effective system instrumentation, designing relevant performance indicators, and interpreting automated evaluation results for program improvement.
Capability implication: This places greater emphasis on knowledge of system instrumentation, data pipeline architecture, automated quality monitoring frameworks, and the ability to interpret operational metrics and dashboards in statistical production environments.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Agree an action plan
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) 'plans and implements long term strategies', 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results', and 'provides expert advisory and consultative services'. The position also manages units and teams involved in systems design, process implementation, and program operation, and develops guidelines and procedures for statistical operations and action implementation.

Future GSBPM expectation: The rapid, automated, and modular environment means action plans need to be developed and agreed much faster, with in-built monitoring for action status and outcomes. Action plan implementation and results must be tracked digitally, with transparent dashboards and visible ownership, and plans recalibrated responsively based on near-real-time feedback—especially if related to AI-driven or automated workflows.

Role evolution: The Head will need to move from traditional project or program action tracking to establishing enterprise dashboards and routine digital progress monitoring, ensuring real-time accountability and transparency. Action planning will be ongoing, integrated into program operation, and deeply entwined with the organization's automated process control structure. Guiding teams and ensuring compliance with automated workflow requirements becomes a daily operational priority, not simply a project phase.

Capability implication: This role requires advanced knowledge of digital project tracking, action item monitoring and escalation platforms, and the capacity to implement and oversee feedback loops between evaluation findings and operational adjustments. Understanding of continuous improvement processes and digital governance will rise in importance.

Senior Economic Analyst.title: Establish output objectives
Senior Economic Analyst.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Senior Economic Analyst plans and conducts analysis and develops strategies, innovative methods and models for analytical outputs, and determines objectives and priorities for specific studies, including evaluation of data source fitness and options for integrating/producing program outputs. '[Assesses client requirements for statistical information; recommends the conduct of feasibility studies or launching of projects; defines project objectives and scope...]' demonstrates involvement in objective-setting and output prioritization. Future GSBPM expectation: The process requires systematic demonstration that objectives are feasible within enterprise automation, as well as default reliance on existing/alternative data assets unless explicitly justified. Automation, digital workflow compatibility, and machine-actionable output criteria are embedded in objective acceptance. Role evolution: The analyst role will need to evolve toward assessing the automation, interoperability, and reusability of data assets as primary criteria when establishing output objectives. Recommendations will be required to be formally documented, with justification for resource-intensive or manual processes, and tightly scoped for digital workflows. Capability implication: Increased importance of enterprise data asset evaluation, automation process alignment, interoperability/machine-actionability assessment, and digital feasibility/cost-benefit analysis allied to subject-matter analytical expertise.

Senior Economic Analyst.title: Identify Concepts
Senior Economic Analyst.justification: Current responsibility: The Senior Economic Analyst (EC-06) is responsible for performing detailed analysis, evaluation, and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determining changes in statistical needs, which includes 'devising new concepts, definitions, methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend statistical information relating to the different subject matter domains.' The job description specifies that this work impacts the development of standards, classifications, and compilation methods, and there is substantial involvement in the creation and review of conceptual frameworks (decision_making | 'Develops and procures in conformity to guidelines and policies new data sources, performs updates and modifications to program content and coverage to align to international frameworks or classifications and devises new concepts, definitions, methods and models...'). Future GSBPM expectation: The process for identifying concepts is shifting from manual, ad hoc creation to prioritization of reusable, standardized concepts derived and harmonized through machine-assisted review of data holdings, metadata inventories, and AI-driven gap analysis. Human experts move toward arbitration and negotiation between competing priorities and ensuring digital interoperability rather than primary conceptual definition. Role evolution: This role will need to transition from manual conceptual development to orchestrating, validating, and steering machine-suggested concepts and frameworks. The focus becomes the resolution and justification of exceptions, negotiation of cross-program alignment, and ensuring statistical concepts are digitally interoperable and FAIR-compliant. Capability implication: Deeper understanding of enterprise metadata, interoperability standards, and the ability to arbitrate between competing concept frameworks, plus the knowledge needed to assess AI-driven suggestions for subject-matter fit, digital re-usability, and organizational strategic alignment, become critical for effective performance.

Senior Economic Analyst.title: Design variables
Senior Economic Analyst.justification: Current responsibility: The Senior Economic Analyst (EC-06) plays a key role in developing new concepts, definitions, methods and models for statistical information within various subject matter domains and contributes to revising classifications and conceptual frameworks (see: 'develops and procures in conformity to guidelines and policies new data sources, performs updates and modifications to program content and coverage to align to international frameworks or classifications and devises new concepts, definitions, methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend statistical information relating to the different subject matter domains'). This includes a strong advisory component to survey standards and the integration of classifications and definitions. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state emphasizes that variable design becomes machine-actionable, standardized, and metadata-driven, with significant focus on maintaining reusable variable libraries, enterprise registries and aligning variables to interoperability standards across pipelines. Role evolution: The Senior Economic Analyst will shift from project-specific or manual variable definition toward stewardship and enrichment of shared variable vocabularies and enterprise metadata repositories. They will be expected to collaborate on the management and integration of variable libraries, contribute to standards and governance processes, and ensure variables are AI-ready and suitable for downstream automation. Capability implication: The analyst will require deeper understanding of enterprise metadata systems, interoperability frameworks, variable standardization, and how variable choices enable or constrain automation and cross-domain analytical workflows. Knowledge about semantic registries, versioning practices, and metadata enrichment will become central.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer currently 'develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' 'designs specifications for the testing of data,' and 'leads project teams... in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' They also negotiate procedural modifications and translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications. Future GSBPM expectation: With outputs expected to be modular, interoperable, and available via APIs and metadata, the development officer will need to shift from building static, manual systems toward designing robust, scalable dissemination platforms that automatically deliver standardized, machine-actionable data assets, including clear access and confidentiality controls. Role evolution: The role will focus less on designing bespoke solutions and more on specifying, building, and evolving output models, metadata schemas, and protocol-based dissemination systems, closely collaborating with IT, metadata governance, and user experience stakeholders. Capability implication: This will intensify the need for knowledge around system interoperability, metadata management, API-driven dissemination, and the application of confidentiality and ethical rules in automated, scalable platforms.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Design processing and analysis
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' (EC-04) develops processing systems and applications, designs specifications for data testing and database maintenance, assesses subject area changes and modifies processing applications, provides subject-matter advice, and leads teams in new system development (“Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data… Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems”). Future GSBPM expectation: The future design phase dictates that all processing system design be modular, metadata-driven, automation-ready, and standardized. Specification work shifts from manual rule documentation to system configuration and automation logic, requiring closer collaboration with process automation specialists. Role evolution: This Officer must transition from traditional system development—often manual and tailored—to producing automation-enabled, template-based, and machine-actionable designs for processing and analysis, anticipating rapid integration and auditability for new data sources and processes. Capability implication: Thorough knowledge of modular, metadata-driven workflow design, automation logic for processing systems, and template specification will be required. Skill in version-control, auditable pipeline design, and embedding privacy and validation logic within system configurations will be increasingly central.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' develops processing systems and applications to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data; designs specifications for testing and maintenance; leads teams implementing new or modified processing systems; and modifies or replaces processing systems as subject areas change. Evidence: 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' Future GSBPM expectation: The future state requires processing systems and collection instruments to be developed within modular, self-service, metadata-rich platforms that empower non-IT staff to build and maintain instruments. Manual intervention is minimal, and cognitive and functionality testing will be automated. Role evolution: This role will shift from developing bespoke systems to configuring enterprise platforms, integrating AI-enabled modules, and validating automated pipelines for collection. Officers must ensure collection instruments are interoperable, capture paradata, and conform to strict digital guardrails set by enterprise standards. Capability implication: Advanced capability in digital platform configuration, metadata-driven development, automation validation, and stewardship of paradata/metadata integration become important, along with platform governance and compliance expertise.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer is responsible for developing processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data, designing specifications for the testing of data, and leading project teams or work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems. Evidence includes statements such as 'Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 mandates a move from ad hoc, program-specific coding toward modular, reusable, AI-enabled and low-code/no-code platforms, with strict standards for automation, interoperability, and auditability. This turns component development and reuse into a process led by business staff using enterprise-standard toolkits, focusing on assembly, configuration, validation, and governance instead of manual coding. Role evolution: The Officer's work will shift from designing and implementing bespoke solutions toward curating, integrating, orchestrating, and validating the use of modular, interoperable components within standard platforms. Their decision-making must increasingly focus on selecting, configuring, and governing components that ensure security, auditability, and reproducibility across programs. Capability implication: Capabilities such as understanding modular microservice architecture, orchestrating workflows, validating AI-enabled and automated components, attesting to audit and governance protocols, and ensuring role-based access and reproducibility in component usage become far more central to the role.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data, assesses changes requiring modifications or replacements of these systems, and leads project teams for new or revised statistical processing systems ('Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.').
Future GSBPM expectation: Building dissemination components will rely heavily on enterprise-level toolkits and modular libraries. Custom or legacy system development is discouraged. Dissemination for both human and machine consumption must be built using corporate, standardized platforms and open formats. Automation and AI-readiness are default requirements.
Role evolution: The Officer must shift from designing custom solutions toward assembling and configuring modular, reusable dissemination components within strict platform, security, and quality guidelines. Efforts will focus on ensuring new or modified systems are interoperable, automation-ready, and able to deliver standardized outputs suitable for both API and traditional channels. System specifications and project planning must align with enterprise platform requirements.
Capability implication: Familiarity with corporate dissemination architectures and shared libraries, automation, metadata standards, and open formats becomes more critical. Knowledge of low/no-code tooling, platform governance, and machine-actionable output validation is increasingly needed for system development and project leadership.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Configure workflows
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04) develops processing systems and applications, designs data testing specifications, determines the need to modify or replace applications, and leads teams in implementing new or modified statistical processing systems. The role includes technical leadership, operational management, and liaison with subject matter and systems specialists. Evidence: 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' Future GSBPM expectation: The configuration of processing workflows necessitates transition from manual, bespoke system development to automated, modular, event-driven pipelines with version control and audit trails, all accessible through enterprise self-service platforms. The future state expands responsibilities to maintaining modular workflow components, enabling business areas in workflow configuration, and supporting operational transparency. Role evolution: The officer will need to reorient development efforts away from custom coding to the configuration and deployment of standardized workflow modules, ensuring operational guardrails are followed, and facilitating business empowerment through new orchestration tools. Their leadership and technical advice will be directed toward supporting the operational discipline of workflow attestation, versioning, and business enablement within standardized platforms. Capability implication: Increased importance will be placed on modular system architecture, orchestration platform governance, automation principles, operational compliance, and the translation of subject matter requirements into standardized workflow configurations and business accessible modules.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Test production systems
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04) is currently responsible for developing processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data, as well as designing specifications for the testing of data and databases ("Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases."). Traditionally, testing may have involved manual or locally-scripted steps. The GSBPM future state demands a shift toward automated, system-level integration testing embedded in deployment pipelines, as well as attestation-based approvals for routine deployments. This changes the officer’s responsibilities from designing singular test cases/specifications to orchestrating automated test suites that validate not only technical correctness but also security, privacy, reproducibility, and compliance with organizational standards. To evolve, the officer will need to move from ad hoc/manual test design toward enterprise-level, continuous validation workflows and be accountable for supporting business developers who use self-service tools, embedding testing in their processes. Capabilities related to understanding enterprise testing infrastructure, documentation of reproducibility and chain of custody, and knowledge of automation and regulatory compliance now become central.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Test statistical business process
