Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer develops and tests processing systems, designs specifications for testing data, and assesses the need for modifying systems and applications. There is explicit mention of "designs specifications for the testing of data" and participation in teams and leading project units in implementation of new or modified systems. Future GSBPM expectation: The future testing phase for statistical business processes will require more systematic, documented, and repeatable approaches to testing, including the management of test data, scenario analysis, and recording results for feedback into process improvement. Role evolution: The Development Officer will be required to formalize testing plans (test documentation, predefined acceptance criteria), support test environments, actively participate in process validation, and ensure that outcomes from tests are fed into modification cycles for systems before they go live. Capability implication: There will be increased importance on design of structured test cases, familiarity with test automation, knowledge of validation protocols, and capturing testing outcomes for audit and continuous improvement.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Finalise production systems
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04, 900-220) develops processing systems and applications, conducts feasibility studies for new system requirements, and leads project teams responsible for implementing new or modified statistical processing systems. Current responsibilities—'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems'—indicate involvement in the technical finalization of production systems. The future GSBPM state transitions this process toward operationalizing modular, automated pipelines with version control, documentation, and ongoing monitoring, with an increased requirement to ensure FAIR compliance and user enablement. The role evolves beyond technical delivery to supporting systems that can be rapidly updated, maintained with minimal manual intervention, and accessible for broader user groups. The most relevant capability implications are around automation, modularity, design for self-service, digital compliance, and agile documentation—integrating these features into system finalization.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Finalise collection
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04)' is responsible for developing, modifying, and implementing processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data. The role includes designing specifications, leading project teams in developing and implementing new or modified statistical processing systems, and providing subject matter advice ('Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'). Future GSBPM expectation: With StatCan2030's vision, the 'Finalise collection' subprocess transitions from manual, ad hoc processes to fully automated, standardized pipelines driven by rich metadata and stringent privacy controls. Human intervention is minimized, shifting the operational focus onto automated validation, versioning, and archiving. Role evolution: The EC-04's responsibilities would need to shift from hands-on design and implementation of discrete processing functions to overseeing, maintaining, and improving enterprise-level automated data pipelines. This includes ensuring processing systems are compliant with machine-actionable metadata standards, managing the integration of privacy controls, and adapting to near-real-time processing flows. Capability implication: The officer must now deeply understand automated data orchestration, metadata-driven system design, exception/monitoring frameworks, and maintain audit-ready, resilient, scalable platforms—moving away from routine manual data manipulation to pipeline oversight, troubleshooting exceptions, and continuous automation improvement.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Integrate data
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' (EC-04) develops processing systems, assesses changes in subject areas, determines the need to modify or replace systems for data manipulation, storage, and retrieval, and leads teams implementing new systems. The current responsibility includes identifying system enhancements based on changes in concepts or data sources, often requiring bespoke solutions. Transitioning to the future GSBPM, integration becomes automated, event-driven, and governed by standardized rules and modules. The Development Officer would need to shift from developing and maintaining system-specific enhancements to designing, configuring, and validating reusable integration components and metadata standards. The role evolves to managing integration configuration and exception handling in a modular environment, prioritizing platform-enabled, auditable processes, and ensuring consistent application of FAIR principles. Capabilities in modular workflow management, metadata-driven integration, and platform configuration become crucial as manual interventions diminish.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Classify and code
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer is responsible for developing processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data, as well as designing specifications for testing data and maintaining databases. The role emphasizes resolving subject-matter, conceptual, and technical issues in the manipulation and retrieval of statistical information, leading teams implementing new or modified processing systems, and implementing enhancements. These responsibilities include hands-on involvement in processing logic, coding routines, and procedural improvements, which are often bespoke or require manual oversight. Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 establishes that the 'Classify and code' subprocess will be predominately automated, AI-enabled, and embedded into modular, orchestrated, auditable pipelines with minimal routine human intervention—manual tasks are limited to exceptional cases, and standard code lists and metadata are centrally managed and AI-driven classification tools span multiple domains. Role evolution: The incumbent must shift from developing and implementing manual or semi-automated coding systems to overseeing, validating, and improving AI-enabled pipelines, focusing on monitoring output quality, managing exceptions and ambiguity cases, retraining models, and maintaining standardized, reusable coding tools. They will need to contribute to pipeline oversight, validation of AI modules, and ensure transparent and reproducible processes, shifting away from custom manual solutions. Capability implication: Deep knowledge of automated pipeline design, AI model validation principles, reproducibility and auditability standards, and metadata management (especially within modular systems) becomes critical, alongside subject-matter understanding necessary for exception handling and evolving classification schemes.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Review and validate
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04) is responsible for developing and maintaining processing systems to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data—specifically including validation steps: 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.' As validation transitions to predominantly automated and AI-driven models per GSBPM 5.3’s future state, these officers must pivot from developing systems for static, manual validation to designing and maintaining orchestrated, event-driven validation pipelines, codifying validation logic for reuse, and embedding auditability and transparency in pipeline outputs. Their role becomes less about configuring single-use manual checks and more about implementing, version-controlling, and refining robust validation modules that operate at scale and across domains. This raises the importance of knowledge areas such as pipeline orchestration, validation rule management, and interface design for exception and audit tracking.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Edit and impute
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer is primarily responsible for developing, maintaining, and modifying processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data. This includes 'implementing enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications' and 'leading project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' Their responsibilities focus on both technological solutions and operational improvements for editing and manipulating data. 

Future GSBPM expectation: The GSBPM 5.4 phase will shift from manual, correction-focused processes to automated, AI-driven pipelines, with standardized, auditable microservices handling most edit and impute tasks. Human involvement pivots to oversight, exception handling, and algorithm validation. Responsibility for system design, modification, and integration becomes critical, but the focus is now on enabling and governing modular AI solutions rather than bespoke tooling or hands-on interventions.

Role evolution: The EC-04 officer will need to transition from developing ad hoc processing/application solutions to architecting and maintaining modular, reusable editing/imputation microservices, possibly participating in configuring and monitoring AI-powered workflows. Their involvement in specifications, technical integration, and change management will align with 'validation and refining algorithmic performance' rather than manual data correction. This implies more engagement with cross-program automation, version control, and compliance frameworks.

Capability implication: Fundamentally, domain expertise in edit/impute is refocused on the ability to enable, monitor and validate AI-driven processing; knowledge of algorithmic fairness, ethical oversight, auditability, and system integration with workflow orchestration frameworks becomes more prominent than hands-on programming or editing techniques.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Derive new variables and units
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04) develops processing systems, designs specifications for data testing, maintains databases, modifies and replaces systems for manipulation and retrieval, and leads project teams on new statistical processing system implementations. This includes hands-on involvement in developing methods for deriving new variables, improving processing techniques, and responding to subject-matter changes through system adaptation or custom coding. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, derivation occurs within automated, metadata-driven pipelines with standardized, auditable transformation logic. Manual coding and ad hoc derivation will be replaced by authoring, deploying, and managing modular logic libraries within governed architectures. Role evolution: The Development Officer will shift from system and code development for manual processing to designing metadata-driven modules, collaborating on cross-team deployments, and governing exception handling and quality in automated environments. They will focus on managing transformation logic repositories, pipeline performance monitoring, and rapid impact analysis in response to upstream or downstream changes. Capability implication: The role demands facility with modular transformation logic design, orchestration of microservice pipelines, and audit and compliance governance. Knowledge of metadata repository management, exception routing, and pipeline integration across statistical domains increases in importance.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Calculate aggregates
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: This position develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data. Typical tasks include designing specifications, modifying processing systems, and addressing problems in manipulation, storage, and retrieval, which often involve aggregation logic and scripts. Future GSBPM expectation: With aggregation handled by standardized, automated microservices within metadata-governed pipelines, development officers will focus more on configuring and maintaining these aggregation components, supporting system audit trails, and validating outputs rather than designing or maintaining custom aggregation scripts. They will contribute to governance procedures for exceptions and modifications to standard pipelines. Role evolution: Direct technical development of aggregation processes gives way to configuration and maintenance of shared enterprise modules, supporting exception management and audit trail requirements, and advising stakeholders on pipeline configuration and validation. Capability implication: Knowledge of enterprise pipeline architectures, microservice-based aggregation logic, metadata governance, automated validation and exception handling, and audit trail documentation replaces the need for hands-on scripting expertise.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Finalise data files
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer is accountable for developing processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data, and for implementing enhancements or modifications to these systems. The role includes leading project teams on new or modified statistical processing systems, and writing analytical reports on methodology and project findings ('Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' & 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'). Future GSBPM expectation: The 'Finalise data files' process will become highly automated, with end-to-end, version-controlled, metadata-driven pipelines, and manual manipulation minimized or eliminated. Oversight will require staff to configure, monitor, validate, and audit automated workflows, and ensure compliance with metadata standards and output requirements. Role evolution: The officer will need to lead and collaborate in configuring modular, automated workflows rather than guiding semi-manual or ad hoc custom processes. Their focus will shift from direct manipulation of data files to stewardship and oversight of system-level outputs, exception handling, and audit trail management for standardized, reproducible data products. Capability implication: Deep familiarity with metadata-driven production, automated solution design, exception management in event-driven environments, and interpreting version-controlled audit outputs becomes central, including the ability to collaborate with IT and methodologist teams to enforce standards and ensure traceability.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Prepare draft outputs
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer 'develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' designs specifications for the testing of data, and participates in the preparation and editing of outputs for dissemination. The role includes hands-on system development for technical output preparation and supervision of teams for statistical processing. Future GSBPM expectation: The role pivots significantly toward pipeline configuration, maintenance, and oversight of automated output generation. Role evolution: The officer will be required to transition from system development for manual processing to developing and maintaining automated AI-enabled analytical pipelines and monitoring their performance and output quality. Capability implication: Advanced knowledge in pipeline development and orchestration, auditability, reproducibility, and automated quality control mechanisms becomes a central requirement.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Apply disclosure control
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04) develops processing systems, assesses changes in subject area for system modifications, implements enhancements to processing applications, and ensures compliance with confidentiality requirements ('Knowledge of the Statistics Act ... and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements ... with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data.'). Future GSBPM expectation: As disclosure control becomes programmatically embedded, automated, and standardized, these officers must ensure disclosure control features are specified, built, and tested within new systems and applications. Role evolution: Responsibilities shift towards designing, specifying, and validating embedded disclosure controls in system development, monitoring real-time outcomes, and troubleshooting exceptions/videoing logs generated by automated disclosure modules, ensuring compliance and adaptability to new formats. Capability implication: Increased demand for system-oriented understanding of automated disclosure control logic, validation and audit trail interpretation, and collaborative design activities involving statistical, technical, and ethical perspectives.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: GSBPM 6.5 Finalise Outputs
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer develops processing systems for manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical data, assesses the need to modify processing systems, and leads teams implementing new systems. They are responsible for output preparation system design and subject-matter advice regarding development and dissemination workflows, as reflected in: 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' and 'Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings and the methodology used.' Future GSBPM expectation: Automated, reproducible pipelines will dominate output finalization, with embedded validation, caveat assignment, translation, and documentation handled by AI and automation. Officers will focus on reviewing exceptions, ensuring the robustness of automated finalization, and overseeing release-readiness criteria. Role evolution: The role will place less emphasis on developing and performing manual output assembly and validation, and more on designing, monitoring, and maintaining automated workflows, reviewing flagged cases, and overseeing systematized release activities. Capability implication: Capability in interacting with automated pipeline tools, exception review, auditing system-generated data and supporting documentation, and facilitating the transition to systematized outputs—including AI-assisted multilingual release—will become highly important.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Update output systems
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' (EC-04) develops processing systems and applications to manipulate, store, and retrieve statistical data, designs specifications for testing data and databases, and assesses changes to determine the need to modify or replace processing systems and dissemination procedures. They also negotiate procedural modifications, lead project teams, and communicate subject-matter requirements for system development. Evidence: 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data.'

Future GSBPM expectation: The focus of updating output systems will be on automated, metadata-driven, centralized platforms that enable real-time dissemination. Manual development and operational control will decline; instead, system modifications must be made according to enterprise-wide schemas and standards, with modular and reusable dissemination components.

Role evolution: The development officer’s efforts would pivot from designing local or bespoke applications or processing systems to supporting the specification, testing, and maintenance of enterprise-level dissemination platforms. They would need to translate subject-matter requirements into standardized metadata specifications, participate in platform-centric configuration, and support governance, validation, and the modularization of output components.

Capability implication: Knowledge in metadata-driven automation, understanding of interoperability standards, and familiarity with enterprise APIs and open formats become more essential. The role also demands proficiency with modular dissemination design, compliance monitoring, and principles for machine- and AI-ready publication, while deprioritizing manual or ad hoc script development for local system updates.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Produce dissemination products
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer' (EC-04) develops and modifies processing systems/applications for manipulating, storing, retrieving, and disseminating statistical data. This role also leads teams in the development and implementation of new systems, evaluates the impact of changes on dissemination, and writes analytical reports explaining methodologies and findings. Key evidence includes 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'
Future GSBPM expectation: Automation and AI-enabled dissemination pipelines become primary vehicles for product generation. The future-state expectation is that output creation is orchestrated via standardized, modular tools, and employees are responsible for monitoring, interpreting, and ensuring quality through oversight rather than hands-on assembly.
Role evolution: This position transitions towards configuring, maintaining, and improving automated dissemination pipelines, contributing to the evolution of templates, metadata and rules for automated outputs, and troubleshooting exceptions. The officer must now collaborate more closely with IT/data engineering to translate subject-matter requirements into user-centric, machine-actionable dissemination products and support rapid, scalable production.
Capability implication: Capabilities around automation orchestration, modular toolkits, standardized dissemination templates, integrated metadata, and system troubleshooting rise in importance. Understanding pipeline logic, version control for outputs, and ensuring compliance with disclosure control measures embedded in technology takes precedence.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Release dissemination products
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04)' develops processing systems and applications for manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, designs specifications for data testing and database maintenance, and leads teams implementing new or modified processing systems. Dissemination content and procedures are directly influenced by this role ('determines the impact ... for statistical methods and procedures and the dissemination of program results', 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used ... to disseminate statistical data').
Future GSBPM expectation: The transition to standardized, platform-driven dissemination alters the officer's traditional development focus. Rather than bespoke solutions or system modifications for program-specific releases, their efforts will be directed toward configuration and enhancement of corporate dissemination platforms, ensuring automatable rules for embargoes, access control, exception management, and machine-readable output formats. Tactical system enhancements move from bespoke development to adaptation within enterprise platforms.
Role evolution: The officer will increasingly collaborate with IT staff and platform owners to specify and implement dissemination logic (e.g., embargo workflows), oversee the integrity of automated release processes, and participate in platform rule-setting and audit processes. The focus shifts from creating custom solutions for dissemination to contributing to the governance and operation of standard dissemination pipelines and managing exceptions or rare interventions.
Capability implication: An understanding of enterprise dissemination platform logic, rules configuration for release workflows, digital governance and workflow auditing, and exception management are required. The officer's role will demand deeper involvement with platform-managed release processes, requiring knowledge of how platform standards support security, reliability, and machine-actionable output formats.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Promote dissemination products
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer leads teams developing processing and dissemination systems, implements enhancements/modifications, and negotiates with stakeholders on procedural improvements. Advises users, develops dissemination specifications and analytical reports, and guides others in adopting new dissemination approaches. Future GSBPM expectation: Promotion and dissemination activities will exploit automation, metadata-driven digital platforms and API-driven logic to reach both human and machine audiences. Continuous, personalized, and proactive promotion via digital channels replaces static manual dissemination. Role evolution: The Officer will need to take responsibility for integrating machine-actionable metadata standards into new dissemination systems, develop/promote digital outreach channels (APIs, real-time notifications), and contribute to ongoing analysis of user engagement to guide system evolution. Capability implication: Enhanced knowledge and operational practice in metadata management for discoverability, API-driven dissemination infrastructure, and real-time analytics for impact evaluation will become central responsibilities.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Provide user support (GSBPM Phase 7.5)
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer is responsible for providing subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiating procedural modifications, and leading project teams for new or modified processing systems. Key activities include 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users,' 'Leads project teams,' and 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' Future GSBPM expectation: The support function will be deeply integrated into digital discovery and dissemination platforms, with emphasis on machine-actionable metadata, scalable automated support, and anticipatory self-service enablement. Human-led support is reserved for complex requests and stewardship of digital trust. Role evolution: The Officer will be expected to lead projects focusing not just on data manipulation, but enhancing user support functions as coded/automated features within production systems (e.g., dynamic FAQs, API guides, programmatic access workflows) and actively monitor/curate digital knowledge repositories. They will increasingly collaborate with platform and metadata specialists to optimize user enablement for AI, power users, and external researchers. Capability implication: The Officer must develop expertise in digital platform curation, advanced metadata management, machine-consumable documentation standards, and feedback analytics. Understanding how to integrate support tools and automation directly into production and dissemination environments becomes paramount.

Data Production and Dissemination Develo.title: Gather evaluation inputs
Data Production and Dissemination Develo.justification:
Current responsibility: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer (EC-04) develops processing systems, designs data testing specifications, and leads teams in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems, including providing advice and resolving system design challenges ('Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information...'). Existing workflows for evaluating system quality depend heavily on collecting and reviewing inputs manually for system testing and quality improvement.
Future GSBPM expectation: The expectation is that processing systems and applications must now routinely emit evaluation inputs automatically, and that staff will focus less on manual collection, and more on monitoring and configuring system instrumentation and dashboards.
Role evolution: The officer’s focus will increasingly shift toward designing and embedding mechanisms for automatic evaluation input capture, configuring quality monitoring dashboards, and interpreting system- and process-level metrics to guide system enhancements. Exception handling will remain, especially where system-generated inputs are inadequate, but the bulk of evaluation input management becomes system-driven.
Capability implication: Knowledge of embedded system instrumentation, experience with configuration of automated data pipelines for quality monitoring, and the ability to interpret operational metrics produced by statistical production systems become critical to effective role fulfillment.

EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and implements long term strategies for divisional statistical programs and controls the development, implementation and operation of statistical systems and processes. It involves defining and coordinating statistical system development work, reviewing trends in data processing methods and presenting recommendations for new technology, and managing units and project teams in system design ('Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work' and 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes').

Future GSBPM expectation: The GSBPM future state redefines this subprocess as enterprise-wide orchestration of modular, reusable, AI-enabled, and metadata-driven workflows. System/workflow design focuses on rapid adaptation, cross-program interoperability, automation, self-service governance, and minimizing manual interventions. EC-06 roles will become responsible not only for divisional systems but for integrating into enterprise-standard architectures and frameworks.

Role evolution: The EC-06 Head will shift from managing bespoke system designs in isolation to overseeing enterprise-level modular architecture, specifying higher-level requirements, curating modular logic, enabling self-service solution development for non-IT staff, and coordinating the boundary between IT and business developer responsibilities. This involves ensuring version control, auditability, horizontal reuse, real-time monitoring, and compliance across program areas, rather than custom solutions per program.

Capability implication: Capabilities become much more centered on understanding modular and event-driven frameworks, metadata governance, cross-functional system interoperability, orchestration of automation/AI modules, the delineation of governance guardrails, and adaptive, enterprise IT-business collaboration. Deep knowledge of open standards, audit trails, and how to operationalize self-service environments is critical.

EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-06 Unit Head, Subject Matter.justification:
Current responsibility: The Unit Head, Subject Matter manages analytical programs and research, leads multidisciplinary teams, coordinates and reviews development and processing of statistical data, and represents the division on development projects and committees. The role involves developing new methods and enhancements in program content, coverage, and operational procedures ('Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data').

Future GSBPM expectation: As workflow design becomes modular and no longer restricted to one-off customization, the Unit Head will need to specify subject-matter requirements in forms that can be translated into modular workflows, reusable across programs. This means active engagement in curating functional logic that is both auditable and interoperable, and participating in enterprise orchestration of automated pipelines, relying on metadata-driven interfaces and rapid prototyping.

Role evolution: Decision-making and project leadership will require translating analytical and methodological needs into enterprise workflow design components. The Unit Head will increasingly supervise the curation of modular logic and oversee adaptive orchestration, ensuring subject-matter standards are embedded in machine-actionable metadata and interoperable frameworks. The role must evolve to interact effectively with IT, methodologist, and business developer teams in horizontally-integrated environments.

Capability implication: The Unit Head's capabilities will prioritize strategic articulation of requirements in modular/specification form, deep fluency in metadata frameworks, familiarity with orchestration of AI/automation modules, and ability to define and maintain high-level guardrails for self-service environments. Understanding of how modular logic and workflow governance is embedded into enterprise platforms becomes more important.

EC-07 Chief.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-07 Chief.justification:
Current responsibility: EC-07 Chiefs manage sections and multidisciplinary teams involved in program operations, system design, and production, plan and implement long-term strategies for statistical programs, and initiate changes and implement new systems and processes ('Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination. Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.').

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state shifts from isolated division-level initiatives to organization-wide orchestration. Chiefs will be expected to oversee the integration of program requirements into modular, AI-enabled enterprise workflows, manage adaptive and reusable pipelines, direct teams to articulate requirements as modular logic, and govern interfaces that support self-service and rapid deployment.

Role evolution: Chiefs will need to redefine how sections collaborate with IT, methodologists, and business developers to translate production requirements into modular, metadata-centric systems, and how horizontal reuse and auditability are integrated from design to operation. Their authority will increase in setting policies that govern event-driven workflows, modularity, and the boundaries of self-service development, as well as ensuring auditability and resilience.

Capability implication: Chiefs will require advanced understanding of modular architecture, orchestration of automated workflows, governance guardrails, event-driven frameworks, version control and auditability principles, and deep cross-program interoperability. Strategic leadership merges operational management with expertise in enterprise workflow governance and adaptive system design.

EC-05 Production and Dissemination Speci.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-05 Production and Dissemination Speci.justification:
Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist develops databases, coordinates and controls staff manipulating and retrieving statistical data, leads project teams in new/modification of statistical processing systems, and defines guidelines for system design, evaluation, and testing ('Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems').

Future GSBPM expectation: This role will need to support modular, automated production pipelines and governance-driven self-service environments. System specification, design, and coordination must be oriented toward rapid reuse, cross-program compatibility, auditability, and embedded metadata—as opposed to unique or bespoke processing systems for each study or program.

Role evolution: The Specialist will increasingly articulate requirements and guidelines as modular components, curate functional logic for reuse, configure systems to enable self-service and role-based interaction for subject-matter experts, and enforce standardization and version control. Coordination activities will intersect more with governance and modular orchestration, rather than only team-level operations.

Capability implication: Specialists will increasingly leverage conceptual knowledge of modular workflow design, metadata-driven orchestration, cross-program standards, real-time monitoring, and auditability. They will need to participate in collaborative enterprise production system design and governance boundary definition.

EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-04 Data Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Development Officer develops processing systems/applications, designs testing specifications, assesses needs for replacement or modification of systems, provides advice, and leads project teams for new processing systems ('Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems').

Future GSBPM expectation: Future production system design depends on modular, automated, and reusable architecture, with embedded machine-actionable metadata and self-service configurability as core organizing principles. EC-04 roles will need to specify system requirements in modular form, curate configurable logic for adaptive reuse, and support automated orchestration, rather than build bespoke or siloed applications. Documentation and specification will serve enterprise-wide auditability and governance.

Role evolution: Activities will focus on translating subject-matter and operational requirements into modular components, curating and testing reusable logic, embedding metadata, and ensuring compatibility with standardized interfaces. Collaboration will extend toward cross-program system orchestration and supporting the delineation of roles in self-service solution development.

Capability implication: Competence in modular system design, metadata frameworks, governance guardrails, automated workflow orchestration, and rapid prototyping for cross-program adaptation rises in importance. Clear understanding of how to design for auditability, version control, and scalable reuse is needed.

EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Economist Sociologist 5 leads teams in subject-matter studies, represents divisions on development projects, makes recommendations for new/revised production systems, and interprets study results to propose system/process enhancements ('Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task manager and Task Force Leader', 'Develops proposals for further study and recommends changes and improvements ... revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software').

Future GSBPM expectation: In the modular, enterprise-wide production system context, EC-05 roles must formulate requirements and proposals as reusable, standardized components, embedded with metadata for automation and auditability, and within governance guardrails that support self-service and cross-program deployment. Engagement in production design goes beyond division or program boundaries.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will increasingly work to specify production logic in standardized, modular forms, participate in collaborative orchestration of automated workflows, and ensure traceability and interoperability. Input on production system enhancements will be shaped by principles of modular design, metadata-driven automation, and cross-program compatibility, rather than ad hoc or program-specific proposals.

Capability implication: EC-05s will increase their fluency in specifying requirements as modular, metadata-driven logic, understanding standards for enterprise-wide automation, orchestration accountability, version control, and governance guardrails. Analytical capacity extends to coordinating and translating subject-matter needs for enterprise workflow integration.

EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4.title: Design production systems and workflows
EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-04 Economist/Sociologist 4 provides feedback and recommendations on survey methods and production activities, participates in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods, and suggests changes to collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods and procedures ('Suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities').

Future GSBPM expectation: Recommendations and operational feedback will be integrated into modular, enterprise-scale automated workflows and system design, requiring EC-04s to articulate and manage subject-matter requirements as modular specifications, participate in auditability and metadata-driven orchestration, and support rapid adaptation. Feedback must be formulated for horizontal reuse and standardization.

Role evolution: EC-04s will move from program-focused feedback toward specifying improvements in scalable, modular forms, supporting metadata-driven processes and automation. Their input will be expected to support rapid adaptation and self-service development, consistent with governance and enterprise orchestration standards.

Capability implication: EC-04s will need greater facility with modular specification, metadata logic, cross-program standards, and understanding how feedback supports adaptive, auditable workflows. They will also be required to collaborate more closely with IT and governance teams in operationalizing feedback.
